title: Reps. Houlahan, Strickland, Sen. Blumenthal Introduce Bicameral Legislation to Depoliticize Military Promotions
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C – Today, Representative Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), with Representative Marilyn Strickland (WA-10) and Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), led the bicameral introduction of the Military Officer Promotion Integrity Act to protect qualified military officers from being arbitrarily removed from promotion consideration for ideological or political reasons, by establishing clear standards, basic due process, and meaningful independent review.

“For the last year and a half, Secretary Hegseth has systematically damaged and undermined the previously unbiased military promotion system, and he has done so under the nose of the President, who reportedly has little to no awareness of Secretary Hegseth’s destructive purge of our military talent and leadership,” said Rep. Houlahan. “Today, we ensure that at least Congress will know when the Secretary tries to strike exceptionally qualified military officers from promotion slates – and we can take action to stop the removal. Once again, fairness, transparency, and objectivity will determine which officer has earned their next rank, and not their allegiance to the political whims of Secretary Hegseth.”

“Secretary Hegseth continues to deny promotions to our most qualified military officials,” said Rep. Strickland. “This bill allows Congress to intervene when a military official is denied or slated to be removed from a rightfully earned promotion.”

“Ironically, no one spends more time obsessing over gender and race than Secretary Hegseth, who is relentlessly blocking promotions and purging the military ranks of women, minorities, and anyone who fails to watch as much Fox News as he does,” said Rep. Blumenthal. “If Secretary Hegseth is really committed to meritocracy, he should fully support this legislation to prevent political meddling in military promotions. His disgraceful promotions decisions are only one piece of a much broader and deeply dangerous effort to politicize our military and undermine its proud tradition of nonpartisan service.”

The legislation is co-sponsored in the Senate by Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), and Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI). The bill is endorsed by VoteVets, Protect Democracy, the National Women’s Law Clinic (NWLC), and Retired Major General Steve Lepper, co-founder of the Former JAG Working Group.

“Military officers earn their promotions through years of service, sacrifice, and proven leadership. Pulling them from consideration because of politics not only derails careers, but it tells every officer and every American that fealty matters more than competence. Most important is our oath to support and defend the U.S. Constitution, against all enemies, foreign and domestic. The Military Officer Promotion Integrity Act makes sure that these decisions rest only on facts. VoteVets applauds Senator Blumenthal’s leadership and we call on Congress to pass this critical bill without delay,” said Retired Major General Paul Eaton, VoteVets Senior Advisor.

“A nonpartisan, merit-based military promotion system is crucial to military readiness. It ensures our senior ranks are filled by officers who have demonstrated the expertise and leadership that our readiness depends on. This legislation strengthens the promotion process, reinforces our operational edge, and sustains the confidence of the American people in their military,” said Zachary West with Protect Democracy.

“Our country and our nation’s service members deserve a promotion system that is based on merit and leadership skills—not one that can be abused to single out and block individuals because of their sex, race or support for diversity, equity and inclusion,” said Gaylynn Burrough, vice president for education and workplace justice at the National Women’s Law Center Action Fund. “Pete Hegseth’s unprecedented and outrageous interference in the promotions of women and people of color in the military is an affront to our nation’s ideals of nondiscrimination and equal opportunity and shows his willingness to put ideology over national security. We are grateful that Senator Blumenthal is taking action to address these senseless actions through Military Officer Promotion Integrity Act of 2026.”

“The United States military’s decisive advantage has always been the quality of its leaders. That’s why the officer promotion processes of each Service are so important. In recent months, individual officers selected for promotion based on their skills, experience, and leadership potential have been removed without explanation by individual senior leaders. Not only are such removals unfair to the removed officers, they undermine the confidence all officers must have in a system so crucial to their career progression and to America’s national security,” said Retired Major General Steve Lepper, co-founder of the Former JAG Working Group. “Senator Blumenthal’s legislation addresses these concerns by establishing minimum fairness standards whenever an officer is removed from a promotion list. If enacted, these standards will provide removed officers opportunities to challenge their removal and will subject the process to necessary congressional oversight. If enacted, this legislation will hopefully restore the fairness, transparency, and confidence needed to ensure America’s military preserves its competitive leadership advantage.”

The full text of the bill is available here.

title: Alford, Davids Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect America’s Medical Supply Chains, Support Kansas City Area Innovation
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives Mark Alford (R-MO-04) and Sharice Davids (D-KS-03) introduced the Critical Biomanufacturing Input Assessment Act. It’s a bipartisan bill that would help strengthen America’s biotechnology supply chains, support the growing medical industry in the Kansas City region, and address growing concerns about U.S. reliance on foreign suppliers — including China — for critical materials needed to produce medicines and other health products.

“As we work to bring more manufacturing back to American soil, we must ensure our biotechnology supply chains are secure, transparent and resilient,” said Congressman Alford. “This commonsense, bipartisan legislation will help identify vulnerabilities, reduce reliance on foreign adversaries like China, and protect the critical materials needed to produce lifesaving medicines and animal health products. I’m proud to partner with Representative Davids to strengthen innovation in the Kansas City region and safeguard our nation’s health and economic security.”

“Kansas City is creating the next generation of medicines, health products, and technologies that improve people’s lives — and we need to make sure American companies have the supplies they need to succeed,” said Congresswoman Davids. “This bipartisan bill will help us identify weaknesses in our supply chains, reduce our dependence on countries like China, strengthen American manufacturing, and create good-paying jobs while lowering healthcare costs. I appreciate Representative Alford’s partnership on this important, bipartisan effort.”

Many products Americans rely on — including medicines, vaccines, and animal health products — are made using biotechnology. But many companies do not have a clear picture of where the materials and equipment they depend on come from. Some critical supplies are made overseas, including in China, creating potential risks for our economy and national security. This bill will help identify these vulnerabilities before a disruption occurs.

The Critical Biomanufacturing Input Assessment Act would require the Department of Commerce to regularly review America’s reliance on foreign sources for important biotechnology supplies and equipment.

The information collected through this review would help:

Help businesses make better decisions about where to source materials;

Identify potential supply chain problems before they become emergencies;

Encourage more companies to manufacture critical supplies in the United States; and

Strengthen America’s ability to compete in the global biotechnology industry.

The Kansas City region is one of the country’s fastest-growing biotechnology hubs. It is home to the KC BioHub, a partnership focused on making Kansas City a national leader in biotechnology research, innovation, and manufacturing. The region is also home to the Kansas City Animal Health Corridor, one of the largest concentrations of animal health companies in the world.

These companies and research institutions rely on specialized supplies and equipment to develop products that improve human and animal health. Making sure those supply chains are strong and reliable is critical to their continued success.

title: Ansari, Titus Lead 65 House Democrats in Demanding Trump Admin Confront Turkey’s Anti-LGBTQI+ Crackdown
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Dina Titus (NV-01) led 65 House Democrats, including House Foreign Affairs Ranking Member Gregory Meeks and Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi, in urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to confront Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and the Turkish government over its escalating campaign of repression against LGBTQI+ people, human rights organizations, and advocates.

“The United States must be a leader in defending human rights and what is happening in Turkey demands an urgent diplomatic response. It’s absolutely appalling to see LGBTQI+ people and the organizations that stand up for their rights be targeted by the Erdogan regime,” said Rep. Ansari. “I stand proudly with the LGBTQI+ community here and abroad and will continue to fight for their right to live openly, freely, and without fear, anywhere and everywhere.”

The lawmakers’ letter follows a nationwide operation in which Turkish authorities have detained hundreds of people since September 12, raided the offices of longstanding HIV and LGBTQI+ civil society organizations, restricted access to websites and social media accounts, pursued the dissolution of human rights associations, and arrested organizational leaders and staff on spurious charges. At least 150 people protesting the crackdown have also been detained.

“Turkey’s crackdown on LGBTQI groups and individuals is disgraceful. No person should suffer from discrimination because of who they are or whom they love,” said Rep. Titus, who co-led the letter. “The Trump Administration must restore the United States’s role in promoting LGBTQI rights around the world and punishing regimes like Turkey that persecute people based on their sexual orientation or gender identity. My GLOBE Act does just that.”

The letter is endorsed by the Human Rights Campaign, the Council for Global Equality, and the Planned Parenthood Federation of America.

“Turkey’s attacks on its LGBTQI+ community are a disturbing reminder that the fight for equality and human rights does not stop at our borders. No one should be silenced or detained for simply being who they are or peacefully demanding dignity and freedom. We are grateful to Representatives Ansari and Titus for recognizing that the fight for LGBTQI+ equality is global and that, even amid the many challenges facing our community here at home, we cannot turn our backs on LGBTQI+ people facing persecution abroad,” said Jennifer Pike Bailey, Senior Director of Government Affairs, Human Rights Campaign.

“LGBTQ+ people deserve to be treated with dignity and respect, no matter where they live. Every person should have the freedom to live as their authentic self without fear, stigma, or discrimination. No one should be detained for simply advocating for the human rights and dignity of LGBTQ+ people. We are thankful for Rep. Ansari, Rep. Titus, and their colleagues for urging the State Department to stand up against Turkiye’s attack on health, safety, and basic human rights,” said Caitlin Horrigan, senior director of global advocacy, Planned Parenthood Federation of America.

“Türkiye’s escalating crackdown on LGBTQI+ people and civil society organizations is a direct assault on equality, democracy, and the rule of law,” said Mark Bromley, Co-Chair of the Council for Global Equality. “We are grateful to Representatives Ansari and Titus for their leadership in calling on the U.S. Department of State to stand up for the human rights of all people. Secretary Rubio should use every diplomatic tool available to press for the release of those detained and defend the fundamental freedoms of expression, association, and peaceful assembly. Human rights are not conditional on who we are, whom we love, or where we live, and the United States should make it clear that no one, no matter their sexual orientation or gender identity, will be abandoned when they are under attack.”

“The Erdogan government’s targeted campaign against the LGBTQI+ community and human rights defenders in Turkey is a violation of the core human rights to freedom of expression and association and a disregard for basic human dignity,” said Rep. Mark Takano, Chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus. “Congressional Equality Caucus members Ansari and Titus know the United States can and should do more to protect Turkish people’s freedoms from the human rights violations by the Erdogan government. I’m thankful for their work to put pressure on the State Department to respond to these human rights violations by working to free the wrongfully detained human rights defenders, pressing Turkey to cease efforts to criminalize LGBTQI+ organizations and advocacy, and ensuring human rights are integrated into all bilateral engagements.”

Ansari’s letter is co-signed by Representatives Gabe Amo (RI-01), Becca Balint (VT), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Everton Blair, Jr. (GA-13), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Angie Craig (MN-02), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Danny Davis (IL-07), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Lois Frankel (FL-22), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Daniel Goldman (NY-10), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), William Keating (MA-09), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Greg Landsman (OH-01), John Larson (CT-01), Teresa Leger Fernandez (NM-03), Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Sarah McBride (DE), James McGovern (MA-02), Gregory Meeks (NY-05), Grace Meng (NY-06), Jared Moskowitz (FL-23), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Jerrold Nadler (NY-12), Eleanor Norton (DC), Chris Pappas (NH-01), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Emily Randall (WA-06), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Janice Schakowsky (IL-09), Bradley Schneider (IL-10), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), Haley Stevens (MI-11), Mark Takano (CA-39), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Dina Titus (NV-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Norma Torres (CA-35), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

Read the letter HERE and below.

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We are writing to express grave concerns regarding President Erdogan and the Turkish government’s alarming campaign of repression against LGBTQI+ people, human rights organizations, and advocates in a recent nationwide operation.

In recent years, we have witnessed an increasingly systematic effort to restrict the human rights and civic participation of LGBTQI+ people in Turkey. The Turkish government has invoked so-called “family values” and “public morality” to justify restrictions on freedom of expression, association, and peaceful assembly, while courts and prosecutors have increasingly relied on vague provisions concerning obscenity and public morality to target LGBTQI+ people, human rights defenders, civil society organizations, and journalists. Authorities have repeatedly banned and violently dispersed Pride gatherings, individuals have faced prosecution for defending human rights, and government officials have escalated anti-LGBTQI+ rhetoric.

This latest crackdown represents a dangerous and significant escalation of that broader campaign. Since September 12, 2026, Turkish authorities have detained hundreds of people, raided the offices of longstanding and trusted HIV and LGBTQI+ civil society organizations, restricted access to websites and social media accounts, and pursued dissolution proceedings against human rights associations. Leadership and staff of LGBTQI+ human rights organizations have been arrested under spurious charges. In addition, Turkish authorities recently detained at least 150 people who were protesting this most recent anti-LGBTQI+ crackdown. Together, these developments mark a dangerous new phase in the Erdogan regime’s efforts to use criminal law and the state apparatus to suppress legitimate human rights advocacy on behalf of the LGBTQI+ community.

The Turkish government’s actions directly violate international human rights frameworks to which Turkey is a signatory, including the European Convention on Human Rights and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, to which the United States is party. They also are an affront to basic human dignity and the values expected of a fellow NATO member, an alliance founded on shared democratic principles, including individual liberty, human freedom, and the right to peaceful assembly.

These developments warrant an urgent diplomatic response from the United States to protect the rights of freedom of expression, association, and assembly for all Turkish citizens, regardless of their sexual orientation or gender identity. We therefore urge you to use all available channels to raise these concerns directly with the Turkish government; press for the immediate release of those arrested and detained for their legitimate human rights activities; and ensure that the U.S. Embassy in Ankara closely monitors related judicial proceedings. We further urge the Department to press Turkish authorities to cease efforts to criminalize LGBTQI+ organizations and advocacy and to affirm the right of all people to peacefully assemble.

We also request an update on the Department’s broader strategy for addressing human rights with the Turkish government. While the current crackdown on LGBTQI+ people and civil society demands urgent attention, it must be seen as part of a broader pattern of human rights violations and democratic backsliding in Turkey. We urge the Department to ensure that human rights are meaningfully integrated into all bilateral engagements and request a clear explanation of how the Department intends to do so.

Defending the rights of LGBTQI+ individuals around the globe is imperative for international peace and stability, the flourishing of liberal democracy, and the protection of the rule of law. As you yourself have noted, “We should never, ever tolerate human rights violations against any person for their political views, their religious beliefs, or their sexual orientation.” The United States must hold true to that principle in its engagement with the Turkish government.

Thank you for your attention to this critical matter. We look forward to your prompt response no later than October 30, 2026.

Sincerely,

Yassamin Ansari

Member of Congress

Follow @RepYassAnsari on all social media platforms and visit Ansari.House.gov to learn more.

title: Barr Applauds President Trump for Securing Major U.S. Coal Export Commitment from China
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, U.S. Congressman Andy Barr (R-KY-06) applauded President Trump’s announcement that China will import at least 10 million metric tons of American coal in 2027 and at least another 10 million metric tons in 2028.

The commitment follows a congressional effort led by Barr and six other Members of Congress urging the Trump Administration to prioritize American coal in trade negotiations with China and expand access to the Chinese market for U.S. producers. The White House announced the commitment following President Trump’s state visit with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

“President Trump delivered a major win for American coal workers, producers, and the communities that depend on them,” said Congressman Barr. “I was proud to lead six of my colleagues in strongly advocating for American coal to be a priority in our trade negotiations with China, and this commitment will expand opportunities for Kentucky miners, producers, railroads, manufacturers, and coal communities across the country. American coal is an abundant, reliable resource and an important economic asset, and I thank President Trump for continuing to advocate for American energy and American workers.”

Promises made, promises kept. Barr was joined in the congressional effort by Representatives Hal Rogers (R-KY-05), Morgan Griffith (R-VA-09), Carol Miller (R-WV-01), Randy Weber (R-TX-14), Barry Moore (R-AL-01), and Riley Moore (R-WV-02).

“Eastern Kentucky coal has powered our country for generations, and expanding overseas markets is good news for our miners, producers, and communities,” said U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers. “I was proud to join Congressman Barr in urging the Administration to put American coal on the table in trade discussions with China. This commitment creates new opportunities for American energy producers, and I appreciate President Trump’s continued efforts to open markets for our coal and support the men and women who produce it.”

“I applaud President Trump for prioritizing increased U.S. coal purchases by China in recent trade negotiations,” said U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith. “As an advocate for Southwest Virginia coal mining, I support President Trump’s negotiating tactics to have China purchase more American coal. This move will help generate economic growth, protect coal jobs and provide certainty for coal operators.”

“American coal is an abundant, reliable source of energy that supports thousands of jobs and helps keep our economy moving,” said U.S. Congressman Barry Moore. “President Trump has made strengthening American energy a priority, and American workers and businesses should have the opportunity to compete on a level playing field and sell our high-quality coal in markets around the world.”

“I was proud to join Congressman Barr in urging the Administration to make expanding access for U.S. coal a priority in our trade negotiations with China, and I’m grateful that President Trump succeeded in doing exactly that,” said U.S. Congressman Riley Moore. “President Trump’s commitment to opening foreign markets for American exports is another example of him always putting Americans first.”

National coal industry leaders also welcomed the agreement and its potential to strengthen U.S. coal exports.

“The agreement reached between President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping represents an important step toward reviving market access for American coal and strengthening U.S. energy exports. China’s commitment to import at least 20 million metric tons of U.S. coal over the next two years would provide a welcome return to our bilateral energy exchange as well as certainty for American producers and exporters,” said National Mining Association President and CEO Rich Nolan. “The National Mining Association appreciates President Trump’s leadership in prioritizing American coal during the most recent U.S.-China discussions, as well as the engagement of U.S. Representative Andy Barr and other congressional leaders who highlighted the effects of trade barriers on U.S. production and jobs. These efforts will help strengthen America’s important coal industry, support mining and transportation jobs, and reinforce the nation’s role as a reliable energy supplier to the world.”

“This announcement underscores the importance of maintaining strong international markets for American coal. We commend U.S. Congressman Andy Barr and his colleagues for advocating on behalf of an industry that supports hundreds of thousands of American jobs and contributes to energy security, economic growth, and industrial development,” said Emily Arthun, CEO of the American Coal Council. “Whether used to generate electricity, produce steel, or support manufacturing, American coal remains a strategic asset. Expanded export opportunities strengthen our coal communities and help ensure that American resources remain competitive on the global stage.”

“Congressman Andy Barr has been a tireless champion for coal. His leadership in expanding international markets for American coal creates new opportunities for producers, miners, and coal communities. We appreciate Congressman Barr’s continued commitment to our industry,” said Sam McKown, President of the Kentucky Coal Association.

title: Bynum’s Bipartisan Bill to Expand Capital Access for Rural Job Creators Heads to President’s Desk
text:
This week, the U.S. Senate passed H.R. 1190, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum’s (OR-05) bipartisan Expanding Access to Capital for Rural Job Creators Act. The legislation would help rural small businesses overcome barriers to accessing capital.

The bill updates the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 by requiring the SEC’s Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation to report annually on the unique challenges rural businesses face when seeking investment. These reports will give Congress better information as it considers ways to improve access to capital for rural job creators.

"Rural small businesses shouldn’t have to work twice as hard just because of their ZIP code,” said Congresswoman Janelle Bynum. “The Senate passing this bill gets us one step closer to changing that. Rural entrepreneurs have the ideas and the hustle. They deserve a fair shot to grow them into something bigger."

“Rural small businesses are essential to communities across Montana, but too many still face unnecessary barriers when trying to access capital,” said Congressman Troy Downing (MT-02), the bill’s co-lead. “I’m proud of our legislation, which will help make sure rural businesses are no longer overlooked when Congress considers how to expand access to capital and support job creation.”

Senator John Kennedy (R-LA.) led the U.S. Senate companion bill to passage.

“Rural small businesses are the backbone of many communities across America, but too many face challenges accessing capital. I’m glad the Senate passed our bill to make sure Congress understands those challenges and help rural job creators grow their businesses, create jobs and serve their communities,” said Senator Kennedy.

Read the bill HERE.

Background:

The SEC’s Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation is required to identify problems that small businesses face when securing access to capital and submit an annual report to Congress.

Currently, the Office’s list of applicable entities are minority-owned, women-owned, and disaster-stricken small businesses.

This legislation would require the SEC’s Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation to add rural small businesses to its list of applicable entities.

title: Carbajal, Padilla Introduce Legislation to Investigate Toxic Waste Dump Off California Coast
text:
U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24) and U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA) introduced the Ocean Protection and DDT Reduction Act, new legislation aimed at addressing the toxic industrial waste and pesticide pollution dumped off the Southern California coast.

For decades, industrial waste — including the pesticide DDT — was disposed of in ocean dump sites off California’s coast, particularly in the San Pedro Basin. The Ocean Protection and DDT Reduction Act establishes a structured federal study to assess the damage to the local marine ecosystem and develop comprehensive solutions to clean up the waste.

“The San Pedro Basin has long been the site of an underwater toxic waste dump. This toxic waste – which includes the pesticide DDT – has been very harmful to the health of local marine life and poses a risk to people who live and work near these waters,” said Rep. Carbajal. “As the representative of California’s Central Coast, I know firsthand how much our communities depend on a healthy ocean – from our fishermen and maritime workers to our tourism and coastal economies. We have a responsibility to protect these waters. I thank Senator Alex Padilla for joining me in introducing this bill as a first step in fixing this environmental tragedy.”

“Our communities deserve to know what's in the water off of the coast of San Pedro and what it means for our health, our fisheries, and our future. By putting NOAA's scientists and our leading research institutions to work mapping the contamination, tracking how it moves, and exploring cleanup through bioremediation, we can finally address this problem head-on,” said Sen. Padilla.

“For decades we used the ocean as a dumping ground for all manner of wastes including deeply-concerning industrial byproducts from DDT manufacturing. This proposed legislation takes an important step to address fundamental issues around the disposition, impacts and remediation options for those wastes. While California may be ground zero for this issue, the legislation provides a needed path to take lessons learned off California's coast and apply them to waste disposal sites that occur along all our Nation's coastlines,” said David Valentine, Norris Chair and Distinguished Professor of Earth and Marine Science, UCSB.

Specifically, the Ocean Protection and DDT Reduction Act would direct the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to monitor waste sites in the San Pedro Basin, study how toxic chemicals like DDT spread into the ocean food web, and build scientific tools to track ocean dumping.

NOAA, in coordination with the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and Department of Defense, may award grants to academic and research institutions to study:

Spatial mapping of contamination

Co-contaminants and chemical mixtures

Movement, fate, and breakdown processes

Bioaccumulation and biomagnification in ecosystems

The bill authorizes $6 million annually from Fiscal Year 2026 through Fiscal Year 2032 to carry out these critical activities.

title: Castor, Schakowsky Introduce Legislation to Modernize FTC and Strengthen Consumer Protections
text:
WASHINGTON – As new technologies, business practices, and online marketplaces create new ways for companies to take advantage of consumers, U.S. Representatives Kathy Castor (FL-14) and Jan Schakowsky (IL-09) are introducing legislation to ensure the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has the tools and independence it needs to protect consumers in the modern economy.

The 21st Century FTC Act, introduced by Rep. Castor, and the FTC Autonomy Act, introduced by Rep. Schakowsky, would strengthen the FTC’s ability to respond to unfair and deceptive practices and hold companies accountable when they harm consumers.

“The current economic pain being inflicted on hardworking Americans shouldn’t be exacerbated by fraudsters and corporate wrongdoers. It’s imperative that corporations be held accountable when they take advantage of consumers,” said Rep. Castor. “The FTC is key to accountability, and the 21st Century FTC and FTC Autonomy Acts will strengthen the ability to act and restore civil penalties for first time offenses. I’m committed to restoring the FTC’s autonomy and authority, and I urge Congress to pass this important legislation.”

“Companies are constantly finding new ways to take advantage of consumers, and the FTC needs the tools to keep up,” said Rep. Schakowsky. “I’m glad to be in this fight with Congresswoman Castor to make sure the FTC has the authority and independence it needs to protect consumers. We need an FTC that can keep pace with the modern economy, not one held back by outdated rules and unnecessary barriers.”

The FTC is the federal government’s primary consumer protection agency, but outdated procedures and restrictions on its enforcement authority can make it harder for the agency to respond to emerging threats.

The 21st Century FTC Act would give the FTC streamlined rulemaking authority under the Administrative Procedure Act and allow the agency to seek civil penalties for first-time violations of the FTC Act. These changes would help the FTC respond more effectively to emerging consumer harms and deter companies from engaging in unfair or deceptive practices.

The FTC Autonomy Act would allow the FTC’s own attorneys to bring cases seeking civil penalties without first having to enlist the assistance of the Department of Justice. Removing this procedural barrier would allow the agency to pursue enforcement actions more efficiently and hold companies accountable.

Together, these bills would give the FTC the modern tools it needs to protect consumers in a rapidly changing economy. As technology and business practices evolve, consumers should not be left vulnerable because federal consumer protection laws have failed to keep pace. The 21st Century FTC Act and FTC Autonomy Act would strengthen the FTC’s ability to set clear rules, respond to new consumer threats, and hold companies accountable when they cross the line.

title: García Leads Illinois Members in Letter Condemning Israeli Settler Violence in West Bank Village
text:
CHICAGO — Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04) led his colleagues Congresswoman Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Congressmen Mike Quigley (IL-05), and Jonathan Jackson (IL-01) in a letter to the U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, condemning the violence by Israeli settlers, police and military in the village of al-Mughayyir in the occupied West Bank. The legislators, who represent several constituents with relatives living in the village, are calling attention to the alarming situation where recently five Palestinian residents under the age of 20 were killed, others including a nine-year old boy have been shot, and food, basic needs and even education have been restricted.

“They have destroyed homes, businesses, and farms, uprooted thousands of olive trees, stolen livestock, blocked food and other necessary supplies from entering the village, and devastated the entire local economy,” state the Members of Congress in the letter. “Those residents who are not murdered by Israeli forces are condemned to a horrific existence marked by poverty, deprivation, and terror.”

“This is not an isolated situation; it reflects an intentional policy of violence and terrorism inflicted by Israeli forces across the occupied West Bank to further the ethnic cleansing and genocide of the Palestinian people,” continues the letter. “Shamefully, the U.S. government has consistently backed this policy by continuing to provide military aid to Israel and failing to act to stop these rampant attacks. This is morally unconscionable and directly affects the U.S. citizens who live in al-Mughayyir or who (like several of our constituents) have relatives that live there.”

The Members urged Ambassador Huckabee to visit al-Mughayyir, hold a town hall with its residents, and specify concrete actions the U.S. government will take to intervene with the Israeli government. “At minimum, the Administration should follow the lead of our allies and impose sanctions and a trade ban on settlements, but much more is required to end our government’s longstanding support of the mass atrocities committed against the Palestinian people,” demand the Members of Congress in the letter.

A full copy of the letter can be found here.

title: Rep. Cisneros and Commissioner Hernández Introduce Bill to Strengthen Small Business Participation in Federal Contracts
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) and Puerto Rico Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández (D-PR) introduced the PROMISE for Small Businesses Act, legislation to enhance oversight of federal contracting and protect the commitments made to small businesses and their participation in subcontracting opportunities.

Currently, large companies and corporations that receive certain federal contracts are required to provide plans outlining how they will provide subcontracting opportunities to small businesses. This legislation directs the Small Business Administrator to conduct compliance reviews to ensure large contractors follow through on their promise to deliver opportunities to small businesses in their subcontracting plans.

“Small businesses are critical to our economy and they deserve a fair shot in the federal marketplace.” said Rep. Gil Cisneros. “I’m proud to join Rep. Pablo José Hernández to introduce the PROMISE for Small Businesses Act to make sure they are not being left out. If enacted, this legislation would strengthen oversight of federal contracts to help ensure that large prime contractors keep their promise to small businesses as outlined in subcontracting plans. It would direct reviews of subcontracting plans and require reporting to Congress on compliance, noncompliance trends, and any enforcement actions taken. We cannot allow our small businesses to be pushed out of federal contracting.”

“When companies receive federal contracts and commit to working with small businesses, we should make sure they follow through,” said Hernández. “These opportunities can help small businesses grow, create jobs, and build experience in the federal marketplace. Our bill strengthens accountability and helps ensure those opportunities reach them.”

Small businesses greatly benefit from competing in the federal marketplace, and this bill will ensure they’re able to continue to do so fairly.

The PROMISE for Small Businesses Act would require the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) to review at least 10 percent of contracts subject to these subcontracting plans at each federal agency every year to determine whether contractors are meeting their commitments.

The legislation would also require the SBA to report:

whether contractors complied with their small business subcontracting plans;

how many compliance reviews the agency conducted;

title: Reps. Cisneros, Chu Introduce Bill to Fund Clean Drinking Water
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) and Congresswoman Judy Chu (CA-28) introduced the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund Reauthorization Act, which would remove the funding cap for the ongoing groundwater treatment by the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority, reauthorize funding at $250 million, and support the completion of the ongoing water restoration project. The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water for over 1.5 million residents in the San Gabriel Valley and Los Angeles County, including the cities of Azusa, Baldwin Park, City of Industry, El Monte, Irwindale, La Puente, South El Monte, and West Covina. The San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority signed on as a supporting organization.

“The San Gabriel Valley relies on the clean drinking water provided by the San Gabriel Basin,” said Rep. Gil Cisneros. “Since 2000, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has supported the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean and restore contaminated groundwater in our region. This legislation would remove funding hurdles and provide the support needed to bring this decades-long project across the finish line. Earlier this year, I worked with Congresswoman Chu to secure critical federal Community Project Funding for the restoration fund, and we’re committed to passing this legislation to further accelerate groundwater cleanup. Clean drinking water is a fundamental human right, and every family in the San Gabriel Valley deserves direct, affordable, protected access to it.”

“The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water to more than 1.5 million people across our region, but it still carries contamination left behind by industries of the past,” said Rep. Judy Chu. “For decades, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has powered the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean up our groundwater, and this bill would provide the long-term federal support needed to finish the job. I’m proud to join Congressmember Cisneros in leading this effort, building on our work securing federal Community Project Funding for this project. Families across the San Gabriel Valley deserve a safe, reliable, and sustainable source of drinking water for generations to come.”

Full text of the bill can be found here.

Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. title: Texas Delegation Urges Selection of Texas to Host U.S. Space Academy
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Members of the Texas congressional delegation today sent a letter to the Presidential Commission on the United States Space Academy expressing strong support for establishing the Academy and urging the Commission to select Texas as its home.

The letter was signed by Senators Ted Cruz and John Cornyn, House Science, Space, and Technology Committee Chairman Brian Babin, and Congressman Michael Cloud. It emphasizes that Texas is uniquely positioned to host the institution charged with developing the next generation of Americans who will explore, operate, build, and defend the Nation’s interests in space.

“Texas has been at the center of America’s space story for more than six decades, and we are leading the way into its next chapter. From NASA’s Johnson Space Center in my district, home to Mission Control and our nation’s astronaut corps, to the cutting-edge commercial space companies developing the technologies of tomorrow, Texas brings together the experience, infrastructure, talent, and innovation that continue to move America forward. As Chairman of the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, I am committed to ensuring the United States wins this new space race and remains the undisputed global leader in exploration and discovery. The United States Space Academy will help prepare the next generation to advance that mission, enhance our space defense capabilities, and protect the homeland. Texas has an unmatched foundation on which to build this landmark institution,” said Chairman Brian Babin.

“For over 60 years, when American astronauts need to reach home base, they make the same call: “Houston”. Today, Texas is home to Mission Control, the astronaut corps, more than 148,000 aerospace professionals, and the companies and universities leading the next era of space innovation — as well as a robust military presence. The next generation of Guardians should train alongside people who not only built our nation’s space legacy but are currently building its future,” said Congressman Michael Cloud.

The letter notes that Texas offers a rare convergence of civil, commercial, and national security space capabilities. Key advantages highlighted include:

• NASA’s Johnson Space Center — home to America’s astronaut corps, Mission Control, and human spaceflight training;

• One of the nation’s largest aerospace workforces, with more than 148,000 professionals across more than 1,400 companies;

• Major industry presence including SpaceX, Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Blue Origin, Axiom Space, Firefly, and Intuitive Machines;

• Texas A&M University’s Space Institute and more than $5 billion in annual aerospace-related research and development across Texas universities; and

• A robust national security footprint, including Space Force training at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland and the Space Force Captain’s Leadership Course at Texas A&M.

The letter underscores that locating the Space Academy in Texas would allow the Nation to leverage more than sixty years of investment in human spaceflight rather than recreating those capabilities elsewhere.

The full letter is available upon request.

title: Congressional PATH Caucus Releases Report Outlining Recommendations for Safe Integration of Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy
text:
Report Responds to Congressional Request for Information on Regulatory, Ethical, and Cultural Considerations for Integrating Prescription Psychedelic Medicine into the United States

Washington, DC — The Congressional Psychedelics Advancing Therapies (PATH) Caucus released a report capturing responses to a 2024 Request for Information into how psychedelic-assisted therapy (PAT) could be safely and ethically integrated into the United States health care system.

The report found broad consensus among clinicians, researchers, veteran advocates, Tribal leaders, payors, regulators, and patients that PAT could offer safe, equitable, and evidence-based treatment for a wide array of treatment-resistant conditions – including generalized anxiety disorder, depression, PTSD, and substance use disorder. It also offered several federal policy recommendations for the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Congress to consider as they aim to improve health outcomes for patients across the country.

“Every day, more than 130 Americans die by suicide, including over 20 veterans,” said Congressman Lou Correa (D-CA-46). “Psychedelic-assisted therapy has shown promising results for treatment, but we need more information. This report is a serious step toward bringing it into our health care system safely and ethically, so that all Americans, especially those who served our country, can get care that works for them.”

“This report is exactly the kind of resource Congress needs to legislate responsibly,” ?said?Congressman Jack Bergman (R-MI-01).?“Our Veterans have waited long enough for successful treatments and breakthrough therapies to help mitigate PTSD and other service-related conditions. It’s time to advance real, actionable policies that meet the unmet mental and physical health needs of Americans in every community.”?

Key Findings

Respondents agree that the U.S. faces a severe mental and behavioral health crisis – including treatment-resistant depression, PTSD, suicidality, substance use disorder, and high unmet needs among veterans, terminally ill patients, minorities, low-income families, seniors, and rural communities – requiring novel and efficacious treatments.

Respondents highlight clinical trial evidence suggesting that PAT can produce meaningful and sometimes transformative improvements in PTSD, depression, end-of-life distress, addiction, and overall functioning and quality of life, though it is not considered a single solution and is seen as appropriate only in structured, supervised medical settings.

Respondents encourage national guidance and credential verification systems to be developed before the first FDA approvals of prescription psychedelic medicines.

Respondents highlight the need for evidence-based, standardized adverse event monitoring and robust ethical guidelines to protect patients and ensure trust.

Respondents recommend federal guidance that supports multidisciplinary, culturally competent care teams.

Policy Recommendations

The report suggests that federal agencies – including the FDA, U.S. National Institutes of Health, Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, Department of Homeland Security, Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Defense, Drug Enforcement Administration, and Office of National Drug Control Policy –

should work with state regulators and Tribal Nations/Territories to develop national guidelines for safe and ethical delivery of prescription psychedelic medicines

The report recommends that federal agencies establish flexible, tiered credentialing pathways to balance safety with accessibility, and to standardize consent and screening protocols nationally.

The report proposes a hybrid policy framework to guide Congress, federal agencies, Tribal Nations/Territories, states, and communities in a balanced, pragmatic rollout of PAT, supported by coordinated leadership, flexible regulation, investment in workforce and infrastructure, and robust long-term data systems.

See here for the full report.

About the Congressional PATH Caucus

The bipartisan Congressional Psychedelics Advancing Therapies (PATH) Caucus, co-chaired by Representatives Jack Bergman (R-MI) and Lou Correa (D-CA), aims to address the nation’s mental health crisis by promoting rigorous, FDA-aligned clinical research into the therapeutic potential of psychedelic-assisted treatments for mental health disorders and integrating these promising treatments into the U.S. health care system for millions of patients with unmet needs.

title: CORREA, BERGMAN INTRODUCE BILL TO FIND ALTERNATIVES FOR DANGEROUS OPIOIDS HARMING VETERAN COMMUNITIES
text:
Washington, DC — Today, Congressmen Lou Correa (D-CA) and Jack Bergman (R-MI) reintroduced the VA Medicinal Cannabis Research Act. The bipartisan legislation directs the Department of Veterans Affairs to conduct clinical research on the safety and efficacy of medical cannabis in treating veterans’ post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and chronic pain.

"With the opioid crisis raging across America, it is imperative to the health and safety of our veterans that we find alternative treatments for chronic pain and service-related injuries," said Correa. "Throughout my district, I consistently meet veterans who depend on cannabis to manage their pain. Numerous veterans attest to the treatment benefits of medical cannabis. It's time the VA did a formal study and began recognizing that cannabis can play a safe role in our veterans' healthcare."

The bill would:

Authorize VA to implement a comprehensive research plan, including clinical trials assessing the effectiveness of medicinal cannabis in treating chronic pain and PTSD.

Expand research into related factors in veterans' health, including improvements to mood and social functioning, impacts on other substance use, and overall quality of life.

Require clinical trials to examine different forms, potencies, and methods of cannabis administration, with veterans' health and safety prioritized throughout.

“Veterans struggling with PTSD and chronic pain deserve access to treatments backed by sound science and rigorous research. The VA Medicinal Cannabis Research Act will help us better understand whether medicinal cannabis can provide safe and effective relief while ensuring Veterans’ health and safety remain the top priority. We owe it to our Veterans to explore every responsible avenue that could improve their quality of life,” said Bergman.

Chronic pain affects one in five Americans and impacts veterans at a higher rate than the general population. Twenty-three percent of veterans receiving VA care have experienced PTSD at some point in their lives, and the two conditions are often linked — veterans with chronic pain have elevated rates of PTSD. This bill would mandate research that could lead to safer, more effective treatment options for veterans managing these conditions.

"Since 2017, IAVA has made empowering veterans who are calling for the medicinal use of cannabis one of our top priorities. Our members have said consistently and passionately that cannabis offers real help with the most pressing injuries we face when we come home, from chronic pain to PTSD to traumatic brain injury. Our national policies are lagging, research is lacking, and the stigma persists. The VA Medicinal Cannabis Research Act is how we start to change that. Every solution begins with research, and veterans have waited long enough for it," said Kyleanne Hunter, CEO of Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA).

“The VFW supports the VA Medicinal Cannabis Research Act of 2023,” said Pat Murray, Director, National Legislative Service, Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW). “VFW members tell us that medicinal cannabis has helped them cope with chronic pain and other service-connected health conditions. They cannot receive these services at VA because of VA’s bureaucratic hurdles. VA uses evidence-based clinical guidelines to manage other pharmacological treatments of post-traumatic stress disorder, chronic pain, and substance use disorder because medical trials have found them effective. VA must expand research on the efficacy of non-traditional medical therapies, such as medicinal cannabis and other holistic approaches.”

title: Costa Leads Bipartisan Effort to Protect $232 Million in Rural Homeownership Funding
text:
FRESNO, Calif. – This week, Congressman Jim Costa (CA-21) led a bipartisan group of 14 members of Congress in urging the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to take immediate action to protect approximately $232 million in funding for the Section 502 Single Family Housing Direct Loan Program that is at risk of expiring at the end of Fiscal Year 2026.

In a letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins, the lawmakers called on the department to preserve funding Congress provided to help low- and very-low-income families purchase homes in rural communities. Recent reports indicate that USDA has obligated only a portion of the approximately $1 billion Congress provided for the program, leaving hundreds of millions of dollars at risk of going unused.

“These resources were provided by Congress to help families in rural America purchase homes and strengthen the communities in which they live and work,” wrote the lawmakers. “Regardless of party, we should share the goal of ensuring that congressionally appropriated funds are administered efficiently and reach the rural families they were intended to serve."

“The USDA's 502 direct mortgage program has been a flagship tool for increasing homeownership opportunities in rural places,” said David Lipsetz, President & CEO of the Housing Assistance Council. “To have these critical funds expire at a time when the program has been challenged with new and burdensome rules would be a real tragedy for rural families looking to buy a home. We applaud Congressman Costa and his colleagues for their leadership on this issue.”

The lawmakers also raised concerns about recent administrative changes that could limit access to the program and delay assistance to eligible families. They urged USDA to preserve the remaining funding, provide Congress with an accounting of unobligated balances, and take steps to improve loan processing and prevent future funding from expiring.

title: Rep. Crane Introduces Bill Honoring Slain Marine Veteran and Warning Travelers of Cartel Violence
text:
Today, Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) introduced the Nicholas Douglas Quets Border Travel Safety Act to inform travelers of dangerous areas or routes near the southern border of the United States. If enacted, the legislation would require the installation of signage warning travelers of areas identified in State Department Travel Advisories as dangerous due to criminal activity, violence, kidnapping, and other threats.

In the House, Rep. Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ) is co-leading the bill and Rep. Greg Stanton (D-AZ) has signed on as an original cosponsor. Sen. Mark Kelly (D-AZ) previously introduced a companion bill in the Senate.

On October 18, 2024, Nicholas Quets, an Arizona Marine Corps veteran, was traveling with friends in the Mexican state of Sonora. After encountering an unauthorized cartel-controlled highway checkpoint, he was pursued, attacked, and fatally shot by armed criminals associated with the Sinaloa Cartel. This occurred on the Altar-Caborca highway (Federal Highway 2), a route frequently listed under a “Reconsider Travel” advisory.

Although State Department Travel Advisories identify certain dangerous regions near the U.S.-Mexico border, travelers entering or departing the United States through land ports of entry may not know these designations exist. Rep. Crane believes clear, visible signage would close that gap and help keep travelers safe.

The bill would direct the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), through U.S. Customs and Border Protection and in coordination with the State Department, to post warnings at land ports of entry along the U.S.-Mexico border and on the routes approaching them. The signage would flag nearby dangerous areas identified in State Department Travel Advisories and provide a reference to additional safety information, such as a QR code linking to the latest advisories. It would also be displayed in both English and Spanish and in a format that can be quickly updated as conditions change. Furthermore, each sign would note that it was installed pursuant to the Nicholas Douglas Quets Border Travel Safety Act, ensuring Nicholas’ name appears alongside the warnings.

The legislation would direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Secretary of State, to annually review the signage for accuracy, visibility, and necessary updates. The Secretary of State would be required to notify DHS whenever critical changes require the signage to be updated. Within one year of enactment, DHS would report to Congress on implementation, including where the signage has been installed. The bill would also require the Government Accountability Office to assess the effectiveness of the warnings and identify potential improvements to how the information reaches travelers. The program would be carried out using existing funds, with no new appropriations authorized.

Rep. Crane is also co-leading two measures introduced by Rep. Ciscomani. The first, the Nicholas Douglas Quets United States-Mexico Rapid Response for Victims of Crime Act, would authorize the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Attorney General, to negotiate a bilateral protocol with Mexico for faster coordination on serious crimes against U.S. citizens in Mexico. The second is a resolution honoring Nicholas Quets’ life and service and condemning the cartel violence behind his murder.

“Nicholas Quets, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and hardworking member of his community, represented the very best of America. While driving to Puerto Peñasco, Nicholas was chased down and murdered by Sinaloa Cartel gunmen after fleeing an illegal checkpoint. The cowardly killing of this tremendous young man is yet another tragic instance of Americans being targeted by sinister cartels that operate with near-total impunity across Mexico. After listening to his father, retired U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel Doug Quets, I was honored to work with him and Representative Juan Ciscomani on two bills and a resolution in Nicholas’ name. Our measures will warn travelers of dangerous areas before they cross the border, push for faster coordination with Mexican authorities when U.S. citizens are victims of serious crimes, formally honor his service, and condemn the criminals responsible for his death. No family should ever endure what the Quets family has, and I’m hopeful this approach will save innocent lives, hold these murderous organizations accountable, and ensure this fallen patriot is never forgotten,” said Rep. Crane.

“Nicholas was a true American hero. His tragic passing demands action and lasting change. It is an honor to work closely with Nicholas’ family, Senator Kelly, and Rep. Crane on this much-needed package to honor Nicholas’ life and legacy. These legislative measures represent a long-overdue response, and I will fight relentlessly to ensure this bipartisan package receives the national attention and momentum required to protect Americans and deliver justice in Nicholas’ name,” said Rep. Ciscomani.

title: Rep. Crane’s Legislation for Gila County Veterans Retreat Heads to President’s Desk
text:
Last night, the Senate passed H.R. 837 by unanimous consent. The legislation, introduced by Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ), will allow Gila County to take ownership of the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site for the continued operation of a veterans center on the property in Young, Arizona, once signed into law by the President.

H.R. 837 is a reintroduction of the first bill Rep. Crane introduced in Congress, and it is now the first of his bills poised to become law. The House of Representatives passed the measure unanimously in two consecutive Congresses, most recently on February 5, 2025. Afterward, it advanced through the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources under the leadership of Chairman Mike Lee (R-UT) before clearing the full Senate.

The legislation directs the Secretary of Agriculture, acting through the Forest Service, to convey approximately 232.9 acres of the administrative site in the Tonto National Forest to Gila County. The county will cover all costs tied to the transfer, and the Congressional Budget Office estimates the bill will have no effect on the federal budget.

In 2016, the Forest Service moved its Pleasant Valley administrative operations to a new site near Payson, leaving most of the property unused. Since 2021, Gila County has operated the land under a 20-year special use permit and has been developing it into the Pleasant Valley Veterans Retreat. However, the county still needs federal approval for projects under the permit. Rep. Crane’s legislation will replace this arrangement with local ownership, giving the county the certainty it needs to invest in the retreat long-term and avoid overly burdensome regulations.

The center is the first of its kind in the region and primarily serves rural veterans and their families, including the nearly 5,500 veterans who call Gila County home. Transferring ownership to Gila County will preserve the property’s rich history while providing family housing, meeting and activity spaces, resource rooms, Veteran Ceremonial Grounds, and outdoor recreation.

Gila County Supervisor Woody Cline testified before the House Committee on Natural Resources on the significant impacts and outstanding resources the center would provide for veterans and their families.

“This site will only be one of two sites in Arizona. There’s one in the southern part of Arizona and one in the northern part […] It’s huge for our local community as well. We have a local veteran community of about 100 people right there in that small town. And then right there between us and Payson, there’s roughly another 5,000-7,000 more right there. Having this accessible, not only to the local members, the state members, the national members, but also, we’re adjacent to the White Mountain Apache Tribe that is not very far away that has a number of veterans in that reservation as well that have been big supporters of this project. It means everything to these folks,” said Supervisor Woody Cline during hearing questioning.

Speaking to Supervisor Cline about the purpose of the veterans center, Rep. Crane stated, “One of the things I love so much about this project, is that you’re not coming here, Mr. Cline, and asking the federal government for any money. You’re actually trying to take something that’s a beautiful piece of land that’s not being used anymore and revitalize it into something amazing for some of our nation’s finest individuals.”

House Committee on Natural Resources Chairman Bruce Westerman stated, “America’s veterans and their families have sacrificed so much to defend our freedom, and Congress must do everything in its power to provide our servicemembers with proper care and opportunities. The commonsense, bipartisan land transfer provided by H.R.837 will do just that by opening up new experiences to veterans in the area for recreation and recovery. A veteran himself, Representative Crane has led on these issues this Congress, and I look forward to continuing to work with him to get this bill […] signed into law.”

title: Rep. Crank Introduces Bill to Support Early Childhood Education Opportunities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Representative Jeff Crank (CO-05) introduced the Supporting Early Childhood Education Opportunities through Upfront Tax Deductions (SPROUT) Act, to help incentivize the creation of more childcare and early childhood education centers.

Families who cannot provide care at home face a lack of available childcare, an issue that Colorado and the entire country faces. While Colorado ranks among the best states in the country for its childcare workforce, it falls short when it comes to the number of infant care and toddler care facilities available to families. For El Paso County, estimates are in the tens of thousands of children lacking access to quality childcare and early education centers.

The SPROUT Act would help reduce this deficit and increase daycare capacity by allowing the owners of new facilities to deduct their costs in the same tax year that they are incurred, as opposed to the current framework requiring them to spread the deductions over decades. This accelerated tax deduction will attract more investment in new facilities.

"Parents want the best education and care for their kids, they just need more options to fill the need that El Paso County faces," said Rep. Crank. "The SPROUT Act makes a simplified tax process and incentivizes the creation of more childcare and early childhood education centers, helping to alleviate a burden impacting families across our community.”

Specifically, the SPROUT Act would:

Allow owners of new childcare or early childhood education centers to immediately expense (deduct) all costs associated with the creation of the center in the same tax year that they incur the cost;

Extend tax benefits to the creation of any center that is licensed by a State and provides care for children under the age of 5;

Clarify that the owner of the center must enter into a written binding contract with an entity licensed by a State to provide care before construction or improvements begin to be eligible for the tax benefit.

Quote of support for the SPROUT Act:

“Allowing businesses to fully and immediately deduct their expenses is a proven policy for boosting growth and investment,” said the Tax Foundation. “The SPROUT Act enables businesses to have a full and immediate deduction for childcare facilities and would boost investment in the sector.”

text:

“Pittsburgh International Airport is one of the gateways to Western Pennsylvania, and the infrastructure behind it has to be safe, reliable, and ready for the people and workers who depend on it every single day,” said Congresswoman Lee. “This more than $11 million federal investment is exactly what public dollars should be doing: coming back home, strengthening the things our communities rely on, supporting good jobs, and making sure a major piece of our regional economy is built to last. I’m glad to see this funding headed home to Pittsburgh International Airport, and I’ll keep fighting to bring federal investment back to Western Pennsylvania.”

Pittsburgh International Airport is an important economic driver for our region and this grant helps to fund airfield improvements at PIT including runway paving and upgrading lighting infrastructure. Thank you to Congressman Deluzio and our entire federal delegation for their continued support,” said Pittsburgh International Airport CEO Christina Cassotis.

title: DESJARLAIS MEETS WITH COLLINS, DISCUSSES PLANS TO KEEP MCMINNVILLE VA OPEN FOR THE FORESEEABLE FUTURE
text:
Congressman Scott DesJarlais met with Secretary Doug Collins today and received news that the McMinnville VA Clinic will remain open for the foreseeable future.

In March, it was announced that the McMinnville VA Clinic, operated by a private contractor, would be closing its doors on May 31st. Through persistent efforts and engagements with Secretary Collins, local leaders, VA staff, and community partners, Congressman DesJarlais expressed his concern about the lack of transparency and the impact this closure would have on those receiving VA care in the district. The VA cited that the clinic was underperforming.

As a result of these discussions, in May, Secretary Collins agreed to keep the clinic open through December 31, 2026. Today, in partnership with the VA, DesJarlais announced the McMinnville VA clinic will remain open under VA management and staff.

Secretary Collins thanked Rep. DesJarlais for his persistence in helping the VA find a solution to continue to provide high-quality service to veterans in Warren and surrounding counties. Collins and DesJarlais discussed plans to staff the McMinnville facility with full-time VA employees moving forward and improve the quality of care.

“I am proud of the joint effort put forth by my office and Secretary Collins’ office to keep the McMinnville VA Clinic open for the foreseeable future. This is great news for the veterans of Tennessee’s Fourth Congressional District. I want to thank my constituents for their patience and perseverance over the last few months. Together, we have respectfully and relentlessly drawn attention to the importance of this rural healthcare facility. Thank you to Secretary Collins and his team for working with us to come up with a solution to not only keep the clinic open but improve the level of care for all its patients,” said Rep. DesJarlais.

Congressman DesJarlais says that he and his staff will continue regularly checking in with Secretary Collins, VA staff, and his constituents to ensure the clinic is being run successfully.

title: DOWNING’S FLOODPLAIN ENHANCEMENT AND RECOVERY ACT PASSES SENATE
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Troy Downing’s (MT-02) bipartisan Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act took a major step toward becoming law this week after the U.S. Senate passed companion legislation led by Senators Steve Daines (R-MT) and Patty Murray (D-WA).

The legislation cuts red tape for ecosystem restoration projects in regulated floodways by creating a streamlined approval pathway for low-risk projects while maintaining flood safety standards. Under current Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) policy, any proposed development in a regulated floodway must prove that it will not increase the area’s base flood elevation (BFE). This requirement, known as the “No-Rise Rule,” has created unintended consequences for conservation work in Montana and across the country.

Many conservation districts have been forced to scale back, delay, or abandon stream restoration projects because of the cost of the required engineering analysis.

The Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act amends the Homeowner Flood Insurance Affordability Act of 2014 to allow communities to permit ecosystem restoration projects in regulated floodways if a professional engineer certifies that the project will not raise the base flood elevation by more than one foot and that no insurable structure or critical infrastructure is located in an area that would be adversely affected by the increase. This would allow qualifying conservation projects to avoid the traditional, drawn-out FEMA approval process.

The bill is supported by the National Association of Conservation Districts, among other organizations.

“I applaud Senators Daines and Murray for getting this commonsense, bipartisan bill through the Senate. FEMA’s No-Rise Rule is blocking critical conservation work in Montana and across the country,” said Congressman Downing. “My bipartisan bill cuts needless bureaucracy and puts more power in the hands of local communities to restore and protect our lands. I’m grateful for the strong bipartisan support behind this effort, and I urge my House colleagues to take it up quickly and send it to the President’s desk.”

“This is huge news for Montana. Critical ecosystem restoration projects across our state have been abandoned due to FEMA’s onerous and costly ‘No Rise’ rule. This commonsense, bipartisan bill will reduce unnecessary burdens on important conservation and restoration work, while continuing to keep our communities safe from flooding, and I’m glad to see it pass the Senate. Next step: the U.S. House!” said Senator Daines.

title: Leger Fernández, Scott, Grijalva, Dean Introduce Bill to Lower Cost of Community College
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Representatives Teresa Leger Fernández (D-NM-03), Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), Representative Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ-07), Madeleine Dean (D-PA-04), and Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) introduced the America’s College Promise Act of 2026. The bill would make community college and two-year Tribal Colleges and Universities more accessible by waiving tuition fees for eligible students.

“In New Mexico, we know free community college can unlock the doors to a brighter future. The America’s College Promise Act builds on New Mexico’s example by making sure students across the country can attend community college without the burden of tuition and fees,” said Representative Leger Fernández. “Our bill will provide funds for services students need to earn their degrees and reduce the financial burden for low-income students to attend TCUs, HBCUs, and MSIs. From recent high school graduates to experienced workers who want to go back to school — every student deserves the opportunity to keep learning without the fear of drowning in debt.”

“Community colleges play a unique and vital role in providing students access to a quality postsecondary degree. Regrettably, the chronic underfunding of community colleges is jeopardizing their ability to support their students and communities,” said House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Scott (D-VA-03). “The America’s College Promise Act is a major investment in expanding opportunities for students and rebuilding a stronger economy.”

“Students in Southern Arizona and throughout the country should not have to take on tens of thousands of dollars of debt to get a college education,” said Representative Grijalva. “The America’s College Promise Act will provide two years of free in-state tuition and fees for students enrolled in community and technical college programs. Whether they’re just starting out or returning to the classroom later in life, every student deserves the opportunity to learn new skills and pursue higher education. By expanding access to education and workforce training, we’re strengthening the workforce that businesses and local economies depend on.”

“As a professor, it was a privilege to witness students claim their education and seize their futures — yet the real fear and burden of immense student loan debt often deters young adults and returning students from expanding their learning,” said Representative Dean. “The America’s College Promise Act provides tuition-free community college courses and expands funding for HBCUs and trade schools, making the path to higher education and career readiness available to more Americans and future generations.”

“Every Wisconsinite deserves the opportunity to get the education and skills they need to land a good-paying job and build a better life, no matter where they come from or how much money their family makes,” said Senator Baldwin. “But for too many working families, the rising cost of higher education leaves students saddled with debt for years to come, or it is simply out of reach. That’s why I am proud to work with my colleagues to remove barriers and lower the cost of community college, so more Wisconsinites have the opportunity to compete, succeed, and live a good middle-class life.”

The America’s College Promise Act of 2026 will make the skills and credentials necessary to succeed in the workforce more accessible to all students by creating a new federal-state partnership to provide two years of tuition-free community college.

Specifically, the America’s College Promise Act of 2026:

Creates a partnership between the federal government and states to waive tuition and fees for two years of community and technical college programs for eligible students, while promoting key reforms to accelerate student success;

Creates a sliding scale for federal share beginning at 100 percent for the first year and ending at 80 percent for the fifth and subsequent years;

Ensures that programs offer academic credits that are transferable to four-year institutions in their state, or occupational training that leads to recognized credentials;

Maintains and encourages state funding for higher education;

Establishes a student success fund to improve enrollment, retention, transfer, or completion rates and labor market outcomes for underserved student populations, including students of color and low-income and first-generation college students, who attend community and technical colleges at disproportionate rates;

Waives two years of tuition and fees for eligible students at tribal colleges and universities; and

Establishes a new grant program to provide pathways to success at historically black colleges and universities and minority-serving institutions by covering a significant portion of tuition and fees for the first two years of attendance for low-income students.

title: Rep. Fry Introduces Legislation to Suspend Federal Gas Tax Temporarily
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Russell Fry (SC-07) introduced the Presidential Emergency Action to Stabilize Energy (EASE) Act. When enacted, the EASE Act will allow the President of the United States to declare a national emergency to suspend the gas tax for up to 120 days. Congressman Joe Wilson (SC-02) is an original cosponsor of the EASE Act.

“All across the country, American families are feeling the pinch with rising fuel prices,” said Rep. Fry. “When gas prices reached $5 a gallon under President Biden in 2022, Democrat majorities in the House and Senate just sat on the sidelines and pretended that fuel prices weren’t real. I refuse to abandon families when they are feeling the pressure financially. I am proud to introduce the EASE Act to give much-needed relief to men and women who are doing their best to make an honest living and put food on their tables. I look forward to Congress passing this bill so President Trump can give families the help they desperately need.”

“Families and businesses across the country feel the impact of higher fuel prices in their everyday budgets, and I am grateful to support this legislation, which provides an important tool to offer temporary relief for Americans,” said Rep. Wilson.

Under the EASE Act, the President would be required to issue a declaration of a national emergency caused by, or the potential to cause, a substantial disruption in the nation’s fuel supply. The initial federal gas tax suspension period would be 60 days. On day 45 of the suspension, the President can extend the relief for an additional 60 days by notifying Congress in writing that the emergency is continuing. The suspension cannot exceed 120 days, and the President may issue only one suspension per emergency.

The President can also declare an emergency when fuel prices increase substantially across the country. Declaration of the emergency gas tax suspension would bring the fuel tax rate to zero for gasoline and diesel fuel. The federal government will be required to make up lost tax revenue from the Treasury General Fund.

The EASE Act would not apply to any transaction after December 31, 2028.

Last month, Rep. Fry called on Congress to suspend the federal gas tax. President Trump and Energy Secretary Chris Wright have both supported lowering prices at the pump and called on Congress to suspend the gas tax temporarily. The EASE Act gives the administration tools to suspend that tax in light of a national fuel crisis.
