title: Rep. Gallagher's AB 2700 Signed Into Law, Delivering Path Forward for Wildfire Victims
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) today announced that Assembly Bill 2700, legislation he introduced while serving in the California State Assembly to help victims of utility-caused wildfires receive fair compensation, has been signed into law by Governor Gavin Newsom.

Gallagher introduced AB 2700 in response to the continued challenges facing wildfire survivors, including victims of the Camp Fire in Paradise, who have spent years seeking full and fair compensation for devastating losses. Following Gallagher's election to Congress, Assemblyman Joe Patterson (AD-05) took over as author and carried the legislation through the State Legislature.

"It was my great honor to take this bill on as one of my last actions in the legislature. Far too many wildfire victims are still waiting for the fair compensation they deserve," said Congressman Gallagher. "AB 2700 provides a pathway for accountability and real justice for fire survivors."

AB 2700 requires the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to determine the amount fire victims are owed and recommend compensation methods that do not raise utility rates.

The legislation builds on Gallagher's years of work representing communities devastated by catastrophic wildfires, including Paradise and other communities impacted by the 2018 Camp Fire.

"I am proud that I have had the privilege of working with Congressman Gallagher on this legislation," said Assemblyman Patterson. "AB 2700 is an essential bill to ensure wildfire victims, who have waited years to be paid their fair share, are provided a path to be fully and fairly compensated. No amount of money can undo what they have suffered, but my hope is that this bill provides a tangible step for them to rebuild and move forward."

Thousands of wildfire survivors, united under the Utility Wildfire Survivor Coalition, were instrumental in passing AB 2700. The survivors championed the legislation by contacting legislative offices and meeting with lawmakers and staff. They also testified at committee hearings.

"Earlier this year, the Utility Wildfire Survivor Coalition broadly reached out to members of the State Legislature to find someone willing to champion this legislation," said Will Abrams, Organizing Advocate of the Utility Wildfire Survivor Coalition. "James Gallagher, and later Joe Patterson, had the courage and conviction to lead this effort and champion the passage of AB 2700. Their leadership and our nonpartisan advocacy as the sponsors of this bill led to the bipartisan and unanimous support that marked every vote in the Legislature. Wildfire survivors across the state are grateful."

title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Introduces Legislation to Bring More Nurses to Public Schools
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — This week, Reps. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and Jen Kiggans (R-VA) introduced the bipartisan More Nurses in Rural Schools Act to address the shortage of nurses in the American public school system and ensure students have access to comprehensive, on-site care during the school day. The bill would provide access to student loan repayment for eligible nurses working in schools in health care deserts by opening up the existing National Health Services Corps Loan Repayment Program (NHSLRP) to part- and full-time registered nurses committed to serving schools in health professional shortage areas (HPSA).

While existing student loan repayment programs exist to bring qualified nurses to communities in need, these opportunities typically do not extend to school nurses, who often cannot meet full-time, year-round requirements and do not work in the 2% of public schools designated as School-Based Health Clinic (SBHC) facilities. As a result, registered nurses must choose between working in their communities and taking on the brunt of their student loans, or move to more established clinics. This leaves students without comprehensive services on-site in communities already combatting health care access challenges inflamed by H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut health coverage for 31,000 people across Southwest Washington.

The following report, by the NASN, elaborates on the challenges facing school nurses:

Specifically, the More Nurses in Rural Schools Act would eliminate these barriers for school nurses by:

Allowing the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to permit an individual who agrees to serve for a time period equal to 2 years or longer as a school nurse in an elementary or secondary school located within a health professional shortage area to participate in the NHSC LRP.

For part-time employees, the Secretary is directed to increase the time period of service to the same number of hours as an individual serving in such a position on a full-year, full-time basis.

Directing the Secretary to establish annual certification requirements for the purpose of verifying the number of hours worked by such individuals.

This follows the application process framework in the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program, which allows states to track these hours as they see fit.

Defining a “school nurse” as “a registered nurse who is employed by a school or local educational agency or State or State educational agency and is qualified under State law to provide assessment, diagnosis, counseling, educational, therapeutic, and other health services to meet student needs.”

In implementation, this bill would help bring comprehensive health care services to elementary and secondary schools across the country in HPSAs – the majority of which are located in rural and partially rural areas.

“Sending your kid off to their first day of school, it’s like your heart came out of your body and it’s walking around in front of you. You want to know your school has every single option they can to take care of kids when they need it.” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. “Letting schools become healthcare deserts isn’t in anyone’s best interest. My bill extends existing loan forgiveness programs to nurses who make the noble choice to serve their community and take care of our children. Especially in rural communities, they’re a priceless lifeline.”

“Every student deserves access to quality health care, regardless of where they live. As a nurse practitioner, I know firsthand how important it is to have a qualified nursing workforce available to care for patients and support their families.” said Rep. Kiggans, “I am proud to join Congresswoman Gluesenkamp Perez in introducing the More Nurses in Rural Schools Act to remove outdated barriers for nurses who want to serve their communities and bring more healthcare professionals to rural and underserved schools.”

“Every student, regardless of where they live, deserves access to a school nurse. The More Nurses in Rural Schools Act is an important step toward addressing persistent workforce shortages and ensuring that students in underserved communities are able to receive the timely, skilled care they need to stay healthy, safe, and ready to learn.” said Lynn Nelson, President of the National Association of School Nurses, “On behalf of the National Association of School Nurses, I thank Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and Representative Jen Kiggans for their bipartisan leadership and shared commitment to strengthening school health services and advancing health equity for rural children and families. Their collaboration demonstrates that supporting the health and success of students is a priority that transcends party lines.”

Supporting schools, especially in rural areas, has been a priority for Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. In 2025, she passed a bipartisan bill to reauthorize the Secure Rural Schools (SRS), recovering $8.9 million in 2024 and 2025 payments for local counties and schools, after it lapsed earlier that year. She has also done extensive work funding and supporting trades education in schools. Recently, she attended the ribbon cutting for a new CTE center at Fort Vancouver High school.

In addition, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez voted against H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was signed into law on July 4, 2025. This law eliminated Medicaid eligibility for roughly 17 million Americans–including 31,000 in Southwest Washington. The bill also failed to extend the Affordable Care Act (ACA) enhanced premium tax credits, which helped cover health care coverage costs for lower-income households. Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez co-led the Bipartisan Premium Tax Credit Extension Act to extend these tax credits for one year, giving families more time to make these important health care decisions.

This legislation is supported by the National Association of School Nurses (NASN)

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Co-Leads Bipartisan House Intelligence Committee Trip to Lebanon
text:
Above: Gottheimer and LaHood with Lebanese President Aoun.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Thursday, October 1, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), a member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, returned from a bipartisan congressional delegation to Lebanon that he led with U.S. Congressman Darin LaHood (IL-16). This trip comes at a moment of rare opportunity, with a new technocratic Lebanese government in place and Hezbollah’s influence significantly weakened.

Gottheimer pressed Lebanese leaders to fully disarm and defund Hezbollah and meet the obligations Beirut accepted when it signed the June 2026 Trilateral Framework with the United States and Israel. The delegation met with Lebanese government officials — including President Joseph Aoun, Speaker Nabih Berri, Lebanese Forces Party leader Samir Farid Geagea, and dozens of Members of Parliament including Michel Moawad — to discuss removing Iranian influence from Lebanon and the full and verifiable disarmament of Hezbollah.

In June, Lebanon and Israel signed a U.S.-brokered framework under which Lebanon would disarm Hezbollah and Israeli forces would withdraw in phases as that disarmament is verified. This marks the first Lebanese government to negotiate directly with Israel, and that momentum must continue to ensure the success of the deal. Implementation is still in its early stages. So far, the Lebanese Armed Forces have deployed to an initial set of villages, but no timetable or way to verify Hezbollah’s weapons and infrastructure are gone has been agreed, and Hezbollah continues to reject disarmament. Completing the framework is critical to returning all of Lebanon’s territory to the control of the Lebanese people, out of the grip of Hezbollah and its Iranian handlers.

“Lebanon is at a turning point. For far too long, Iran has used Hezbollah, its terror proxy, to hold the Lebanese people hostage. It has drained the country’s economy, weakened its institutions, and pulled it into wars the Lebanese people never chose,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “It’s time to return Lebanon to the Lebanese people. That means removing Iran’s influence and fully disarming and defunding Hezbollah. Lebanon made that commitment in June, and now it has to follow through fully, verifiably, and across the entire country. A Lebanon without Hezbollah is better for the Lebanese people, for the Middle East, and for America.”

On the trip, Gottheimer and the delegation focused on:

Enforcing the Trilateral Framework: Backing a time-bound, Cabinet-approved plan to disarm Hezbollah with real third-party verification, so that Hezbollah’s weapons, tunnels, and command structure are removed.

Removing Iranian influence: Stopping Iran from spreading its money, weapons, and influence through Lebanon. That means cutting Hezbollah’s smuggling routes and cash couriers, enforcing sanctions on the banks and businesses that rearm and refinance it, and rejecting any Iranian role in deciding Lebanon’s future.

Disarming Hezbollah: Holding Lebanon to the commitment it made when it signed the Trilateral Framework for the full, verified disarmament and dismantlement of Hezbollah nationwide, including the seizure or destruction of its weapons and tunnels, the closure of its smuggling routes, and the demobilization of its fighters.

Returning Lebanon to the Lebanese people: Backing Lebanese leaders and institutions working to rebuild a sovereign, free, and prosperous country.

Combating terror in the region: Working with partners to cut off terror financing, stop weapons smuggling, and protect U.S. troops, Israel, and our allies.

“Lebanon made a commitment in June, and what comes next is critical to the future of the country,” Gottheimer continued. “Every day Hezbollah keeps its weapons is another day Iran gets a vote in the future of Lebanon. A stable, sovereign Lebanon, free from Iran’s terror proxies, is good for the Lebanese people and vital to America’s national security. I’ll keep working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to support that outcome.”

While in Lebanon, Gottheimer also visited Maghen Abraham Synagogue and the Shrine of Our Lady of Lebanon.

Gottheimer has repeatedly pressed for Hezbollah’s disarmament. In June 2026, he and U.S. Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) introduced a bipartisan resolution condemning Hezbollah’s repeated ceasefire violations and calling on the Lebanese government and the Lebanese Armed Forces to ensure Hezbollah ceases all attacks and disarms. In December 2025, he and U.S. Congressman Jefferson Shreve (IN-6) led a bipartisan letter to the Lebanese President and Prime Minister urging them to disarm Hezbollah immediately, including by force if necessary.

title: Rep. Grijalva Introduces America’s College Promise Act to Expand Access to Tuition-Free Community College
text:
Tucson, AZ — Today, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva alongside House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), Representative Teresa Leger Fernández (D-NM-03), Representative Madeleine Dean (D-PA-04), and Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), introduced the America’s College Promise Act of 2026, legislation to make community college and two-year Tribal Colleges and Universities more accessible by waiving tuition and fees for eligible students.

“Students in Southern Arizona and across the country should not have to take on tens of thousands of dollars in debt just to get the education and skills they need to build a better future,” said Rep. Adelita Grijalva. “The America’s College Promise Act is about making sure that opportunity is within reach for every student — whether they are graduating from high school, entering the workforce, changing careers, or returning to the classroom later in life. By expanding access to community and technical colleges, we are investing in students, strengthening our workforce, and giving communities the tools they need to thrive.”

“At Pima Community College, our students are working toward a better future while balancing jobs, family responsibilities, and the cost of their education,” said Dr. Jeffrey Nasse, Chancellor of Pima Community College in Tucson, Arizona. "45 percent of PCC students are low-income. The America’s College Promise Act would help ease that financial burden and invest in the support students need to succeed in college and contribute to our local economies. We appreciate Congresswoman Grijalva’s leadership on legislation that would help more Southern Arizonans gain the skills and credentials to advance their careers and pursue their long-term goals.”

The legislation would create a federal-state partnership to waive tuition and fees for two years of eligible community and technical college programs. It would also provide support for institutions to improve enrollment, retention, transfer, and completion rates, particularly among low-income, first-generation, and underserved students.

“Community colleges play a unique and vital role in providing students access to a quality postsecondary degree. Regrettably, the chronic underfunding of community colleges is jeopardizing their ability to support their students and communities,” said Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott. “The America’s College Promise Act is a major investment in expanding opportunities for students and rebuilding a stronger economy.”

“In New Mexico, we know free community college can unlock the doors to a brighter future,” said Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández. “The America’s College Promise Act builds on New Mexico’s example by making sure students across the country can attend community college without the burden of tuition and fees. Our bill will provide funds for services students need to earn their degrees and reduce the financial burden for low-income students to attend TCUs, HBCUs, and MSIs.”

“As a professor, it was a privilege to witness students claim their education and seize their futures — yet the real fear and burden of immense student loan debt often deters young adults and returning students from expanding their learning,” said Rep. Madeleine Dean. “The America’s College Promise Act provides tuition-free community college courses and expands funding for HBCUs and trade schools, making the path to higher education and career readiness available to more Americans and future generations.”

“Every Wisconsinite deserves the opportunity to get the education and skills they need to land a good-paying job and build a better life, no matter where they come from or how much money their family makes,” said Senator Tammy Baldwin. “That’s why I am proud to work with my colleagues to remove barriers and lower the cost of community college, so more Wisconsinites have the opportunity to compete, succeed, and live a good middle-class life.”

The America’s College Promise Act of 2026 will make the skills and credentials necessary to succeed in the workforce more accessible to all students by creating a new federal-state partnership to provide two years of tuition-free community college.

The America’s College Promise Act of 2026 would:

Create a federal-state partnership to waive tuition and fees for two years of eligible community and technical college programs while promoting reforms designed to accelerate student success;

Establish a sliding federal funding share, beginning at 100 percent in the first year and transitioning to 80 percent beginning in the fifth and subsequent years;

Ensure educational pathways lead to opportunity by requiring programs to offer academic credits transferable to four-year institutions in their state or occupational training leading to recognized credentials;

Maintain and encourage state investment in higher education;

Establish a Student Success Fund to improve enrollment, retention, transfer, completion, and labor market outcomes for underserved students, including students of color and low-income and first-generation college students;

Waive two years of tuition and fees for eligible students attending Tribal Colleges and Universities; and

Create a new grant program for HBCUs and minority-serving institutions to cover a significant portion of tuition and fees during the first two years of attendance for eligible low-income students.

title: Rep. Hageman Introduces Battery Safety Placarding Act
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Harriet Hageman (R-WY) introduced the Battery Safety Placarding Act to require shipping labels for containers transporting lithium-ion batteries.

The lithium-ion battery market has exploded by more than 20 percent since 2024 with nearly every mode of transportation now involved in carrying this $150 billion dollar industry. A series of recent conflagrations across multiple modes of transit, however, have demonstrated the need to reduce safety risks associated with delivering this highly combustible technology nationwide. The danger presented by lithium-ion battery fires are often exacerbated by thermal runaway, wherein a violent chain of chemical reactions lead to extreme temperatures, toxic gas release, and an occasional explosion.

“Clear labeling for hazardous material in transit is fundamental for the safety of our law enforcement, first responders, and traveling public,” said Rep. Hageman. “Explosives, flammable liquids, and toxic substances are all examples of items that require visible placards to immediately signify when hazardous material is present. Knowing the risks that lithium-ion batteries can pose, they should be no exception.”

In addition to introducing the Battery Safety Placarding Act, Rep. Hageman also sent a letter to the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration requesting that they update the federal hazardous materials regulations administratively while Congress considers this new policy. title: Comisionado Residente responsabiliza al Gobierno por el alza en la luz y presenta alternativas
text:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, responsabilizó hoy al Gobierno por el aumento en la factura de luz que entra en vigor hoy. Una familia que consume 800 kilovatios-hora al mes pagará unos $42 más. El Comisionado Residente presentó cuatro alternativas para aliviar a las familias a corto plazo.

"Hoy las familias puertorriqueñas empiezan a pagar 18% más por la luz, y no es por mala suerte. Es el resultado de una reconstrucción lenta, de plantas averiadas y de un sistema que depende de una sola empresa para recibir el gas. La gente no puede seguir pagando los errores de otros", expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Nueve años después del huracán María, el 75% de los $14,300 millones en fondos federales obligados para la red eléctrica sigue sin desembolsarse, según la Oficina de Rendición de Cuentas del Gobierno federal (GAO). Mientras tanto, las plantas averiadas obligan a quemar diésel, un combustible mucho más caro.

"El Gobierno negoció con New Fortress un contrato de gas que la propia Junta de Supervisión Fiscal criticó por falta de competencia. Hoy esa empresa controla el única terminal por donde entra el gas a San Juan. Desde el 16 de septiembre las unidades 5 y 6 de la Central San Juan no reciben gas y estamos quemando diésel, que es cuatro veces más caro. El Negociado de Energía ya dejó fuera de la factura, por ahora, unos $75 millones vinculados a alegados incumplimientos de New Fortress, e investiga $19 millones en gas que Genera, su subsidiaria, habría pedido de más. El conflicto en el Medio Oriente ha empeorado los precios, pero no lo explica todo: el propio Negociado señaló plantas fuera de servicio y fallas en la entrega de gas", añadió el Comisionado Residente.

El Comisionado Residente propuso cuatro medidas inmediatas:

Que New Fortress responda por sus alegados incumplimientos. El Negociado de Energía dejó fuera de la factura, por ahora, unos $75 millones vinculados a los alegados incumplimientos de New Fortress. Esos costos no deben pasar nunca a la factura del pueblo.

Que el Gobierno asegure la entrada del gas y tenga un plan B. La demanda que presentó el Gobierno contra New Fortress es un paso, pero no basta. Hay que resolver ya la entrada del gas a San Juan y tener otro suplidor con contrato firmado por si New Fortress vuelve a fallar. Cada día que se quema diésel se paga en la factura de enero. El gobierno debe garantizar el suministro de gas finalizando su contrato de respaldo y comenzando a utilizar a los otros proveedores de GNL en la isla.

Que ADSEF aclare cuántos fondos federales de LIHEAP tiene disponibles. Este programa federal ayuda a pagar la luz a participantes de TANF y a otras familias de bajos ingresos que cualifiquen. ADSEF debe informar cuánto dinero tiene y cuándo abre las ayudas, ahora que más familias las necesitan.

Que el Gobierno identifique recursos para un alivio temporero. Si se encontraron $554 millones para el cheque de alivio contributivo, debe poder identificar recursos para aliviar la factura de luz mientras dure esta crisis, junto con incentivos para que las familias ahorren energía. Otras posibles medidas incluyen la reducción de la crudita y el trabajo a distancia. No obstante, urge que los alivios mantengan el presupuesto balanceado y que cada pérdida sea subsanada mediante recortes en otras áreas del presupuesto.

"Desde el Congreso he exigido que los fondos federales para la red se usen ya: he llevado el reclamo al Departamento de Energía federal con apoyo de republicanos y demócratas, y a Vivienda federal. También seguiré defendiendo en el Congreso los fondos de LIHEAP. Mi agenda es priorizar lo básico, y no hay nada más básico que prender la luz sin tener que escoger entre pagarla y comer", concluyó el Comisionado Residente.

title: Jayapal Introduces Legislative Framework Establishing National Charter System to Rein in AI
text:
SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) is introducing a new policy framework that reins in artificial intelligence (AI) by requiring every AI company to hold a federal charter to do business in the U.S. The AI charter is modeled after existing regulatory frameworks, combining the round-the-clock federal oversight, strict safety mandates, and structural separation built into national bank charters with the rigorous pre-release federal testing required for nuclear materials and dangerous weapons. The charter would ensure that the public’s interests come first and that the government has broad authority to hold AI companies accountable before they create harm rather than addressing abuses after the fact. AI companies that don’t agree, don’t comply, or put the public in danger get shut down.

“The crux of this bill is simple: if you want to be an AI company in this country, you have to obtain a public charter that has a broad set of terms and conditions to operate and ensure public benefit without the harms,” said Jayapal. “For too long, we’ve allowed a few Big Tech companies to dominate the market. They have used mass surveillance to steal private information, labor, and creative work, building trillion-dollar empires on our tracked personal lives. AI corporations and Big Tech are now following that same playbook. My National AI Charter Act framework gets at the root of the problem by disrupting the way the AI market is structured to give a very few companies all the power over our data and what happens with it and instead establishes clear rules of operation for these AI companies and prioritizes safety over profits.”

To date, traditional Big Tech policies have tried to patch up problems around the edges after harm is done, treating data privacy, children’s safety, worker rights, market concentration, and all the rest as separate issues. That approach hides the full scope, reach, and systemic impact of Big Tech’s surveillance monopolies. The fragmented response has allowed their lobbyists to divide the broad coalition of their victims, narrow fights to single-issue bills that they stall, make the case for self-regulation, and ignore the root profit drivers incentivizing their bad behavior.

The National AI Charter Act takes a fundamentally different approach by addressing the full scope of AI harms comprehensively upfront. The charter would be required to operate AI and its terms and conditions would be mandatory. At its core, the charter framework recognizes that AI risks are connected and driven by underlying market structures, surveillance business models, and profit motives. AI companies would be banned from building empires, releasing risky models, stealing through surveillance, exploiting workers, or causing harm. Gating market access to companies that comply with these requirements would break Big Tech’s grip on AI and protect the public from dangerous AI models.

The framework’s new legal authorities to hold AI companies accountable would build on those that already apply. They would not preempt or replace federal, state, and local laws, nor would they prevent or impede law enforcement agencies from enforcing those laws against AI companies or their executives. Instead, they would strengthen the hand of prosecutors and plaintiffs by proactively confirming the many ways these laws apply to AI, rather than leaving it to judges to interpret case by case. Most importantly, making this illegal conduct a charter violation would create a powerful additional enforcement tool with serious, mandatory consequences.

The National AI Charter Act framework’s comprehensive approach would bolster existing law enforcement by:

Taking power back from billionaires and putting the public and workers first: The handful of billionaires and tech giants that control AI’s future are locked in a dangerous race to the bottom. The framework separates AI companies from Big Tech monopolies and bans their predatory commercial surveillance so that AI isn’t baked into the core Internet platforms everyone uses or trained with data harvested by tracking everything people do online. It also claws back Big Tech’s ill-gotten gains from their monopoly data to fund direct payouts to all Americans.

Preventing harm up front instead of chasing it afterward: AI harms can spread too fast for after-the-fact enforcement to stop them, and fines don’t remedy the damage or truly deter it from happening again. The framework’s upfront charter requirements are not just rules to follow; they are a mandatory price of entry into the AI industry and the condition for remaining in it. Companies must continuously comply or get shut down.

Drawing bright lines on the full range of AI dangers: AI’s dangerous capabilities cannot be prevented with technical rules that quickly become obsolete; they have to be comprehensively banned outright. Under the framework, AI systems capable of going rogue, creating catastrophic hazards, replacing skilled work, exploiting children, or causing other serious public harms are outlawed and cannot be released.

Putting the government in charge of safety at every stage: AI companies have admitted the risks of their own systems while still insisting they should police themselves. The framework replaces the AI industry’s failed self-regulation with round-the-clock federal oversight, testing in government facilities and approval to release, adversarial stress tests, and a government-controlled kill switch.

Imposing strict liability on AI companies and executives: As long as the price of causing harm is likely to cost less than the potential profits, AI companies will keep taking reckless risks. The framework reverses these incentives by holding AI companies and their executives strictly liable for lawbreaking, with loss of charter and criminal penalties for the most serious violations.

“At the end of the day, the American people are feeling a loss of control, of their personal data, of their jobs, of their ability to even know what they see online is real,” Jayapal added. “This legislation would restore a level of control and ensure that every search made online isn’t tracked, every family photo posted isn’t training an AI model, and every piece of our lives isn’t monetized by corporations.”

A wide range of experts have weighed in on the need for a comprehensive approach:

“The public has paid an extraordinary price for big tech’s self-regulation. Representative Jayapal’s framework learns from those mistakes. For generations we have required banks, drug makers, and nuclear operators to meet public terms before they do business, and AI companies should be no different,” said Lina Khan, Director, Center for Law and the Economy, and former Chair of the Federal Trade Commission.

“This legislative framework meaningfully advances the ball to establish a comprehensive set of reforms to address the potential for societal harms from AI,” said Jonathan Kanter, former Assistant Attorney General of the Department of Justice’s Antitrust Division.

“We really need a framework like this to start getting to the big question of how Americans want to regulate AI,” said Tim Wu, Julius Silver Professor of Law, Science and Technology, Columbia Law School.

“Innovation and safety are not opposing concepts; they’re two sides of the same coin—which is why regulation is vitally important. AI is rapidly transforming our classrooms, workplaces, and economy, but Big Tech must be held accountable for their business models, just like every other industry in the country. If these companies want to win the trust of the American people, they must respect the rules of the road. Representative Jayapal’s framework does exactly that by establishing preemptive guardrails that compel AI firms to serve the public interest, not just the narrow interests of shareholders,” said Randi Weingarten, President, American Federation of Teachers.

“The comprehensive approach being pioneered by Representative Jayapal’s National AI Charter Act gets to the root of the extreme harms of unregulated and out-of-control AI. The mandatory requirement to be chartered and operate only under strict guardrails and associated liability will hold companies accountable and ensure that protecting the public is considered first as tech is created. Public Citizen applauds this move to fight concentration and to defend children, workers, and the general public from pervasive harm,” said Lisa Gilbert, Co-President, Public Citizen.

“I’m thrilled that Representative Jayapal is taking such a leading role in addressing the enormous societal risks posed by increasingly powerful and uncontrollable AI systems. Efforts like the National AI Charter Act to address the full scope of AI harms are more important today than ever before,” said Anthony Aguire, President and CEO, Future of Life Institute.

“Big Tech companies have continually pulled the rug out from under families, workers, and small businesses to build powerful and unaccountable Big Tech monopolies that dictate to us how we should live our own lives. Enough is enough. We are proud to support the National AI Charter Act because it will establish desperately-needed rules of the road, punish AI companies that release dangerous products, and create the clear public benefit that the American people are calling for,” said Sacha Haworth, Executive Director, Tech Oversight Project.

“The same billionaires who walked away with huge tax breaks last year are now racing to take over AI. For years they’ve lobbied every attempt at regulation to death. Representative Jayapal’s plan goes after the source of their power: their monopolies, their surveillance, and their stolen data. It’s the first plan big enough to match the problem, and it puts families back in charge,” said Kristen Crowell, Executive Director, Families Over Billionaires.

“This is not a time for half measures. We are facing serious challenges, if not crises, on every possible front in this country, and we need leaders who are putting forward proposals that meet the moment. This framework puts humans at the center of the debate about AI and regulation and puts power back in the hands of people over the technology that shapes their lives,” said Shaunna Thomas, Executive Director, Guardrails Action.

“We have a long history of governing banks, utilities, critical infrastructure. In all of these, we have leverage over market interests, and the ability to gate access to the market on the condition that the public interest is protected. We need commensurate leverage over large AI companies, and this is the right lineage to draw upon,” said Amba Kak, Co-Executive Director, AI Now.

“Rep. Jayapal is right: if you want to run an AI company in this country, you should have to accept the public’s terms. For too long, Big Tech has acted first and answered for the harm later, if ever. A national charter would change that. We also support her proposal to structurally separate the AI stack. And we urge Congress to consider building on the authorities existing agencies already have. There’s more work ahead to make sure this framework can stand up to Big Tech’s lawyers and lobbyists, and we look forward to doing it with her,” said Nidhi Hegde, Executive Director, American Economic Liberties Project.

“We are in the midst of a reckoning on AI as working families and communities across the country are rightfully standing up and sounding the alarm on the growing harms that this technology is posing on our day to day lives. For too long, Big Tech CEOs have been able to divide and distract policymakers while they use the public’s own data to raise prices, push millions of working people into debt, and rake in record profits. It is long past time for policymakers to break Big Tech’s grip on AI and we applaud Congresswoman Jayapal for unveiling the National AI Charter Act Framework which marks a critical first step in reining in Big Tech and protecting families,” said Mike Pierce, Executive Director, Protect Borrowers.

“It’s unacceptable that Big Tech continues to abuse our data, turbocharge scams, and act with impunity. This framework reflects the interconnectedness of the harms that AI companies are already causing and the necessity of strong, robust enforcement mechanisms that can provide meaningful protections for consumers,” said Susan Weinstock, CEO, Consumer Federation of America.

“We welcome Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal’s leadership to address AI’s real harms. We’re encouraged to see a comprehensive, structural approach with sharp guardrails and bright lines. For too long, a handful of tech giants have written the rules and remade society to suit themselves. It’s high time the public wrote the future instead,” said Stacy Mitchell, Co-Executive Director, Institute for Local Self-Reliance.

“For far too long, the tech oligarchs and those whom they directly or indirectly fund have sought to normalize how the modern technology sector prefers to operate. Congresswoman Jayapal rightly recognizes as illegitimate those practices that tech oligarchs have long celebrated as creative and adventurous even as they violate longstanding laws and norms. In a democracy, it is publicly elected figures who are responsible for leading the future, not the oligarchic class,” said Jeff Hauser, Executive Director, Revolving Door Project.

“AI poses very real risks to safety, privacy, workers, competition, and more. This range of harms requires a comprehensive, structural policy response. In many critical industries, we mandate charters to do business, impose bright-line bans on problematic conduct, subject firms to independent inspection, and use other common-sense tools to reduce risks. The U.S. needs to deploy these same tools to keep powerful firms accountable and to put the public’s interest first in AI,” said Asad Ramzanali, Director of AI & Technology Policy, Vanderbilt Policy Accelerator.

“This is a smart framework that recognizes how powerful AI companies are already putting the public at risk, exploiting data, and consolidating control over critical technologies and markets. Adopting the charter model offers a sweeping yet adaptable way to welcome innovation while imposing enforceable obligations for safety and fair competition, placing necessary checks on private power, and ensuring corporations develop AI in the public interest,” said Courtney Radsch, Director of the Center for Media and Digital Governance, Open Markets Institute

“AI companies and their executives are threatening working people’s health, safety, and pocketbooks in their reckless race for profits. Congresswoman Jayapal’s National AI Charter framework would take on these threats in a comprehensive way by putting the public interest first and making the existence of AI firms contingent on their compliance with strong safety and privacy requirements alongside worker, consumer, and investor protections,” said Maya Jenkins, Senior Policy Analyst, Americans for Financial Reform.

An outline of the framework can be found here.

The framework was developed, in part, following a hearing that Jayapal hosted on the dangers of surveillance AI conducted by Big Tech.

title: Kaptur Announces Over $5.5 Million Federal Investment in UToledo Research
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, announced that several University of Toledo research projects will receive awards from the United States Department of Health and Human Services. In total, $5,559,857 will be awarded to fuel the pursuit of understanding across many disciplines of medical research.

“Our region is privileged to have an institution like University of Toledo that is committed to furthering medical knowledge for the benefit of all,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “As a recently designated R1 Research Institution, UToledo’s extremely talented scientists and medical professionals lead the way in pioneering research. Federal investments in medical and scientific research are critical to new innovations, and I am honored to have helped secure today’s awards. I look forward to seeing the many impacts of the University of Toledo’s research in our Northwest Ohio communities and beyond in the years to come.”

The awards include:

$401,618 for research on the relationship between gut bacteria and blood pressure regulation under Dr. Tao Yang

$249,000 for research on the Zika virus’s harm to blood-retinal barriers under Dr. Sneha Singh

$455,827 for research on opioid toxicity in the human body under Dr. Issac Schiefer

$561,300 for research on bone marrow blood cell development and its effects on diseases like leukemia and lymphoma under Dr. Fan Dong

$768,796 for research on Lyme disease prevention under Dr. Mark Wooten

$1,675,569 for breast cancer research under Dr. Jianmin Zhang

$496,344 for research on developing pancreatic cancer therapies under Dr. Shi-He Liu

$448,793 for research on early cell development in the reproductive process under Dr. Tomer Avidor-Reiss

$502,610 for research on arthritis and spinal disc degeneration under Dr. Mohammad Yunus Ansari

As a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, Congresswoman Kaptur is dedicated to securing bipartisan support and funding for Northwest Ohio communities. She has also been instrumental in delivering Federal support to the UToledo’s research efforts, a major factor in its recent recognition as an R1, top-tier university for Doctoral Universities: Very High Research Activity in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. In August 2026, she announced over $1.8 Million in National Science Foundation and National Institute of Standards and Technology research awards andnearly $4 Million in US Department of Health and Human Services awards for the university.

title: Whip Clark on CNN: Democrats Are Putting the American People Front and Center
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (MA-5) appeared on CNN News Central to call out Republicans for refusing to rein in AI and highlight Democrats’ fight to lower costs for working people. Below are excerpts of the conversation.

On Republicans Refusing to Put Guardrails on AI:

“We should be here in DC — where I am today — but there are no Republicans around working on this very issue.

“We want to be the leaders in this technology, but we want it to benefit the American people. We want to protect jobs, and protect our kids, and develop a way to harness AI for good, and protect the American people from harm.

“What we have is a president who is out there berating Americans opposed to data centers in their communities, saying they are ‘backwards’ and will be ‘poor’ if they don’t get on board. Inviting in — not regulation and outside oversight over this powerful technology with all its benefits but its very real threats — instead, bringing in the heads of these companies and saying, ‘Okay guys, you just police yourselves. We’re sure that will work out fine.’ Meanwhile, the Trump family continues to enrich itself by investing in data centers and AI.

“So, we have a total lack of addressing this very real concern of the American people by the president and the Republican Party.”

On GOP Cancelling Votes Instead of Finding Solutions for Americans:

“Again, we want to be the leaders in this. But there are ways as we are working with experts and we should be here working on these solutions to answer what the companies say they want: outside regulation, outside audits of what they’re doing. That’s not just people they hire who work within their companies, but let’s have people outside evaluating what happened. We have set up agencies for this kind of review in transportation, in financial services, and this is something we need to come together as Americans to address.

“Meanwhile, Mike Johnson’s response was to send us home early, rather than tackling this very key issue that Americans are worried about. I hear about it everywhere I go in my district and everywhere I go in this country.”

On Pete Hegseth’s Incompetence:

“I am extremely concerned about where Secretary Hegseth is taking our military as we are at war in Iran — a war that the president and the secretary recklessly put us into without making the case to the American people. Without coming to Congress as required.

“Democrats three times have put forward War Powers Resolutions asking them to stop this war, to come and make sense of this for people.

“And what are we seeing? We are seeing them covering up casualties of our service members. What a disgrace for the secretary of defense to cover up those casualties. Then we are seeing the impacts of this war on Americans — whether it’s at the gas pump or the cost of diesel that is driving our farmers into debt. They are not sure if they’re going to be able to afford to plant because of this record high cost of diesel. And all of this is going to come home in continued rising prices of groceries and other goods that American families are already struggling to purchase.

“So, to have the secretary try and make this into some ‘it’s their appearance and their testosterone levels that count.’ It is their military readiness. It’s making sure we have enough munitions. It is having a clear mission that is defined and aligns with our national security needs. None of that is being met by this secretary and this president.”

On Democrats’ Fight for an Affordable America:

“We keep talking to the American people and listening to them. Our message is very clear: We see your family, and we’re going to fight for you. We’re going to fight to lower the cost of housing and groceries and gas. We’re going to fight to make sure that when you need healthcare, you can afford it and you can get it when and where you need it. And then we’re going to make sure that we are holding the crooks accountable, because [the] corruption we are seeing in this Republican Party has a real cost for the American taxpayers.

“It’s time to put the American people first. Put their priorities first. Put their voices back in these halls, here in the Capitol.

“We have great candidates who are connected to their communities, who understand how hard it is for people to get a foothold, never mind have success, in this economy.

“The terms I hear are ‘I’m drowning. I’m barely able to keep my head above water. I can’t keep treading water.’ This is not how we build security for American families… And when we win the majority, this is how we’re going to govern: with the American people front and center.”

Watch the full interview, HERE.

title: ICYMI: Kelly honors latest Community Champion in Erie County
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- On Tuesday, September 29, U.S. Rep. Mike Kelly (R-PA) presented a Community Champion Award to Joe Pfadt for his outstanding community service to the Erie area.

As President and Founder of Warriors to Washington, Pfadt annually leads Erie-area veterans to Washington, D.C. where they tour the nation's capital. As CEO of the Oliver Hazard Perry Shipyard, Pfadt continues to preserve Erie's maritime history for future generations. Pfadt is also a retired high school social studies teacher at Harbor Creek High School.

"Joe Pfadt exemplifies what it means to be community-minded and to put his neighbors first, particularly our local veterans. Without his leadership, so many of the amazing projects in Erie County would not be possible. He is most deserving of this award," said Rep. Kelly.

BACKGROUND

The Community Champion Award recognizes and thanks service-minded individuals throughout Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District for selfless and significant contributions to their surrounding communities. Each winner is presented with an official award plaque from Rep. Kelly’s office, a flag flown over the U.S. Capitol building, and a statement of congratulations entered into the official Congressional Record.

title: Larsen: Naval Station Everett is Ideal Homeport for Future Frigates
Tower Development with Alleged Kremlin-Linked Owner Hits Roadblock
text:
MENLO PARK, CA – A controversial development at 80 Willow Road is facing a significant roadblock after the Menlo Park City Council refused to approve it.

Days before, the property’s owner, billionaire Vitaly Yusufov, drew scrutiny for his reported ties to Kremlin officials and individuals linked to organized crime when Congressman Sam Liccardo (CA-16) called on Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to launch an immediate federal review of the project’s ownership and financing. Liccardo urged the Office of Foreign Assets Control and the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States to investigate Yusufov and consider sanctions if the review uncovered sanctionable conduct.

“We need more housing, but our housing shortage cannot turn our communities into safe harbors to avoid sanctions or launder illicit funds,” said Liccardo. “This marks an important step toward keeping Kremlin-linked money out of our community and protecting our national security.”

title: Lofgren Demands Answers to Overdue Oversight Requests Regarding DOE Award Terminations, Warns Secretary Wright of Consequences for Continued Evasion
text:
(Washington, DC) – On Monday, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) sent a letter to Department of Energy (DOE) Secretary Chris Wright demanding that he answer multiple months-overdue oversight requests from the Committee regarding DOE’s 2025 award terminations.

“For more than 15 months, my colleagues and I have attempted to conduct oversight of DOE’s award termination activities,” writes Ranking Member Lofgren in her letter. “We have asked questions, requested documents, and demanded answers directly from you during official testimony. But DOE has thwarted our oversight repeatedly by refusing to provide the requested information and documents. In doing so, DOE has hindered our ability to evaluate DOE’s actions and obstructed the Committee’s ability to fulfill its constitutional role. The following oversight requests from the 119th Congress remain outstanding, and DOE must comply with them.

1. Please provide to the Committee a comprehensive list of DOE officials who participated in the “Portfolio Review Process” in 2025 and 2026.

2. Please provide to the Committee copies of the “one pagers” or “one-page summary memos” that were created for each award being reviewed as a part of the “Portfolio Review Process.”

3. Please provide to the Committee copies of the assessments that were completed for each award terminated in May 2025 and October 2025 for the purpose of evaluating whether those awards had sufficiently met the criteria utilized by DOE under the “Portfolio Review Process.”

“Secretary Wright, these are straightforward requests for specific documents and information. I cannot help but believe that your ultimate goal in refusing to comply with them is to evade responsibility for your actions. Did you believe that you could arbitrarily terminate billions of dollars’ worth of awards, lie about the reasons why, and escape accountability? Now, as the political consequences of your actions mount, it appears you hope to quietly walk away from the entire issue, while Congress simply moves on without holding you accountable. That hope would be mistaken. Congressional oversight must be respected, and my oversight requests must be complied with. If DOE fails to do so, we will redouble our efforts using every available tool at our disposal. I urge DOE to comply now.”

Access the letter here and below.

Dear Secretary Wright,

In 2025, the Trump Administration illegally began to erase all traces of federal activity that it disagreed with. At the Department of Energy (DOE), you led the charge. You targeted billions of dollars’ worth of clean energy and infrastructure investments, engaged in a politicized “review” to cast a veneer of legitimacy over your arbitrary decisions, terminated awards that you disliked in a manner that was designed to inflict maximum pain on your political opponents, and then lied continuously to the public about why you had done it. The process was a sham and a disgrace, unworthy of the oath you swore to uphold the Constitution.

But now, as lawsuits accumulate, criticism mounts, and judges declare your actions illegal, you do not seem quite as proud of the decisions that were supposedly so righteous a year ago. Indeed, you appear eager to distance yourself from the award terminations of 2025 and to avoid responsibility for them. Since the early spring of 2025, I have attempted to conduct oversight of the Department’s actions to get to the bottom of what happened. DOE has evaded my oversight at every turn. This letter serves to reaffirm that my prior oversight requests from the 119th Congress pertaining to DOE’s award terminations remain outstanding. I expect DOE to comply. If the Department does not, it should prepare to face the consequences of its obstruction.

The story of DOE’s award terminations in 2025 has been told so many times by this point that it barely needs retelling. I will briefly do so merely to provide context for my oversight requests related to the issue. Upon taking office in January 2025, the Trump Administration immediately froze tens of billions of dollars’ worth of research, development, demonstration, and commercialization projects at DOE that had been awarded under the Biden Administration. In your first Secretarial Order on February 5th, 2025, released two days after you were confirmed as Secretary of Energy, you announced that DOE would “comprehensively review its R&D portfolio” without providing any additional detail. On May 15th, 2025, you initiated a new process to “conduct focused reviews of awards and other forms of financial assistance on a caseby-case basis,” while asserting that DOE possessed the discretion to “terminate [a] project based on the outcome of DOE’s evaluation.” This process, called the “Portfolio Review Process” or PRP, moved suspiciously quickly. A mere two weeks later, on May 30th, 2025, DOE announced the termination of 24 awards issued by the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations (OCED) totaling more than $3.7 billion. Several months after that, on October 1st, 2025, DOE announced the termination of 321 additional awards from across the Department totaling roughly $7.56 billion. In both instances, DOE claimed that the terminations resulted from a “thorough and individualized financial review of each award,” during which the Department had concluded that the awards “were not economically viable and would not generate a positive return on investment of taxpayer dollars.” After the October 2025 award terminations, DOE also asserted that the awards “did not adequately advance the nation’s energy needs.” Finally, in April 2026, you appeared before a House Appropriations Subcommittee and testified that the PRP was complete and that no additional award terminations would be forthcoming.

The repercussions of DOE’s award terminations were immense. Projects were thrown into chaos, companies were pushed to the brink of collapse, and jobs were lost. Taxpayer dollars were wasted. Major clean energy research, development, and demonstration projects – indeed, entire nascent clean energy sectors – were destabilized. Congressional energy priorities enshrined in law were thwarted. We continue to deal with the fallout of these award terminations to this day. From the beginning, as the Ranking Member of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (“the Committee”), I sought to conduct oversight of DOE’s actions in order to understand the processes and motivations that lay behind the Department’s attempt to wipe out over ten billion dollars in taxpayer-funded awards. On May 5th, 2025, I sent a letter to DOE along with a group of my Ranking Member colleagues in the House of Representatives and Senate that condemned the Department’s comprehensive freeze and review of Biden-era awards as “illegal and harmful to the public.” We asked how “DOE or any other part of the administration [is] assessing which DOE projects to cancel or continue, and under what criteria?” We did not receive a response from the Department before the PRP was announced on May 15th and $3.7 billion in awards was terminated on May 31st.

After DOE terminated the first round of awards on May 31st, Department officials provided a briefing for Committee Staff. Based upon the information disclosed in that briefing, I sent another letter to DOE on September 9th, 2025, along with two other Ranking Members, expressing “serious concerns” that the PRP was “haphazard, disorganized, and politically driven,” and calling upon DOE to “cease the cancellation process and restore respect for independent, merit-based reviews.” We also requested specific documents created during the Department’s review of OCED awards related to DOE’s evaluation of those awards and its assessment of whether the awards should be terminated, as well as a comprehensive list of DOE officials who had participated in the review process. DOE never provided those requested documents.

When DOE terminated more than $7.5 billion worth of awards on October 1st, 2025, the Department publicly claimed that the terminations were rooted in policy-based criteria such as economic viability, taxpayer return, and national energy priorities. You denied any political motivation behind the terminations in congressional testimony as recently as April and June 2026.3 But DOE’s cover story unraveled due to an unlikely source: its own concessions in court. Over the course of one lawsuit filed in November 2025, DOE formally stipulated that “a primary reason” for the October 2025 award terminations was “whether the grantee was located in a ‘Blue State’”; a judge ruled that DOE’s award terminations were unconstitutional and illegal in January 2026. Over the course of a second lawsuit related to the same terminations, DOE went even further and formally stipulated that the October 2025 award terminations were “based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state,” and that they were not based upon “any programmatic, statutory, cost-reduction, or performance-based factor.”

When you testified before the Science Committee on June 10th, 2026, Science Committee Democrats confronted you about the award terminations and reiterated the oversight requests that I had previously made to DOE. One of my colleagues, Energy Subcommittee Ranking Member Deborah Ross, demanded that DOE disclose the identities of the Department officials who participated in the PRP; once again, you refused to do so. Another one of my colleagues, Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Gabe Amo, pressed you to explain the contradiction between your denials of any political motivation in the award terminations and DOE’s formal concessions in the November 2025 lawsuit; once again, you denied that any of the October 2025 award termination decisions were made based on politics. It was July 2026, the very next month, when DOE’s formal concessions in the second lawsuit – even more sweeping – became public, even though you had surely known about them when you testified before the Science Committee. Your materially false statements to the Committee left me with no choice but to formally refer you to the Department of Justice, which I did along with Ranking Member Amo on August 4th, 2026.

For more than 15 months, my colleagues and I have attempted to conduct oversight of DOE’s award termination activities. We have asked questions, requested documents, and demanded answers directly from you during official testimony. But DOE has thwarted our oversight repeatedly by refusing to provide the requested information and documents. In doing so, DOE has hindered our ability to evaluate DOE’s actions and obstructed the Committee’s ability to fulfill its constitutional role. The following oversight requests from the 119th Congress remain outstanding, and DOE must comply with them. Please provide the requested information and documents no later than 5:00 PM on Wednesday, October 14th, 2026:

1. Please provide to the Committee a comprehensive list of DOE officials who participated in the “Portfolio Review Process” in 2025 and 2026.

2. Please provide to the Committee copies of the “one pagers” or “one-page summary memos” that were created for each award being reviewed as a part of the “Portfolio Review Process.”

3. Please provide to the Committee copies of the assessments that were completed for each award terminated in May 2025 and October 2025 for the purpose of evaluating whether those awards had sufficiently met the criteria utilized by DOE under the “Portfolio Review Process.”

Secretary Wright, these are straightforward requests for specific documents and information. I cannot help but believe that your ultimate goal in refusing to comply with them is to evade responsibility for your actions. Did you believe that you could arbitrarily terminate billions of dollars’ worth of awards, lie about the reasons why, and escape accountability? Now, as the political consequences of your actions mount, it appears you hope to quietly walk away from the entire issue, while Congress simply moves on without holding you accountable. That hope would be mistaken. Congressional oversight must be respected, and my oversight requests must be complied with. If DOE fails to do so, we will redouble our efforts using every available tool at our disposal. I urge DOE to comply now.

Pursuant to Rule X of the House of Representatives, the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology “shall review and study on a continuing basis laws, programs, and Government activities relating to nonmilitary research and development.” The Committee possesses jurisdiction over “all energy research, development, and demonstration, and projects therefor, and all federally owned or operated nonmilitary energy laboratories, as well as the commercial application of energy technologies.”

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Releases Statement on 50-Car Pileup on I-95
text:
CHARLESTON, S.C., (Oct 1, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace released the following statement on this morning's mass-casualty 50-car pileup on I-95 near Lake Marion:

“Lives can change in an instant, and this morning, they did. What began as an ordinary commute for hundreds of South Carolinians and travelers quickly turned into a horrific scene.

“Our first responders ran straight into the chaos. Santee Fire, Clarendon County Fire Rescue, and the South Carolina Highway Patrol worked to reach those trapped and injured. We owe these brave men and women more than words can say.

“Moments like this remind us who our first responders are. They do not hesitate. They do not stop. They get the job done.

“We’re praying for everyone injured and for their families. We’re asking God for strength, healing, and a full recovery.

“To everyone traveling I-95, please be patient, follow local officials’ guidance, and give crews the space they need to safely clear the scene.

“God bless South Carolina, and God bless our first responders.”

title: Rep. Nancy Mace's Jobs Bill Heads To President's Desk
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (Oct. 1, 2026) – If you can do the job, you shouldn't need a diploma to prove it. That's the idea behind Congresswoman Nancy Mace's (SC-01) Skills-Based Federal Contracting Act, which passed the Senate unanimously late last night and now goes to President Trump to be signed into law.

Right now, federal agencies can require degrees or years of experience for contract work, even when those requirements have nothing to do with the job. Mace's bill changes that. Under the bill, agencies can only demand those credentials if they put in writing why they're truly needed.

The result: more skilled Americans get a fair shot at government work, more companies can compete, and taxpayers get the best people for the job.

"The best people for the job can now get the job,” said Congresswoman Mace. "For too long, Washington has rewarded unnecessary college degrees over proven work skills and shut hardworking Americans out of job opportunities. My bill tears down this wall down and puts merit and skills first. If you can do the job, you deserve the job. Taxpayers deserve the best results, and America deserves the best workforce built on skill known to man."

The Skills-Based Federal Contracting Act prohibits federal agencies from including minimum education or experience requirements in contract solicitations unless they provide a written justification demonstrating those standards are essential to meeting mission needs. The legislation expands opportunities for skilled American workers, promotes greater competition, and helps ensure taxpayer dollars are spent on the most qualified talent rather than unnecessary credential requirements.

If signed by President Trump, the bill will become law, marking a bipartisan milestone in modernizing the federal contracting process and expanding opportunities for skilled American workers. The last republican before Rep. Mace to have a bill signed in to law was Congressman Henry Brown more than 25 years ago, in 2010.

“Talent doesn't always come with a college diploma attached," added Congresswoman Mace.

title: Congressman Mackenzie Announces Over $20 Million Returned to Constituents Through Federal Casework
text:
BETHLEHEM, Pa. — Today, Congressman Ryan Mackenzie announced that his office has helped return $20.7 million to constituents across the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos through federal casework and assistance since taking office.

Of the $20.7 million returned since taking office, $10.3 million was returned to constituents in 2025, and more than $10.4 million has already been returned so far in 2026.

Congressman Mackenzie and his constituent services team work directly with residents to navigate federal agencies, resolve outstanding issues, and recover money owed to them. The office assists constituents with issues involving the Internal Revenue Service, Social Security Administration, Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Personnel Management, passports, immigration matters, and other federal agencies.

“Helping people cut through red tape and get the answers, benefits, and money they are owed is one of the most important services our office provides,” said Congressman Mackenzie. “Reaching $20 million returned to constituents represents thousands of individual cases where our team was able to step in and help someone who did not know where else to turn. Whether it is a delayed tax refund, Social Security benefits, veterans’ benefits, or another issue with a federal agency, our offices are here to help people throughout the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos.”

For constituents like James A. Bestider of Lehighton, assistance from Congressman Mackenzie’s office helped resolve a reimbursement that had been severely delayed.

“After months of frustration trying to have a government agency reimburse me thousands of dollars in overpayment, I reached out to Congressman Ryan Mackenzie’s office for assistance,” said Bestider. “Congressman Mackenzie and his staff were able to procure my reimbursement in a timely manner. I am a retired senior citizen on a fixed budget, and I am deeply grateful for Congressman Mackenzie and his staff for helping me and my family resolve this issue.”

John Yaswinski of Nazareth contacted the office after an IRS refund had remained unresolved for nearly a year. With assistance from Congressman Mackenzie’s office, the refund was returned within weeks. The office also helped Yaswinski secure a Social Security appointment as he considered retirement.

“Words cannot express my heartfelt gratitude for Congressman Mackenzie and Ms. Pasquariello’s assistance in securing my IRS refund in such a timely manner,” said Yaswinski. “My IRS refund sat in limbo for the better part of a year prior to contacting the Congressman’s office. Within a few weeks, my refund was returned. Their care, attention, and service to me are unmatched by any elected official I have known. They really went above and beyond.”

For John Tegan of Palmerton, the office helped resolve issues surrounding his federal retirement after he left the General Services Administration. Congressman Mackenzie’s staff contacted the agency on his behalf, helped move his application to the Office of Personnel Management for review, and continued following up until his retirement package was completed.

“Rochelle and Congressman Mackenzie’s office provided continuing follow-up and attention to make sure the matter was resolved,” said Tegan. “Rochelle also offered support and empathy for my situation.”

Mary Hittinger of Walnutport also turned to the office for assistance recovering money owed by the IRS.

“I am very appreciative for the assistance we received from Congressman Mackenzie, Rochelle, and the rest of the office staff in recovering money owed to us from the IRS,” said Hittinger. “Their assistance made such a meaningful difference, and we sincerely appreciated their support. It’s so nice to know that we have a congressman who’s always there for us.”

Since taking office, Congressman Mackenzie’s team has:

Returned $20.7 million to constituents through federal casework and assistance;

Completed more than 11,000 constituent services, including casework, meetings, tours, and other assistance; and

Responded to more than 291,000 constituent letters and emails.

Bringing home over $160 million to support local health care, first responders, manufacturing, and more.

Securing more than $12 million in FY26 Community Project Funding for public safety, infrastructure, first responders, and other local priorities across the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos

Congressman Mackenzie has offices in Lehigh, Northampton, and Carbon counties, as well as a downtown Allentown office offering Spanish-language services by appointment. The office also holds mobile office hours throughout the region to make federal constituent services accessible to residents across the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos.

title: Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) Secures $2,062,000 for Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office and Syracuse Police Department’s New Mobile Command Centers
text:
SYRACUSE, NY — Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today announced that $2,062,000 in federal Community Project Funding he secured for the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office and the Syracuse Police Department to purchase and equip new Mobile Command Centers has been formally awarded.

Representative John W. Mannion said, “Our law enforcement professionals need proper support and resources to protect our communities and respond to emergencies. These federal investments answer a locally identified need, giving the Onondaga County Sheriff's Office a new mobile command unit and helping the Syracuse Police Department replace its Mobile Command Post Bus. Together, these upgrades will improve emergency response, strengthen regional coordination, and better protect residents and visitors across Central New York. I am proud to stand with our professional local law enforcement officers and continue building on my record of supporting public safety initiatives, both in Congress and during my time in the State Senate.”

Onondaga County Sheriff Toby Shelley said, "When a critical incident unfolds, seconds count, and clear communication across jurisdictions can mean the difference between chaos and control. I want to express my sincere gratitude to Congressman Mannion for securing this federal funding, which directly invests in the safety of every resident in Onondaga County and throughout Central New York. This Mobile Command Unit is not just a vehicle; it is a state-of-the-art operational backbone. It provides our Tactical Operations Division, our local police, fire departments, EMS, and regional emergency management partners with the interoperable, on-scene communications and unified command capabilities required in high-stakes environments. When crisis strikes, our responders must be connected, protected, and fully coordinated. This grant ensures our men and women on the front lines have the reliable, modern technology they need to manage complex emergencies effectively and return home safely."

Syracuse Police Chief Mark Rusin said, “The Syracuse Police Department is deeply grateful to the Department of Justice for its support of our efforts to enhance public safety and regional emergency preparedness. The investment in a modern Mobile Command Post will significantly strengthen our ability to coordinate unified responses to major incidents, protect our residents and visitors, and collaborate effectively with our public safety partners throughout Onondaga County. This support ensures that our officers have the reliable tools and technology they need to meet today’s complex challenges and continue serving the community with excellence.”

The $1,031,000 for the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office will allow for the procurement and outfitting of a state-of-the-art mobile command unit to enhance emergency response, strengthen interagency coordination, and improve operational effectiveness in the field. The Mobile Command Center will assist in all aspects of Onondaga County emergency operations, including safety and coordination at large public events, search and rescue missions, SWAT operations, enhanced communications, and deployment of modern equipment during critical incidents.

The $1,031,000 for the Syracuse Police Department will allow the department to replace its Mobile Command Post Bus with a modern and fully equipped vehicle to enhance emergency response and public safety operations. The vehicle will support unified command during active shooter incidents, major criminal investigations, natural disasters, hazardous materials incidents, search and rescue operations, and other large-scale incidents. The project also includes integration into emergency operations plans, operator training, equipment testing, and regional exercises with public safety partners.

The $2 million investments to support the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office and the Syracuse Police Department are part of 15 Community Project Funding priorities advanced by Representative Mannion in partnership with local leaders across Central New York and the Mohawk Valley. All 15 projects have passed Congress and been signed into law, delivering a total of more than $15 million in federal funding to address locally identified needs—including public safety improvements, lead service line replacement, water and wastewater modernization, workforce training, airport infrastructure upgrades, and research critical to America’s economic and national security.

title: It’s a Girl! Rep. McIver Gives Birth To Her Second Child, A Symbol Of Hope For Her Family
text:
NEWARK, NJ – Today, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) announced the birth of her second child, a healthy baby girl. She released the following statement:

“Being a mom is one of the greatest joys of my life, and I feel deeply grateful to welcome this beautiful, healthy baby into the world,” said McIver. “There really aren’t words to describe how blessed my family feels to welcome a new life into the world. Getting the chance to raise a family is a priority and a delight for me, something I hope everyone who wants to, gets the chance to do. Bringing a child into the world is a reminder not only of why we fight for maternal healthcare and reproductive rights, but of why we fight for the rights and freedoms of our most vulnerable– they are someone’s babies too.”

McIver is only the fifteenth-ever member of Congress to give birth while serving. She also has a ten-year-old daughter and is one of only a small group of women serving in Congress with school-aged children.

She has shared her tumultuous reproductive health journey, including her battle with uterine fibroids, which required multiple surgeries. One such surgery had her in New Jersey in the morning and rushing to Washington, D.C., that same night to make it in time to vote on the House floor. These experiences have bolstered her deep commitment to advocating for women’s reproductive rights, and strong reproductive and maternal healthcare for all.

McIver is also in the middle of a legal battle, facing 17 years in federal prison from charges brought by the Trump Department of Justice (DOJ). The charges stem from a lawfully authorized oversight visit McIver conducted at Delaney Hall, the controversial immigration detention center in her district. The case is ongoing.

McIver is a strong supporter of the recent push for proxy voting for new parents, as she will not be granted any paid maternity leave from Congress. She will take the month of October to heal, be with her family, and bond with her new child. She plans to return to voting in November.
