title: ICYMI: Senators Blunt Rochester, Cruz Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Give Families Greater Flexibility with 529 Savings
text:
U.S. Senators Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.) and Ted Cruz (R-Texas) introduced the 529 Retirement Enhancement Act of 2026. This bipartisan legislation eliminates the $35,000 lifetime cap on rollovers from 529 education savings accounts to Roth IRAs.

“529 accounts can be incredibly useful in helping families prepare for higher education, but plans can change. A student may receive a scholarship, not use the full balance of their account, or simply choose a different path. Families should be able to preserve financial flexibility regardless of what their child’s education decisions are years down the road,” said Senator Blunt Rochester. “I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan 529 Retirement Enhancement Act to remove barriers to saving and give families greater peace of mind when investing in their children’s future.”

“I have been committed throughout my Senate career to expanding 529 savings accounts to give parents increased flexibility to save and invest in their children’s future,” said Senator Cruz. “The law currently penalizes families when their children receive a scholarship or choose an alternative to college, leaving education savings unused, which in turn serves as a disincentive to initially use these accounts. The bipartisan 529 Retirement Enhancement Act will give parents greater flexibility to roll over unused education funds into their children’s Roth IRAs, and I’m proud to introduce it.”

This legislation is supported by the Investment Company Institute.

Investment Company Institute Chief of Government Affairs and Public Policy Tom Quaadman said, “ICI applauds Sens. Cruz and Blunt Rochester for their commonsense legislation giving families greater financial flexibility and security. Families with unspent funds in a 529 plan should not be penalized because a student received a scholarship or pursued other options. The Cruz-Blunt Rochester bill permits unused education savings to be moved into a Roth IRA allowing young people to get started on their path to a secure financial future.”

title: NEWS: Senators Blunt Rochester, Booker Lead Resolution Recognizing World Menopause Awareness Month
text:
U.S. Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), a member of the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, and U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-N.J.) introduced a resolution recognizing October 2026 as World Menopause Awareness Month. The onset of menopause can be life-changing, with standard symptoms lasting over seven years, even longer for Black and Hispanic women. Yet, each year, women from all backgrounds begin menopause with little guidance on what to expect, and report having limited access to strategies to help ease the transition. The World Menopause Awareness Month Resolution seeks to increase awareness of the menopausal experience and expand access to care during and after menopause.

Below is an excerpt of the resolution:

“Each year, women in the United States enter the menopausal transition with little guidance on what to expect before, during, and after their reproductive years…As many as 40 percent of menopausal women say their symptoms interfered with their work performance or productivity weekly, and nearly 1 in 5 have left or considered leaving the workforce because of their symptoms.

“[This resolution] expresses support for the recognition of October 2026, as “World Menopause Awareness Month,” recognizes the impact of menopause on women at individual and societal levels, as well as on the health and economic development of the United States… [and] supports women having access to appropriate health information and services to promote healthy aging and a high quality of life before, during, and after menopause.”

title: NEWS: Senators Blunt Rochester, Curtis Introduce Bills to Help Public Understand Impacts of Data Centers
text:
U.S. Senators Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.) and John Curtis (R-Utah) today introduced the Data Center Transparency Act of 2026 and the Data Center Community Empowerment Act of 2026 to improve understanding of data centers’ impacts on the environment and quality of life and increase community involvement in the development of future data centers. The Data Center Transparency Act would require federal agencies to collect information on data centers’ environmental impact, energy consumption, and water consumption. The Data Center Community Empowerment Act would give communities access to technical expertise to understand the potential benefits, costs, and infrastructure impacts of proposed data center development. The House companion to the Data Center Transparency Act is led by Congressman Robert Menendez (D-N.J.-8).

“The development of data centers is rapidly increasing across the country, and there is legitimate concern about how these projects could raise utility bills, harm our environment, or impact public health,” said Senator Blunt Rochester. “I am proud to work with Senator Curtis to introduce The Data Center Transparency Act and the Data Center Community Empowerment Act to ensure communities have a say in how these projects impact their quality of life. These bills are a necessary step to create a safer, more inclusive, and informed process.

“Americans are rightly skeptical when a large company tells them not to worry about the impacts of a new data center in their community,” said Senator Curtis. “The answer to that distrust is transparency. Communities deserve independent, reliable information about what these projects mean for their power bills, water, infrastructure, and local economy. These bills give local leaders the facts and expertise they need to ask tough questions and make informed decisions—without Washington or industry making those decisions for them.”

The Data Center Transparency Act would:

Require EPA to collect and update data every three months on the environmental impacts that data centers have on:

Water consumption, utility costs, and potential pollutants; and

Air pollution cumulative impacts and greenhouse gases.

Require the Energy Information Administration to collect and update data on energy consumption of data centers, including total energy consumption of data centers, associated grid build-out, and impact on household energy bills every six months.

The Data Center Community Empowerment Act would:

Establish a program at the Department of Energy to:

Provide technical assistance to State, local, and Tribal governments on the potential energy, water, infrastructure, economic, and other community impacts associated with data center development;

Develop a Data Center Community Toolkit with easy-to-understand information and resources specifically designed for nontechnical local officials;

Provide independent project analysis at a community’s request, including an assessment of information voluntarily provided by a data center developer and the reliability of its data and reasonableness of its assumptions, projections, and conclusions; and

Preserve local decision-making by requiring DOE to remain neutral on individual data center projects and prohibiting the Department from recommending whether a particular project should be approved or rejected.

title: Booker, Van Hollen, Hirono, Blunt Rochester Introduce SOAR Act to Expand Support for New Small Businesses with Up to $1 Million in Grants
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), and Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE) introduced the Startup Opportunity Accelerator (SOAR) Act, legislation to expand support for early-stage businesses in rural, low-income, and historically underserved communities.

The bill would authorize $80 million annually for 10 years through the Small Business Administration (SBA), including grants of up to $1 million for eligible startup accelerators, incubators, universities, and other organizations that help entrepreneurs launch and grow their businesses. Funding could support mentorship, leadership development, access to financing, workspace, and other services for early-stage businesses.

“America’s next great entrepreneurs, inventors, and creators are already hard at work building in communities all across the country. But too often, whether a small business gets the chance to turn their ideas into something bigger depends more on where you live, who you know, and where you are from,” said Senator Booker. “America can’t afford to keep talent on the sidelines. Our bill would build ecosystems in every corner of the country to ensure that the next generation of innovators are supported with the access to capital, mentorship, and resources they need to turn their big ideas into thriving businesses.”

“Investing in entrepreneurs and small businesses in underserved areas can create jobs and build wealth in communities that have been historically left behind. This legislation would provide entrepreneurs across the country with resources to support their success, helping to build a more inclusive and prosperous economy that works for all Americans,” said Senator Van Hollen.

"Capital has never flowed equally in this country, and the numbers prove it: Black entrepreneurs receive just one percent of all venture capital, even as businesses under five years old drive nearly every net new job created in America. Senator Booker's Startup Opportunity Accelerator Act doesn't just acknowledge that gap, it closes it, requiring that half of every dollar in this fund reach the entrepreneurs our economy has overlooked for too long. This is the kind of deliberate, measurable action U.S. Black Chambers, Inc. has been calling on Washington to take, and we are proud to stand behind it,” said U.S. Black Chambers Inc.

Startups are a major driver of job creation, but access to capital and business support remains uneven. Between 1982 and 2011, businesses five years old or younger generated nearly all net new job creation nationwide. Yet only 1 percent of venture capital funding goes to Black-owned firms, 1.5 percent goes to Latino-owned firms, and 1.9 percent goes to startups owned solely by women.

The SOAR Act would specifically:

Establish a competitive grant program for organizations supporting early-stage startups.

Provide grants of up to $1 million to eligible startup accelerators, incubators, universities, and other organizations.

Prioritize programs serving women, veterans, minority entrepreneurs, people with disabilities, and rural communities.

Strengthen oversight and transparency of the program.

The SOAR Act is cosponsored by U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), and Mazie Hirono (D-HI), and Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE).

The SOAR Act is supported by Small Business Majority, U.S. Black Chambers, Inc., The Innovation Space, United States Hispanic Business Council, BBC Entrepreneurial Training & Consulting, LLC, New Jersey Innovation Institute, Frontier Mission Network, LegalCORPS, Rockies Venture Club, Inncuvate, Oregon Entrepreneurs Forum / Oregon Entrepreneurs Network, and the Arrowhead Center at New Mexico State University.

Read the full one-pager on the SOAR Act here.

title: Booker Announces $7.2 Million Federal Grant to Connect Millville Executive Airport to Regional Highway Network in South Jersey
text:
NEWARK, N.J. – Today, U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) announced that the City of Millville will receive $7,215,300 from the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) for the Cumberland Freight Access and Economic Development Project. The project will extend Nabb Avenue to Millville Executive Airport, closing a key gap between the airport's industrial corridor and the regional highway network. Senator Booker supported the city's application in a July letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.

The grant comes from USDOT's Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight and Highways Projects (INFRA) program, which was significantly expanded by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL). Signed by President Biden in 2021 with Senator Booker's vote, the law increased INFRA funding by more than 50 percent over previous levels, providing approximately $8 billion for the program from Fiscal Year 2022 through 2026. This year's awards are the final round of INFRA grants that received this infusion of funding under BIL.

"Cumberland County has the highest poverty rate and lowest median household income in New Jersey, and this project opens the door to the jobs and investment its residents deserve," said Senator Booker. "Extending Nabb Avenue gives Millville Executive Airport the road connection it needs to grow as a freight and trade hub, and it makes the roads safer for the families who live nearby. This is exactly what the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law was designed to do: put federal dollars to work on the projects communities have been fighting for."

The project will build an approximately 1.35-mile, two-lane extension of Nabb Avenue (County Road 634) from West Main Street (New Jersey Route 49) to Fairton-Millville Road (County Road 698). It will also convert the intersection of Buckshutem Road and Fairton-Millville Road into a modern roundabout, add a new traffic signal at West Main Street, and install stormwater management basins.

The extension will directly serve Millville Executive Airport, the second-largest airport in New Jersey by acreage, as well as the James R. Hurley Industrial Park and the New Jersey Motorsports facility. The airport holds a Foreign-Trade Zone designation in conjunction with the South Jersey Port Authority, can land jets as large as a Boeing 737, and serves as an emergency landing site for Philadelphia and Atlantic City International Airports. The project is expected to create more than 200 jobs for residents of Millville and surrounding communities while improving freight access, safety, and emergency response across the region. It has support at the state, county, and local levels, as well as from the metropolitan planning organization and the Delaware River and Bay Authority.

Millville Mayor Dan Dixon thanked Senator Cory Booker, Congressman Jeff Van Drew, and their offices for their work in securing $8.2 million in federal funding to support the Nabb Avenue Extension, advancing a project that has been stalled for nearly 20 years. The funding includes a $7.2M grant through the United States Department of Transportation’s INFRA (the Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight & Highway Projects program), as well as a $1M federal appropriation in the fiscal year 2026 federal budget for land acquisition and utility relocation associated with the extension.

“This funding is a major step forward for Millville,” said Mayor Dixon. “We appreciate Senator Booker’s and Congressman Van Drew’s work to secure this investment through the United States Department of Transportation and look forward to continuing our partnership as the project moves ahead.” The extension would provide a more direct route to the James R. Hurley Industrial Park, allowing construction vehicles and other heavy trucks to bypass the center of Millville. It would reduce downtown truck traffic, improve industrial access, and support business expansion, new development, and job creation.

“Nabb Avenue is an important investment in Millville’s economic future,” added Dixon. “Providing better access to our industrial park will help existing businesses grow and attract new employers while improving conditions for residents, pedestrians, and businesses downtown.” “Together, these investments bring us closer to delivering a project that will benefit Millville for years to come.”

“The County is so pleased to see this strong collaborative effort for improved traffic and freight access receive much-needed funding,” said Sandra Taylor, Cumberland County Commissioner Director. “It is partnerships like this, between the city, county, state and federal levels of government all working in unison that ultimately form solutions to hard challenges. The Nabb Avenue extension project will be a huge catalyst for a new level of economic development in the county and I sincerely want to thank everyone who has played a part in this success.”

“The success of the City of Millville in securing these very competitive funds is a testament to the importance of the Nabb Avenue Extension project and to the work of all involved,” said Matthew Pisarski, Cumberland County Planning Director. “I want to sincerely thank all of our funders. There are so many wonderful things happening in Cumberland County, and it is exciting to see the strong support being provided from Trenton and Washington, D.C.”

The full text of Senator Booker's letter is below and available here.

July 15, 2026

The Honorable Sean Duffy

Secretary

U.S. Department of Transportation

1200 New Jersey Avenue, SE

Washington, DC 20590

Dear Secretary Duffy:

I write in support of the application submitted by the City of Millville to the Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight and Highways Projects (INFRA) program for Fiscal Year 2026. The Cumberland Freight Access and Economic Development Project will extend County Road 634 (Nabb Avenue) to the Millville Executive Airport, the second-largest airport in New Jersey by acreage. The Nabb Avenue Extension is the missing surface transportation link needed to connect an airport-industrial growth corridor in southern New Jersey to the regional highway network.

The extension of Nabb Avenue will improve freight access, safety, emergency response, economic development, and quality of life in Cumberland County, the county with the highest poverty rate and lowest median household income in New Jersey. This extension will directly support the Millville Executive Airport, the James R. Hurley Industrial Park, and the New Jersey Motorsports facility. Millville Executive Airport has a Foreign-Trade Zone designation, in conjunction with the South Jersey Port Authority, which enhances the regional and national potential for international commerce. Furthermore, the airport has the capacity to land up to 737-sized jet aircraft and acts as an emergency landing site to support both Philadelphia and Atlantic City International Airports.

The Cumberland Freight Access and Economic Development Project will increase the airport's capacity as a freight hub and create more than 200 new jobs for residents of Millville and surrounding communities. Support for this project includes the state, county, and local levels as well as the metropolitan planning organization and the Delaware River & Bay Authority. The extension of Nabb Avenue, estimated to cost more than $17 million, will boost throughput in Millville's downtown and surrounding neighborhoods. Once completed, this extension will result in safety improvements, transportation cost savings, and quality of life improvements for local residents. INFRA funding for this project will enhance Millville Executive Airport's standing as a nationally significant commercial and industrial center and a prime location for multimodal freight, aviation growth, and new trade opportunities.

I ask that you give this proposal all due consideration and thank you in advance for your attention to this important project. Should you have any questions, please contact me or my staff at (973) 639-8700.

Sincerely,

Cory A. Booker

United States Senator

title: Booker, Scott Sickle Cell Awareness Resolution Passes The Senate with Unanimous Support
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — The U.S. Senate unanimously passed a resolution introduced by Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Tim Scott (R-SC) designating September 2026 as Sickle Cell Disease Awareness Month.

“For decades, people living with sickle cell disease have faced devastating pain, serious health complications, and an inequitable health care system that has too often failed to take their suffering seriously — and Black Americans have been disproportionately impacted ,” said Senator Booker. “This bipartisan resolution recognizes the nearly 100,000 Americans living with sickle cell disease and serves as a reminder that Congress must do more to close racial gaps in care, invest in better treatments, and ensure patients can live longer, healthier lives.”

“Raising awareness about sickle cell anemia means working toward a future where Americans living with the disease can lead healthier lives with fewer limitations. The Senate’s unanimous passage of this resolution reinforces our commitment to making treatment and care more accessible, affordable, and attainable,” said Senator Scott. “New gene therapies should give us all hope, but we still have significant hurdles to overcome to ensure every American battling SCD has the opportunity to live out their American Dream.”

This resolution builds on Senator Booker’s longstanding work to improve access to treatment and care for Americans living with sickle cell anemia. In 2025, Senators Booker and Scott reintroduced the Sickle Cell Disease Comprehensive Care Act, which would allow state Medicaid programs to provide comprehensive, coordinated care to patients with sickle cell anemia through a health home model.

The resolution was cosponsored by U.S. Senators Katie Britt (R-AL), Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS), James Lankford (R-OK), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Tina Smith (D-MN), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Todd Young (R-IN).

title: Boozman Recognizes 2026 Angels in Adoption Honoree Tiffany Wright
text:
U.S. Senator John Boozman (R-AR) recognized Tiffany Wright as a 2026 Angels in Adoption honoree for her longstanding commitment to improving outcomes for children and families across Arkansas.

Wright serves as the Director of the Division of Children and Family Services at the Arkansas Department of Human Services. She oversees programs focused on child safety, abuse and neglect prevention, foster care and adoption. Since joining the division in 2009 as a family service worker, she has dedicated her career to protecting vulnerable children, supporting families and helping those in foster care find stability and thrive.

“Tiffany has consistently and compassionately shown up for Arkansas children and families, often during some of the most difficult moments of their lives,” Boozman said. “Her dedication to creating better futures for children and giving families the support they need reflects the very best of public service. I appreciate all she has done and continues to do for Natural State kids, families and communities.”

Throughout her tenure, Wright has worked to strengthen foster family recruitment and adoption efforts across the state, including through the Project Zero Heart Gallery, which shares the stories of children in foster care to help connect them with adoption-minded parents. In 2025, she took that commitment a step further with a pledge that saw her run 179 miles, one for every child in Arkansas’s foster care system awaiting adoption.

The Angels in Adoption program is coordinated by the Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute (CCAI), a nonpartisan organization that works to raise awareness about children in need of safe, loving homes. Members of Congress select honorees who have made extraordinary contributions to adoption, permanency and child welfare.

“Every day, across the country, people are doing extraordinary work to help children and families find safety, stability, and permanency, and Angels in Adoption gives us an opportunity to shine a national spotlight on that work,” CCAI Executive Director Kate McLean said. “In Arkansas, Director Tiffany Wright exemplifies the kind of dedicated leadership and commitment to children that this program was created to recognize. We are proud to celebrate her contributions and to highlight the important work happening in communities across the country to ensure every child has the opportunity to find a permanent family.”

Boozman annually recognizes an Arkansan or Arkansas organization for outstanding contributions to adoption, foster care and the well-being of children and families.

title: U.S. Senators Katie Britt and Maggie Hassan’s Clergy Act Passes United States Senate Unanimously
Cassidy, Warner Legislation to Improve IRS Customer Service Passes Senate
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA) and Mark R. Warner (D-VA) applauded Senate passage of the bipartisan Taxpayer Assistance and Service (TAS) Act, which includes several provisions from the Improving IRS Customer Service Act. The legislation will improve communication between the IRS and taxpayers, streamline tax compliance processes, and ensure taxpayers have timely access to expert assistance, among other necessary tax administration reforms. The bill now awaits passage in the House of Representatives.

“Taxpayers should get the help they need without a fight. This package gives the American people a stronger voice and makes help easier to access,” said Dr. Cassidy.

“Provisions from my Improving IRS Customer Service Act will bring clarity and relief to taxpayers in Virginia and across the country,” said Sen. Warner. “I want to thank my colleagues in the Senate for passing this crucial bill to make tax season a little bit easier for the millions of Americans who file taxes. I urge my colleagues in the House to pass the bill and send it to the president’s desk to become law.”

The provisions of the Improving IRS Customer Service Act included:

Establishing a dashboard to inform taxpayers of backlogs and wait times;

Expanding electronic access to information and refunds;

Expanding callback technology and online accounts;

Informing individuals facing economic hardship of collection alternatives.

Background

Cassidy first introduced the Improving IRS Customer Service Act in 2024, reintroducing it in 2026. Cassidy has also introduced the bipartisan Fairness in Foreign Filing Act, which would protect well-meaning taxpayers from harsh penalties and strengthen the Taxpayer Advocate Service. Provisions from both efforts were included in the TAS Act, which contains 65 reforms to improve taxpayer services, strengthen taxpayer rights, and modernize IRS operations.

title: Senator Collins Announces $27.8 Million to Restore Nearly 44 Miles of I-295
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins, Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, announced that the Maine Department of Transportation (MaineDOT) has been awarded $27,808,000 to restore nearly 44 miles of I-295 between Portland and Topsham. The funding was awarded through the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Infrastructure for Rebuilding America (INFRA) grant program.

The 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) increased funding for the INFRA program by more than 50 percent, providing approximately $8 billion for the program from Fiscal Years 2022 through 2026. Senator Collins was part of the core group of 10 senators who negotiated the IIJA.

“Interstate 295 is a vital corridor in Maine’s transportation network for residents, businesses, and visitors alike,” said Senator Collins. “This funding will help extend the life of nearly 44 miles of I-295, improving safety and reliability for motorists traveling between Portland and Topsham. As a lead negotiator of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, I am pleased to see this law deliver significant investments in Maine’s transportation infrastructure.”

The project will resurface nearly 44 miles of I-295 between Portland and Topsham. Crews will mill the existing asphalt down to the concrete, perform structural concrete repairs, and install a stress-absorbing mastic interlayer and a high-polymer asphalt overlay. The project will also improve surface drainage, apply reflective pavement markings, upgrade guardrails, and replace weigh-in-motion and continuous vehicle count stations.

Since joining the Appropriations Committee in 2009, Senator Collins has helped direct more than $2 billion in federal funds to Maine’s transportation infrastructure.

title: Cornyn, Cruz Resolution Recognizing Texas A&M University’s 150th Anniversary Passes Senate
Cornyn, Weber Introduce Bill to Establish a National Recreation Area Along Texas Coastline
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Senator John Cornyn (R-TX) along with U.S. Congressman Randy Weber (TX-14) introduced the Lone Star Coastal National Recreation Area Act, which would establish the Lone Star Coastal National Recreation Area, a 168-mile unit of the National Park System along the Upper Texas Coast, to strengthen coastal resilience and conservation:

“The Texas Gulf Coast supports a thriving ecosystem, vital fisheries, and critical infrastructure that helps meet our nation’s energy needs, but it’s increasingly vulnerable to threats from flooding, hurricanes, and shoreline erosion,” said Sen. Cornyn. “By establishing a National Recreation Area along nearly 170 miles of the Upper Texas Coast, this legislation would strengthen coastal resilience, promote conservation efforts, and better protect the Lone Star State’s natural resources for generations to come.”

“The Texas Gulf Coast is home to families who have spent generations fishing its bays, walking its beaches, and taking pride in every community on our corner of the map,” said Rep. Weber. “This bill will help more families enjoy this coast and bring more visitors to local businesses, all while protecting private property rights and keeping decisions in local hands. I’m grateful Senator Cornyn is joining me in leading this effort so the Texans who know this coast best can lead the way in sharing it with the next generation.”

U.S. Congressman Randy Weber (TX-14) is leading companion legislation in the House of Representatives, and the legislation is also cosponsored by Representatives Brian Babin (TX-36), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Wesley Hunt (TX-38), Troy Nehls (TX-22), and Beth Van Duyne (TX-24).

Background:

This legislation establishes the Lone Star Coastal National Recreation Area (LSCNRA), which would span nearly 170 miles of the Upper Texas Coast across portions of Jefferson, Chambers, Galveston, Brazoria, and Matagorda counties to enhance the coastal region’s recreational and natural assets, strengthen coastal resilience, and support local economies through Texas-led public-private partnerships.

The Upper Texas Coast includes major ports, navigation channels, energy infrastructure, and other industrial facilities that are critical to Texas and the United States. Specifically, this coastal region manufactures 80% of the nation’s military-grade fuel, 60% of the nation’s aviation fuel, and 30% of the nation’s gasoline. The LSCNRA will support these thriving industries, recognize the importance of wetlands and coastal systems in protecting communities from flooding, and support wildlife, fisheries, and water quality.

The Lone Star Coastal National Recreation Area Act would:

Establish the Lone Star Coastal National Recreation Area (LSCNRA) as part of the National Park System;

Direct the U.S. Secretary of the Interior to administer the LSCNRA with Texas, local governments, private landowners, and other private partners;

Establish the Lone Star Coastal Partnership to coordinate participation between public and private entities, including the U.S. Department of the Interior, to develop, submit, and implement a management plan;

Preserve Texas and local governments’ civil, criminal, regulatory, taxation, and fish-and-wildlife authority;

And authorize Congress to appropriate federal funds that would support the LSCNRA and Partnership.

This legislation is endorsed by the Greater Houston Partnership (GHP), Gulf Coast Protection District (GCPD), Matagorda County Economic Development Corporation, Bay City Community Development Corporation, National Parks Conservation Association, Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation, Ducks Unlimited, the Texas Conservation Alliance, Matagorda County Judge Bobby Seiferman, Jefferson County Judge Jeff Branick, Chambers County Judge Jimmy Sylvia, League City Mayor Nick Long, and Trust for Public Land.

title: Cortez Masto Fights for Independent Oversight of Federal Housing Finance Agency
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) pushed back against the unprecedented step taken by Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) head Bill Pulte to defund the agency’s Office of the Inspector General (FHFA-OIG). The proposed 60 percent funding cut is a significant break from previous funding levels and comes as Pulte is under increased scrutiny for his abuses of power. Acting Principal Deputy Inspector General James Hodge has come out against these cuts, which would make it harder for FHFA-OIG to investigate waste, fraud, and abuse throughout the agency, including at Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and the Federal Home Loan Banks.

“Bill Pulte has abused the power of the FHFA to target his political rivals – on both sides of the aisle,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “The Inspector General’s office goes after the exact type of fraud, waste, and abuse Mr. Pulte himself is engaging in. Significantly scaling down the operations of the watchdogs who could investigate you for wrongdoing is completely unethical.”

Last night, Senator Cortez Masto was blocked by Senate Republicans from passing her legislation to protect funding for the FHFA-OIG. Her legislation would mandate funding for FHFA-OIG be set at levels requested by the office, enabling them to carry out their mandate. Raising its operating budget from penalties it collects, the FHFA-OIG is tasked with investigating title and mortgage fraud, protecting mortgage lenders and home buyers from predatory practices, and ensuring a sound and secure mortgage and banking system. Despite Senator Moreno’s objections, this legislation is not about overfunding FHFA-OIG, but about preserving its very operations. Read the full bill here.

Cortez Masto has also joined her Democratic colleagues on the Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee in a public condemnation of Pulte’s unprecedented move to defund the FHFA watchdog. The Senators note that this reduction in funding would result in a layoff of 70-80% of the FHFA-OIG staff, including experienced law enforcement officers, drastically impeding the office’s work to investigate waste, fraud, and abuse at FHFA.

The Senators conclude by stating: “Your decision is unacceptable and yet another example of this Administration’s willingness to flout the law and evade accountability. It also indicates that FHFA is uninterested in finding and eliminating mortgage fraud—an issue that you have repeatedly claimed to prioritize at FHFA. We demand that you immediately reverse course and fully fund the FHFA OIG for FY27 with a budget no less than the OIG’s original FY27 funding request.” Read the full letter here.

Senator Cortez Masto has pushed for oversight of multiple Departments under the Trump Administration – including at the Department of the Interior, the U.S. Forest Service, the National Nuclear Security Administration, the Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Agriculture, and General Services Administration. The Senator has been a vocal opponent of Pulte, advocating for oversight of his abuses of power as head of the FHFA and pushing back against his appointment as Acting Director of National Intelligence.

title: Cortez Masto Statement on Ninth Anniversary of the Route 91 Harvest Festival Massacre
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Catherine Cortez Masto released the following statement on the ninth anniversary of the Route 91 Harvest Festival Massacre, the deadliest mass shooting in modern American history:

“On October 1, 2017, the city of Las Vegas, the state of Nevada, and the entire United States were shaken to their cores when 58 people were killed and nearly 500 were injured at the Route 91 Harvest Music Festival. Two more people died later from their injuries. It’s been nine years since that harrowing day and the weeks that followed, but I still remember it so clearly.

“Those were some of our darkest days as a city, and I know it was felt throughout the country. It would have been so easy for Las Vegans to give in to the fear and despair. But instead of letting the shock of this tragedy take over, Nevadans from across our state brought the light back to Las Vegas. Nine years later, we are still Vegas Strong.

“We remain grateful for the first responders, the members of the Las Vegas Metro Police Department, the health care workers, and the everyday Nevadans who dropped everything to help save lives in the aftermath. And we will never forget the victims of the Route 91 Harvest Festival massacre and their families. Today and every day, we carry them in our hearts.”

title: Cortez Masto, Wyden, Durbin Demand Trump Administration Abandon Plan to Strip Tax Credits from 700,000 American Taxpayers
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), and Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) led six of their colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration abandon a plan that would prevent up to 700,000 Deferred Action on Childhood Arrivals (DACA) and Temporary Protected Status (TPS) recipients and other tax-paying immigrants from claiming tax credits they are eligible for.

The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and the Department of Treasury are proposing a rule change that would prevent hundreds of thousands of taxpayers from claiming the Adoption Tax Credit, the American Opportunity Tax Credit, the Child Tax Credit, and the Earned Income Tax Credit. DACA and TPS recipients have been lawfully claiming these taxes for decades.

“According to your own estimates, the proposed rule change could affect up to 700,000 taxpayers,” the Senators wrote in a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and IRS CEO Frank Bisignano. “This would include more than 300,000 individuals living in households with a DACA recipient, two-thirds of whom are U.S. citizens and who have, on average, lived in the United States for over 28 years. The practical effect of these new regulations would be to deny tax credits to immigrants who are legally eligible for them and lawfully present in our country, and to create a byzantine and unworkable system for both tax preparers and taxpayers.”

“The Administration has no legal authority to change congressionally enacted tax law via regulation…” they continued. “Since the passage of PRWORA in 1996, no federal agency has interpreted refundable tax credits as federal public benefits restricted to qualified immigrants. If Congress intended for refundable tax credits to be treated as federal public benefits, it has had over 30 years to clarify the statute.”

“The proposed rule is clear regulatory overreach that would have disastrous impacts for lawfully present immigrants and their families who are legally eligible for refundable tax credits,” they concluded.

In addition to Senators Cortez Masto, Wyden, and Durbin, the letter was signed by Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), and Patty Murray (D-Wash.). The full text of the letter is available here.

The first and only Latina Senator, Cortez Masto has consistently supported immigrant communities in Nevada. She has called on both the Biden and Trump Administrations to protect Dreamers, TPS holders, and other immigrants. Cortez Masto has worked to pass meaningful immigration reform that balances critical border security measures with a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers. Earlier this year, the Senator attended and spoke at a naturalization ceremony for new American citizens at the Sand Harbor Amphitheater at Lake Tahoe, Nevada.

title: Crapo Statement on Support for Ratepayer Protection Act
text:
Washington, D.C.—U.S. Senator Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) released the following statement after voting in favor of the Ratepayer Protection Act, legislation led by Senator Jon Husted (R-Ohio) to address the increasing energy infrastructure demands associated with large data centers:

“The U.S. must remain globally competitive in the advancement of artificial intelligence, which requires supporting the infrastructure and energy resources necessary for this growing technology,” said Crapo. “However, those costs should not be borne by Idaho ratepayers and communities. Large-load customers, such as data centers, should be responsible for the infrastructure and resources needed to power and maintain their facilities.”

The Senate voted 57-43 in favor of advancing the legislation, falling three votes short of the 60 votes needed to invoke cloture and proceed to consideration of the bill.

Background on the Ratepayer Protection Act

The legislation would codify key elements of President Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge, announced in March 2026, under which major technology companies committed to covering the energy and infrastructure costs associated with new data center development rather than shifting those costs to consumers.

If enacted, the Ratepayer Protection Act would propose standards that state regulators could enforce when considering integrating new large-load customers with a demand of 100 megawatts or more onto the grid. Those recommendations include:

Recovery of full, incremental cost of upgrades by the large-load customer over a long period of time through a special rate charge or other agreements. This protects utilities and their ratepayers from being left responsible for upgrade costs associated with a large-load customer, even if that customer later reduces operations or leaves the system entirely.

Financial assurances requiring the large load customer to pay for any generation, transmission or other infrastructure necessary to serve their load, protecting utilities and ratepayers from that financial burden. This ensures large-load customers are responsible for the fixed costs associated with serving their demand rather than passing those costs on to families and businesses through higher monthly electricity bills.

The U.S. House of Representatives passed the House companion to the Ratepayer Protection Act, by a bipartisan vote of 417-3 on September 16, 2026.

title: Crapo, Wyden, Risch, Merkley Introduce Three-Year Reauthorization of Secure Rural Schools Program
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Mike Crapo (R-Idaho), Ron Wyden (D-Oregon), Jim Risch (R-Idaho) and Jeff Merkley (D-Oregon) introduced bipartisan legislation to reauthorize the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act program (SRS) for three years, providing continued support for rural schools and counties home to nontaxable federal land to fund education, road maintenance and other essential services.

“Counties across Idaho should not have to repeatedly face uncertainty about whether the federal government will uphold its responsibility to communities containing vast amounts of tax-exempt federal land,” said Crapo. “Without action, rural schools and counties will lose resources they rely on to maintain roads, support schools and provide basic services. This three-year reauthorization provides needed stability, but we must continue working toward a permanent solution that gives these communities the predictability they need to effectively plan and budget for the future.”

“Secure Rural Schools is a lifeline for rural Oregon,” Wyden said. “I’ll be working as hard as I can to get this bill across the finish line, but the well-being of rural America shouldn’t be dependent on Congress getting its act together to renew this funding every few years. It’s past time to get rural communities off the financial rollercoaster and deliver a permanent funding solution.”

“Secure Rural Schools funding is a commitment the federal government made to Idaho’s rural counties, helping them maintain roads, schools and other essential services,” said Risch. “As we work to restore the timber revenues that have long sustained these communities, Congress must honor that commitment and reauthorize SRS.”

“The SRS program provides crucial payments that are a lifeline for rural communities here in Oregon and across America—keeping schools open, maintaining roads, restoring watersheds, and providing funding for police officers and firefighters to keep families safe,” said Merkley. “A three-year extension of the program is critical to ensuring the federal government upholds its promise to our communities and that local governments can reliably access these important resources.”

"More than 700 counties across the country depend on the Secure Rural Schools program. Counties applaud Senators Crapo, Wyden, Risch and Merkley for leading this bipartisan legislation that will keep schools operating, roads and bridges maintained and public safety services funded in rural communities. SRS was reauthorized already once this Congress with overwhelming, bipartisan support. Now that it has lapsed again, Congress must act quickly to preserve SRS for rural counties across the country by passing this bipartisan legislation, so counties and communities have fiscal certainty." - Matthew Chase, Executive Director, National Association of Counties (NACo)

"Secure Rural Schools funding is vital to Idaho counties, supporting the maintenance of county roads and bridges, search and rescue services on federal lands, and K-12 education. As this critical funding nears expiration, we urge Congress to reauthorize the program for an additional three years to ensure counties can continue to meet these essential obligations. We thank Senator Crapo and his team for their continued efforts to raise awareness of this program's importance to Idaho communities." – Seth Grigg, Executive Director, Idaho Association of Counties

“Idaho’s rural schools shouldn’t be disadvantaged simply because so much of the land surrounding their communities is federally owned. Secure Rural Schools recognizes that reality and provides critical resources that help rural communities support their students. I applaud Senator Crapo’s commitment to providing Idaho’s rural communities greater stability through this essential funding while honoring the local control that allows communities to determine how best to serve their students.” – Debbie Critchfield, Idaho Superintendent of Public Instruction

Background

Congress created SRS in 2000 to provide financial assistance to counties with federally owned forestlands that are exempt from collecting local property taxes. Historically, rural counties received a share of receipts generated from timber harvests on federal lands. As timber harvests and associated revenues declined, SRS was established to provide predictable resources for counties and school districts that had historically relied on those receipts.

Crapo, Wyden, Risch and Merkley have worked together for years to maintain the program and provide greater certainty for rural communities. Most recently, the Senators led bipartisan legislation reauthorizing SRS through Fiscal Year 2026 and restoring lapsed payments for Fiscal Years 2024 and 2025. That legislation was signed into law in December 2025. Without further congressional action, the program will again expire after Fiscal Year 2026.

The U.S. Forest Service and U.S. Bureau of Land Management administer SRS payments. Funding is distributed using a formula that takes into account historic timber receipts, economic activity and other factors that vary by county. Depending on the payment title and eligible lands, SRS funding supports schools and roads, projects benefiting federal lands and specified county services such as emergency response and wildfire preparedness.

In Idaho, 34 of the state’s 44 counties received SRS payments in 2023. Under Idaho law, 30 percent of SRS funding is directed to schools, while the remaining 70 percent supports roads, bridges and other infrastructure projects.

title: Daines Bill to Support Floodplain Ecosystem Restoration Passes U.S. Senate, One Step Closer to Becoming Law
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Steve Daines today announced that his bill, the “Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act,” passed the U.S. Senate and now heads to the U.S. House of Representatives. The bill creates a new expedited pathway for ecosystem restoration projects that meet low-risk criteria, streamlining approval for important restoration work while still upholding flood safety standards.

“This is huge news for Montana. Critical ecosystem restoration projects across our state have been abandoned due to FEMA’s onerous and costly ‘No Rise’ rule. This commonsense, bipartisan bill will reduce unnecessary burdens on important conservation and restoration work, while continuing to keep our communities safe from flooding, and I’m glad to see it pass the Senate. Next step: the U.S. House!” said Daines.

Read the bill text HERE.

Background:

Under current Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) policy, any proposed development in a regulated floodway must prove that it will not increase the base flood elevation (BFE) of the area. This requirement is commonly referred to as the “No Rise” rule. While important for protecting communities from increased flood risks, it has had major unintended consequences on important environmental restoration in Montana and around the country. The “Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act” will create a new pathway only for ecosystem restoration projects that result in less than a one-foot increase in BFE and has no adverse impact to critical infrastructure.

Read the release from when Daines introduced the bill HERE.

title: Daines Talks U.S.-China Relations at Nixon Foundation’s Grand Strategy Summit
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Steve Daines today spoke at the Nixon Foundation’s 2026 Grand Strategy Summit, where he laid out a vision for the future of U.S.-China relations.

Watch Daines’ full remarks HERE.

Daines on his background working in China:

[My history with] China began back in 1991. I was a chemical engineer by degree, and I began work for Procter & Gamble in management…I spent seven years managing operations in the United States, and I got a call one day from our senior executive team that asked if we might be willing to go over to China 1991 to launch our businesses there, to take American brands, compete against the Chinese brands, and, of course, that massive consumer market. So my wife and I, we had 18-month-old little David at that point and little three-month-old Annie, we moved to Guangzhou in January of 1992. It was about a 400 billion dollar economy then… we got to see firsthand the incredible evolution, arguably an economic revolution, that’s occurred in China. We were the first non-state-owned enterprise allowed to recruit on the campuses of China…so I think part of my role here in Washington, I feel like Paul Revere, trying to just build awareness in terms of what’s at stake in the competition we face in China. It’s a world-class innovation ecosystem that is rapidly progressing.

Daines on the tech ecosystem in China vs the U.S.:

When I bring U.S. senators over to China, my goal is for them to understand the technology ecosystem. There’s a lot of goals you can have for a visit, but I want them to really understand that. Because there’s a lot of, I would call it, rear-view mirror thinking on China that’s primarily a supply chain issue…They can do a phase one clinical trial now in half the time that the United States does a phase one clinical trial to basically FDA standards. It’s not a perfect model, but more or less. So they’ve been able to get all the good coming from an FDA process for safety without the incredible regulatory burdens that we face sometimes that slow us down to getting drugs out to market faster. But number two, they do it at 20 percent of the cost…if you remember, Europe used to be the epicenter of pharma research and development and innovation. That shifted to the United States because of Europe’s overreaching regulation and government burden. It came to the United States. If you look at… clinical trial starts globally last year. The United States was at 45 percent a few years ago. It dropped down to 35 percent. China has come from nowhere to last year with 32 percent. So that’s one example. We talk a lot about AI, but I also keep an eye on the biotech and biopharma ecosystem. That’s very, very important. So if the… Innovation ecosystem supply chain shifts to China, which it’s doing right now as we speak. That becomes yet another, I think, concern for us in America as it relates to the next breakthrough, cancer drug, brain disease drug, Alzheimer’s, and so forth.

Daines on China’s AI adoption:

They’re [China is] doing a much better job of adoption, as I mentioned. At least Stanford’s ranking says number two. And you see it diffusing much more into their industry. At Zheijing university in Hangzhou, as I mentioned, it is an AI-driven curriculum now on the campus. They took us through. We met with the university officials. It’s pretty much free-form AI that the students use now to developing their learnings and by the way China graduates three times more PhDs every year than we do and five to ten times more engineers every year that we do and so not only is their ecosystem now becoming world class but it’s growing larger.

Daines on peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan:

What we did is we brokered a peace agreement between Azerbaijan and Armenia. And I was playing a shuttle diplomat between Baku and Yerevan, and I’ll tell you the secret sauce here was President Trump. They didn’t trust each other necessarily, but the United States had to step in the middle of that as the superpower and broker that deal. They came to Washington on August 8th last year and signed a peace agreement. I was up at UNGA last week, Wednesday, and we had the Central Asian and South Caucasus countries in one room. We had the foreign minister of Azerbaijan sitting next to the foreign minister of Armenia. And rather than talking about bloodshed and maybe thinking about a ceasefire and figuring out a way through this, you can see it in their body language and certainly their remarks, they’re both talking about their optimism right now economically as they’re opening up that corridor. As Brzezinski wrote in his book, The Grand Chessboard in the late 1990s, he said Central Asia is the wine bottle, the South Caucasus is the cork. We’ve popped the cork. And one of the best ways to understand that part of the world in a very simple… 10-second illustration. If you look at a, like, FlightAware, an app that shows where the air traffic is around the world, you can see the airplanes shoot the gap there between Georgia, Azerbaijan, Armenia, because they can’t overfly Russia, and they can’t overfly Iran, and then it explodes again. It spreads out again as they move through that little choke point. That choke point has just gotten opened up. And what that means is you’ve got incredible oil and gas reserves there certainly in Central Asia. Kazakhstan is the leading supply of uranium in the world. Turkmenistan is the fourth largest reserves of natural gas in the world. Severely underutilized. If we can start moving those resources, given what’s going on in the Strait of Hormuz at the moment, having an alternative kind of routing. that bypasses Russia and Iran and comes through the Caucasus, then you can go to the Black Sea, Turkey, or to Europe. This is absolutely a breakthrough moment for us. And so that whole Trans-Caspian opportunity is now opening up before our very eyes. And I credit Steve Witkoff and Areyh Lightstone and the President.

title: Senator Darline Graham Welcomes Grants for South Carolina Veterans Programs
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Darline Graham (R-South Carolina) today welcomed news that the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) awarded grants to South Carolina veterans’ programs that provide suicide prevention services. Through the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program, the Upstate Warrior Solution and the Lowcountry Veterans Home will receive $750,000 and $300,000 respectively.

“I am proud to announce that the VA has awarded grants to the Upstate Warrior Solution and the Lowcountry Veterans Home, organizations that provide meaningful and truly lifesaving care to veterans. These two organizations are worthy recipients with established ties to local communities and a proven commitment to serving South Carolina veterans,” said Senator Darline Graham.

“A crucial aspect of the Fox Grant Program is reaching veterans at risk of suicide who may not yet be receiving clinical care through the VA. Most of the veterans we lose to suicide are not receiving VA care in the year before their death. That is why reaching at-risk veterans through trusted community organizations is urgent. I welcome these grants and will always fight to ensure that our veterans have access to the care, support, and resources they need and deserve,” concluded Senator Darline Graham.

Background on the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program:

Community-based grant program aimed at reducing veteran suicide by expanding prevention efforts beyond the clinical setting, serving eligible veterans where they live, and connecting them with both VA and non-VA services

Grants are awarded to organizations that provide suicide prevention services for eligible veterans at risk of suicide

Qualifying organizations complete outreach, offer mental health screening, provide educational materials on suicide risk and prevention, clinical services for crisis intervention, case management, peer and family support services, and assistance in obtaining VA benefits

title: Senator Graham: Democrats Failed to Protect South Carolinians And Americans from Rising Energy Costs Borne by Data Centers
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Darline Graham (R-South Carolina) today said Senate Democrats should be blamed for any citizen who faces rising energy costs because of data center construction.

A majority of Senate Democrats voted to prevent the legislation from moving forward, even though it passed the U.S. House of Representatives in an overwhelming bipartisan 417-3 vote.

Graham voted to advance legislation she cosponsored, the Ratepayer Protection Act (S. 5028), which ensures hard working Americans are not left paying for the energy needs of data centers.

Senator Darline Graham said, “I am very disappointed in Senate Democrats for blocking this important legislation. We had a chance to protect hardworking families and small businesses from rising energy costs caused by data centers. But Senate Democrats, instead of passing this overwhelmingly bipartisan legislation, said ‘No.’

“In order to protect our national security, it’s imperative we are able to compete with China, but that cost should not be passed on to consumers. It’s also imperative that local communities are actively involved in any decision whether to bring data centers to their community because they know what’s best.”

“Data centers should have to pay for any new energy infrastructure they need and that’s the standard set forth by the Ratepayer Protection Act.”

“I find it ridiculous that Democrats won’t work with Republicans to pass this extremely reasonable proposal.”

Background on the Ratepayer Protection Act:

The House passed the bill 417–3 on September 16, 2026.

It directs state utility commissions to consider new standards for data centers drawing more than 100 megawatts of power.

100 megawatts of power are equivalent to roughly 100,000 homes

These standards would protect ratepayers from paying the costs of new power infrastructure needed to serve data centers.

Implementation is left up to the states and utility commissions.

title: Duckworth, Durbin, Budzinski Call for Pause on 183rd Wing Deactivation, Push for Replacement Mission
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – As the Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) and the House Armed Services Committee (HASC) prepare to negotiate the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), along with U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) and U.S. Representative Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13), today urged SASC and HASC leadership to add language into the final bill to temporarily halt any plans to deactivate the 183rd Wing’s Central Repair Facility (CRF) in Springfield, Illinois. In the letter, the new language would require that the deactivation not occur until the Air Force and National Guard Bureau identify a replacement mission to provide Illinois servicemembers and their families with a clear path forward.

The lawmakers wrote: “The addition [to the bill] we seek would place a temporary halt on closing or deactivating any Air Force Central Repair Facility (CRF) until September 30, 2028, unless the Air Force assigns a deployable replacement mission, and require the Secretary of the Air Force to submit a report within 90 days detailing fighter engine repair demands and a comprehensive sustainment plan for the fighter fleet, including the technician workforce needed to maintain required technical skillsets.”

“We are concerned a hasty deactivation of the Central Repair Facility (CRF) mission could risk adequate sustainment of our fighter fleet.” the lawmakers continued. “Centralized repair capacity provides critical maintenance depth by concentrating the specialized equipment, technical expertise and trained personnel that are necessary to return engines and components to service. This capacity is especially important as the Air Force sustains forward fighter forces in Europe and the Indo-Pacific, supports ongoing operations in the Middle East and transitions to platforms such as the F-15EX and F-35A.”

At a time when U.S. forces are facing sustained operational demands in the illegal Iran War and across the globe, the lawmakers underscored how the importance of preserving the skilled workforce and repair capacity needed to keep fighter aircraft ready is critical to ensuring our Airmen can do their jobs and fly safely.

The 183rd Wing’s specialized repair workforce plays a critical role in maintaining the Air Force’s fighter fleet and is the only single dedicated repair facility for the F-15EX in the Joint Force. The lawmakers underscored how preserving that capability is in the best interest of both our national defense and the 115 highly trained servicemembers and their families in Illinois who rely on this mission.

Following the announcement that the CRF mission at the 183rd Wing would be deactivated, Duckworth, Durbin and Budzinski spoke with Illinois Adjutant General Major General Rodney Boyd and advocated for a suitable replacement mission. Earlier this month, the lawmakers also sent a letter to Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink and National Guard Bureau Director General Steven Nordhaus, calling for them to establish a new Air Operations Group at the 183rd Wing and delay the CRF’s deactivation to allow adequate time for impacted airmen and women to be retrained for a new replacement mission or to retire if eligible.

Full text of today’s letter is available on Senator Duckworth’s website and below:

Dear Chairman Wicker, Ranking Member Reed, Chairman Rogers and Ranking Member Smith:

As you prepare to conference the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), we respectfully urge you to expand existing language in Section 131 of the Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) NDAA and include the updated language in the conferenced version of the bill. The addition we seek would place a temporary halt on closing or deactivating any Air Force Central Repair Facility (CRF) until September 30, 2028, unless the Air Force assigns a deployable replacement mission, and require the Secretary of the Air Force to submit a report within 90 days detailing fighter engine repair demands, an assessment of evolving repair needs, readiness impacts of deactivation and a comprehensive sustainment plan for the fighter fleet—including an inventory of all airframe and component repair facilities and the technician workforce needed to maintain required technical skillsets.

We believe this addition would complement the intent of the provision, as we are concerned a hasty deactivation of the CRF mission could risk adequate sustainment of our fighter fleet, especially if Congress mandates an updated inventory of fighters, as required in the current iteration of Section 131. Centralized repair capacity provides critical maintenance depth by concentrating the specialized equipment, technical expertise and trained personnel that are necessary to return engines and components to service. This capacity is especially important as the Air Force sustains forward fighter forces in Europe and the Indo-Pacific, supports ongoing operations in the Middle East and transitions to platforms such as the F-15EX and F-35A. Preserving sufficient repair capacity and a skilled maintenance workforce is therefore essential to sustaining geographically dispersed operations without degrading readiness elsewhere.

We are also specifically concerned about the troubling decision to deactivate, without a suitable replacement mission, the CRF mission at the 183rd Wing in Springfield, Illinois. Since 2012, the 183rd Wing has capably provided fighter jet engine maintenance for U.S. Armed Forces aircraft, including the U-2, F-16, A-10 and F-15EX. The 183rd’s CRF remains the only mission of its kind within the Joint Force and is the single dedicated repair facility for the F-15EX aircraft fleet. A deferred deactivation would mitigate the impact on the lives of our Illinois servicemembers and their families and make sure the Air Force has a plan for how to maintain the repair capability of our fighter fleet before sunsetting this critical capability. We appreciate your consideration of this language intended to safeguard critical maintenance capability and capacity organic to our Air Force and ensure adequate sustainment of the fighter fleet.

Sincerely,

-30-

title: WATCH: At HSGAC Subcommittee Hearing, Gallego Warns of Dangers Posed by AI, Especially as More Models Go Rogue
text:
WASHINGTON – Yesterday, during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee (HSGAC) Subcommittee on Disaster Management, District of Columbia, and Census hearing, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) questioned AI experts on the threats posed by the rapidly developing technology and the industry’s failure to act as more of its models are going rogue.

At the hearing, “Rogue AI: Securing the Homeland Against AI Agent Attacks,” Senator Gallego sounded the alarm about the potential dangers of AI systems developing their own language that humans cannot comprehend, the lack of requirements for AI companies to report when their models go rogue, and the absence of a universal “kill switch” capable of shutting down AI models. He also raised questions about who should be held accountable when an AI system acts in an illegal manner.

Watch Senator Gallego’s questioning HERE and read excerpts below:

Senator Gallego began by raising concerns about how quickly advanced AI models could begin communicating in ways humans cannot understand or monitor. Apollo Research CEO, Marius Hobbhahn, warned that models could reach that point in as little as 12 months and acknowledged that researchers do not yet have a reliable solution for monitoring AI systems once their reasoning becomes incomprehensible to humans.

“How far away are [AI models] from creating language where [we] cannot understand what they’re doing?” asked Senator Gallego.

“Minus twelve months,” said Hobbhahn. “Last year, we studied the chain of thought of one OpenAI model in collaboration with OpenAI, and what we found was that the model was already using language that is not English and not perfectly understandable by humans.”

“When we get to that point in time, how can we detect, observe, block, or anything like that?” Senator Gallego continued. “How does that work? How do we legislate to do anything at that point?

Hobbhahn responded: “From a scientific perspective, it is unclear how to do this. And we do not have a solution as of yet. There are different hypotheses of what you could do. There is interpretability, but it does not work sufficiently well yet. You could try to train additional models to understand the language that the humans don’t understand, but obviously that seems like a very brittle solution.”

Gallego also pushed back on arguments that the United States must avoid guardrails on AI in order to compete with China, noting that the Chinese government has historically imposed significant controls on technology and information.

“The reason I bring this whole China hypothesis—a country that has severely restricted the internet, social media—is all of a sudden going to allow AI rogue agents to go crazy in their very controlled economic environment, social environment, and we have to therefore allow ours to go as crazy as them? It just doesn’t make sense,” said Senator Gallego. “The Chinese Communist Party has been consistently controlling technology to try to shape their society. They’re never going to allow this to go crazy.”

Senator Gallego continued: “ Once these agents start speaking their language, they will not be detectable in China or America. Is there a sandbox that says, ‘Please attack the United States, but do not attack any Chinese interests’? […] Is there a sandbox that can hold? No.

“That should scare the shit out of people.”

Gallego then questioned witnesses about whether AI companies are currently required to alert the federal government when their frontier models are hacked or used by adversaries.

Georgetown University Professor of Law Paul Ohm responded: “Not under any requirement I can think of.”

Gallego pointed to the use of an AI model by the Houthis to assist in targeting U.S. military systems as an example of the potential national security consequences.

“There was a Claude AI model being used by the Houthis to figure out how to recalibrate their missile position and be able to strike our U.S. systems,” said Senator Gallego. “The only reason it was caught and reported to us was because Claude caught it and they saw the accounts using it.”

If it were an open-source AI, “there is no requirement by law for them to call the DOD and say, ‘By the way, they are using this to target your destroyers,’ correct?”Senator Gallego questioned.

Ohm responded: “Again, we talked about transparency measures in some of these systems that might help you with Houthi rebels—

“If you don’t tell us someone is using your tech to kill us, we will hold you responsible,” Sen. Gallego stated.

Gallego also pressed witnesses on whether developers have a reliable “kill switch” capable of stopping a dangerous AI system if it begins operating across multiple data centers. Hobbhahn said there are currently no technical measures that could guarantee such a shutdown.

“As far as I know, there are no technical measures that would guarantee something like a kill switch,” said Hobbhahn.“Because of the complexity of these AI models, there are many data centers involved and so on. Currently, we can’t guarantee that.”

Hobbhahn further acknowledged that an AI system could potentially deploy copies of itself to other data centers, meaning shutting down its original location would not necessarily stop it.

“It would just keep moving?” asked Senator Gallego.

“The AI would keep moving,” Hobbhahn responded.

Finally, Gallego questioned whether existing civil and criminal liability laws are sufficient to hold AI companies accountable when their systems cause harm, arguing that liability could provide a powerful incentive for companies to adopt stronger safeguards.

“Sometimes when the government doesn’t work, torts work. Torts, sometimes, are a way better way to regulate private industry than having individual regulations,” said Senator Gallego.

“Right now, have we created the environment where torts can be the incentives for them to act correctly, in the sense of making sure the language allows a certain level of liability?” Senator Gallego asked. “And number two, on the criminal side, do we need to change the criminal law with intent to make sure that these companies are held responsible?”

Ohm responded that while the tort system alone would not be sufficient, “it is a great place to start,” noting that liability can establish standards of care that influence how companies behave.

title: Gillibrand Slams Trump’s Costly $1.8 Billion Vanity Projects, Misplaced Priorities

title: Grassley, Hassan Take Action to Improve Access to Cancer Screenings
text:
Click HERE for video of Grassley’s remarks from the Senate floor.

Click HERE for separate audio of Grassley discussing the legislation.

BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Senate Finance Committee members Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.) introduced the Standardizing Cancer Recommendations for Earlier Evaluation and Navigation of Screenings (SCREENS) Act to make cancer screening recommendations more accessible, transparent and user friendly for patients and health care providers.

Cancer is the second leading cause of death in the United States, and Iowa has the second-highest cancer incidence rate in the nation. Cancer screenings can increase the chance for earlier treatment and reduce mortality, but screening recommendations are often complex, fragmented and difficult to interpret and navigate.

The bipartisan SCREENS Act would simplify and improve the process by establishing a national data and technology framework for cancer screening recommendations, to make these recommendations more accessible, interoperable and effective for providers and patients.

“Detecting cancer early can save lives. I know that based on the personal experience of my wife, Barbara, a nearly 40-year breast cancer survivor. Unfortunately, patients and providers are navigating a complex and confusing maze just to keep up with cancer screening recommendations. By making these recommendations more accessible through technology, our SCREENS Act would strengthen cancer care and help save lives. For my home state, this bill would proactively support Iowans by helping providers identify patients who could be overdue for a screening,” Grassley said.

“Cancer screenings can identify cancers during the early stages when they are easiest to treat, but patients often do not know when they are due for potentially life-saving screenings,” Hassan said. “This bipartisan bill will help make sure that patients and doctors are informed about federal cancer screening recommendations so that they can catch cancer earlier and get people the treatment that they need. I’m glad to introduce this bill, and I will continue working across the aisle to strengthen preventative care for Granite Staters.”

Click HERE for video of Grassley discussing the legislation from the Senate floor.

Click HERE for separate audio of Grassley speaking about the bill.

Click HERE for text of the legislation and click HERE for a section-by-section.

Background:

In 2022, the Presidential Cancer Panel recommended the federal government develop a digitally accessible version of the cancer screening and risk assessment guidelines. The SCREENS Act carries out this recommendation and builds on Grassley’s work to improve access to breast cancer screenings, strengthen breast and cervical cancer treatment under Medicaid, and support cancer research.

Under the legislation, the national data and technology framework would be publicly available in machine-readable format for use by health information technologies, interoperability tools and patient-facing applications. The legislation would also help providers identify which patients are at risk and overdue for screenings.

title: Grassley Presents Congressional Adoption Award to Iowa Nonprofit, My G.E.A.R. Outreach
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa), co-founder and co-chair of the Senate Caucus on Foster Youth, presented My G.E.A.R. Outreach with the Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute’s (CCAI) “Angels in Adoption” award.

My G.E.A.R. Outreach provides children with welcome boxes and overnight bags to help them transition as they enter foster care. The program serves Iowa youth in Clinton, Jackson, Scott, Dubuque, Fayette, Winneshiek, Howard, Buchanan, Delaware, Allamakee and Clayton counties.

“Every child deserves a welcoming and loving home. That’s why I appreciate My G.E.A.R. Outreach’s work to provide foster youth some sense of comfort and certainty as they face a tough transition. My G.E.A.R. Outreach’s generosity should inspire us all, as they work to improve conditions for foster youth across Iowa and Illinois. I’m proud to have nominated them for this year’s award,” Grassley said.

Founder Liz Estilow accepts the Angels in Adoption award from Senator Grassley.

Download more photos HERE.

Background:

The Angels in Adoption Program annually recognizes outstanding groups and individuals for their contributions to adoption, foster care and child welfare. CCAI invites “Angel” honorees to Washington to celebrate their efforts, participate in advocacy training and share their experiences with congressional representatives. Grassley was named a member of the Advisory Council of the CCAI in 2015 and is a longtime advocate for adoptive and foster parents and children.

title: Hagerty Formally Calls for Disbarment of Jack Smith
text:
Jack Smith, a Biden DOJ prosecutor, is accused of withholding critical information from a federal court in violation of Tennessee ethics rules

WASHINGTON—On Wednesday, United States Senator Bill Hagerty (R-TN) submitted a formal complaint to the Tennessee Supreme Court’s Board of Professional Responsibility, calling for the disbarment of former special counsel Jack Smith.

The complaint centers on Smith’s unconstitutional acquisition of phone records associated with Hagerty and other members of Congress as part of the Arctic Frost investigation. Hagerty alleges that Smith withheld critical information from a federal court in violation of the ethics rules applicable to Tennessee lawyers, which includes Smith. Because Smith withheld that information, the court issued a nondisclosure order preventing Hagerty and his colleagues from challenging Smith’s unconstitutional collection of their records.

The complaint was filed following Smith’s appearance before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday, which revealed that Smith obtained confidential donor information of thousands of Americans, including many Tennesseans, and that Smith’s team violated filter protocols put in place to comply with the Constitution.

“Jack Smith’s lack of candor before a federal tribunal directly resulted in injury to the United States Congress,” said Hagerty. “The Board should investigate and pursue the most serious remedy possible—disbarment—in light of the gravity of Smith’s intentional conduct.”
