title: ICYMI: Hawley Convenes First Senate Hearing on Rogue AI Attacks
text:
Hearing expands Hawley subcommittee investigation into OpenAI and hacking risks

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Josh Hawley chaired a Senate Homeland Security Subcommittee on Disaster Management hearing that focused on the growing number of rogue AI cyberattacks on critical infrastructure. Senator Hawley called for AI companies and developers to be held liable for these attacks. The hearing is an expansion of Senator Hawley’s investigation into OpenAI, the unprecedented hack of Hugging Face by OpenAI’s rogue AI agents, and its cybersecurity implications.

Senator Hawley invited Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, to testify in yesterday’s hearing. He failed to response to the invitation.

Chairman Hawley opened the hearing, “Every day you turn on the television, it seems like AI is doing something else bad: setting up surveillance camera networks nationwide, data centers in all of our states, and hacking, hacking, hacking. The reports of cyber attacks just continue to metastasize … We’ve got the cyber attacks now on the United States government, on the Commerce Department, the Education Department, the Securities and Exchange Commission. We’ve got the cyber attacks on the Australian government, on their public health apparatus. We have numerous reports of private companies being hacked by AI agents. Of course, the Hugging Face incident and attack, which we’re going to discuss today in some detail.”

Hawley continued, “I think it’s time to have a conversation about who bears responsibility … If it’s not trying to say to these AI companies who are creating these frontier models, however fancy and complicated they are, at the end of the day, they’re a product, and if you make that product in a reckless kind of way, and that product causes these AI agents cause significant harm and damage … then it’s the people who made it who should be responsible. I think it’s time to talk about that, and it’s time to talk about what we’re going to do to hold the companies, the product makers, accountable.”

“I hope that what will come from this is a rational conversation about what we need to do together now, as Americans, to make sure that we protect our rights, that we protect our economy, that we protect our health care, that we protect our critical infrastructure, but most of all, we protect the values that we hold dearest together as Americans,” he asserted.

Chairman Hawley asked Chris Painter, President of Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR), “Just thinking about this Hugging Face hack that we’ve already alluded to multiple times here. Your company, your organization, METR, audited that hack. Can you start by telling us, just in simple terms, what exactly happened there? I mean, what was the hack?”

Painter responded, “In this incident … you had 10,000 agents that were tested on a benchmark called ExploitGym, which is a cybersecurity vulnerability kind of benchmark, where they had to discover or use cyber vulnerabilities. And some of the agents had tasks that they couldn’t complete, and so they worked on a universal cheat for all of their tasks in the first four hours. They then, over multiple days, embarked on a research program to try and hide the fact that they cheated. And an offshoot of that research program was hacking Hugging Face to get information about their tasks.”

“In this particular incident, you had more than 1,200 OpenAI agents that broke out of their testing environment, began to collaborate, exchanged over 70,000 messages and files with each other over a period of how long?” Hawley questioned.

Painter answered, “This is over a period of about five to six days.”

The chairman continued, “Why is this so significant? We know that they coordinated in this fashion. You you did the audit. Tell us a little bit about what your audit revealed … Why should we be paying attention to this?”

“What’s remarkable about this case, is the extent and persistence of the effort that the agents went to to hide the fact that they cheated on their tasks and the kind of breadth of agents involved … They attempted to kind of falsify tool calls so that in their action transcripts you wouldn’t be able to see what tools they called. They also engaged in this kind of behavior of having individual agents sacrifice their work online, sacrifice their individual tasks to get information for the rest of the message board,” Mr. Painter stated.

Senator Hawley said to Daniel Kokotajlo, Executive Director of the AI Futures Project, “Could you just explain to us why the incentives of the industries they are currently misaligned? The incentives push the frontier labs to continue at breakneck speed the development of these kind of AI agents that are prone to this misalignment that we’ve just been talking about. That there’s huge incentives to keep pushing, pushing, pushing. Help us understand. Help us to understand why that’s the case.”

Kokotajlo responded, “Short answer is that there’s a lot of money. If a company tries to go slow and understand better how their AIs work and improve their training environments, for example, so that they don’t have so many broken tasks in the training environments, well, that all takes time, and that means that the launch of their next model might be delayed, and then they might fall behind other companies.”

Hawley turned back to Dr. Paul Ohm, a Georgetown Law Professor, “Who right now under our laws … is responsible the Hugging Face attack? You know who could be held responsible for that under our existing statutes and regulatory framework?”

Ohm answered, “Developers and deployers may be negligent … “

Hawley continued his questioning, “If you cause damage, you got to make it right. If you cause somebody harm, you’ve got to make it whole. Right now, as you said earlier, Professor, under our law, because of the unique position of these AI agents, it’s difficult to know exactly how the doctrine would would deal with them …Isn’t this a good place to begin? What we’ve been discussing here, let’s impose both civil and criminal liability, but let’s make sure that we can actually open courthouse doors so people can say, ‘Listen, OpenAI, if your agents hack Hugging Face or crash a hospital system, and we can show that you trained them recklessly or you develop them recklessly, you’re going to be liable?'”

Dr. Ohm said, “Absolutely … I’m with you that you know finding the vehicle to make sure developers and employers, and it’s key that we have both of them, are held to account for the harms that happen from their uses.”

“If we told them, listen, if your AIs do bad stuff and harm people, and you’ve been reckless in it, you’re going to be responsible. Don’t you think that that would reshape their incentives a little bit?” Chairman Hawley asked Kokotajlo.

“Yes, I completely agree. Although I must say, I don’t think it would go far enough. I do think that we should hold them liable for the damages that are caused, but but I think if that’s all we do, then they’re going to continue to take reckless gambles, and eventually they’ll be taking a gamble that’s big enough that we start the protection,” Kokotajlo affirmed.

“It’s time these companies assume some personal responsibility. It’s time that we reaffirm that together. We’ve got to make some choices now together as Americans, all together, for this technology in order to make sure that the technology works for us and not the other way around. And those are some very big choices to make. They have very serious moral ramifications, and it’s time that we made them as a society. But I will go so far as to say, I sort of suspect. I think most Americans actually agree. I don’t think there’s a lot of disagreement on this issue. I think the American people are saying, protect our rights, give us a voice, give power back to us, and we do that by imposing responsibility on these companies, we should start with that today,” Senator Hawley concluded.

title: REMARKS: Heinrich Introduces the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act with Capito, Lee, and Whitehouse Heinrich Introduces the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act with Capito, Lee, and Whitehouse
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, introduced the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 to reform the federal environmental review and permitting process. This groundbreaking agreement will deliver cheaper energy, more jobs, and responsible growth across the United States.

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Energy and Natural Resources Committee, speaks at a press conference announcing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, September 30, 2026.

“Today I wore a pin that was my dad’s 60-year IBEW pin, and it represents 60 years of him working for a local utility company to keep the lights on. Today in my home state of New Mexico there is a switchyard named after my dad, Pete Heinrich, and that switchyard is connected to the SunZia transmission line,” said Heinrich. “That transmission line, which is 550 miles long and carries the electrons from three and a half gigawatts of clean wind generation, took 17 years to permit and build. That’s why I’m here today, because we need to be able to build big things in this country again.”

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act provides certainty that permitted energy and infrastructure projects will retain their permits absent extraordinary circumstances, violations of law, or court order, as well as targeted reforms for various energy projects. This legislation reflects input from members of Congress on both sides of the aisle and from a diverse group of stakeholders. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act also forces data centers to pay their fair share by requiring them to pay for all of their associated transmission costs.

The bill text is available here.

Watch the full video of Heinrich’s remarks here.

A transcript of Heinrich’s remarks as delivered is below:

Thank you.

I want to start, too, just by thanking my colleagues.

This was a pretty remarkable effort, and everyone really did work in good faith to achieve this result.

I wore a pin today.

It’s not my Senate pin.

It’s a pin that I like to wear, that was my dad’s 60-year IBEW pin, and it represents 60 years of him working for a local utility company to keep the lights on.

Today in my home state of New Mexico there is a switchyard named after my dad, Pete Heinrich, and that switchyard is connected to the SunZia transmission line.

That transmission line, which is 550 miles long and carries the electrons from three and a half gigawatts of clean wind generation, took 17 years to permit and build.

That’s why I’m here today, because I was part of that process that should have taken probably five years to figure out how to get to yes or how to get to no a whole lot faster than that.

We need to be able to build big things in this country again, and if we don’t, experts like the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas have estimated that we will see 20 to 30 percent increases in the cost of electricity in the near term.

Not a decade from now, but a couple of years from now.

And so, with the incredible demand that is on our grid right now, we came together to find ways to do the things that we’ve done historically, but do the processes in parallel. Don’t do them one after the other after the other, and keep the process open for years and years at a time.

This process will mean that we develop responsibly.

It’ll mean more jobs.

It’ll mean cheaper energy.

It’ll mean that we actually require big load centers, whether that’s a factory or a data center, to not pass those costs on to the American consumer: By statute, not a suggestion, but an actual law.

This is an opportunity for us to unleash American innovation and our incredible skilled labor force to build big things again.

And I have to say, I wasn’t sure at the beginning if we could all get there, and it’s because this group of people and the amazing staffs of the Energy and Natural Resources Committee and the Environment and Public Works Committee kept at it in good faith – through thick and thin – that we have arrived at this product.

I want to thank everyone who contributed to that.

title: Hickenlooper, Tillis, Rosen, Sheehy, Cramer, Lee, Fulcher Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Establish National Critical Minerals Council, Federal Strategy on Critical Minerals
text:
U.S. is 100% reliant on imports for 16 critical minerals

WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper, Thom Tillis, Jacky Rosen, Tim Sheehy, and Kevin Cramer, along with Representatives Susie Lee and Russ Fulcher, introduced the bipartisan National Critical Minerals Council Act, which would establish a National Critical Minerals Council to develop and implement a national strategy on critical minerals and build reliable supply chains at home and abroad.

Critical minerals power our modern way of life, including vehicles, smartphones, defense systems, medical equipment, AI and clean energy. Yet, China dominates the market, processing or refining about 70% of the world’s critical minerals. The U.S. is fully reliant on imports for 16 critical minerals. Given the scale of the challenge, our federal response remains fragmented, with more than 15 federal agencies and departments working on critical minerals issues. Absent a unified effort, the U.S. risks falling behind in securing the minerals essential to our competitiveness and leadership in energy security and national defense.

“China doesn’t need to fire a shot. It just needs to stop a shipment,” said Hickenlooper. “We need a national strategy on critical minerals now. Otherwise, Beijing decides who gets the supply — and who doesn’t.”

“The United States can no longer afford to take a piecemeal approach to address our critical minerals needs,” said Tillis. “I am proud to reintroduce this bipartisan legislation to establish a comprehensive and unified strategy to secure the minerals that are essential to our national security and economic stability.”

“As the world races to acquire and leverage the critical minerals that power the modern economy, the United States needs an efficient and effective plan to secure these important resources,” said Rosen. “I am proud to help introduce this bipartisan bill to ensure the United States has the infrastructure it needs to secure critical minerals and remain at the forefront of modern development.”

“It’s common sense: we cannot continue to rely on adversaries like China, which dominates the world’s critical minerals processing, for our critical mineral needs because it puts America’s national security at risk and threatens our competitive edge,” said Sheehy. “This crucial legislation reduces our dependence on others and bolsters America’s critical mineral supply chains by centralizing federal coordination, strategy, and research, making our nation more secure and self-reliant. I’m proud to cosponsor this legislation as we work to ensure America’s needs can be securely met.”

“We cannot afford to become more dependent on other countries for the critical minerals needed to power our economy and strengthen our national security,” said Cramer. “Our bill establishes a National Critical Minerals Council to unite all federal investment, research, and development on critical minerals under a single national strategy. The demand for critical minerals is growing every single day, and we need to seize every opportunity to jumpstart domestic production.”

“Critical minerals are used in everything from our phones to solar panels and aircraft used by the Department of Defense. It’s essential we develop our domestic critical mineral supply chains and reduce our dependence on foreign countries for rare earths,” said Lee. “That’s why I’m proud to join my colleagues in introducing the bipartisan, bicameral National Critical Minerals Council Act. This commonsense legislation will ensure the United States continues to grow our domestic supply of critical minerals, strengthening our national security and energy grid.”

“For far too long, our country has depended on foreign adversaries for vital minerals that support many of our defense capabilities and energy systems. This legislation will establish important structures for mineral development and help build critical partnerships,” said Fulcher. “I am proud to co-lead the National Critical Minerals Council Act with my colleague, Congresswoman Lee. By securing the critical minerals we have here at home today, we can build stronger energy security for tomorrow.”

The Secretary of the Interior, the National Security Adviser, and the Director of the National Economic Council would co-chair the council. They would appoint a Chief Minerals Adviser to oversee the Council’s operations and collaborate with experts from universities, industry, national labs, governments, Tribes, non-profits, and civil society.

Specifically, the council would:

Develop a national critical minerals strategy to reduce our reliance on foreign adversaries.

Work with allied nations and private entities to make the U.S. the partner of choice on critical minerals projects.

Track foreign investments in global critical mineral projects.

Coordinate education and workforce development.

Oversee the responsible development of domestic resources.

Hickenlooper has introduced several bills that boost the supply of critical minerals:

Critical Materials Future Act, which would establish a pilot program for the Department of Energy to financially support domestic critical material processing projects.

Unearth Innovation Act, which would create a Mining and Mineral Innovation Program within the Department of Energy to drive the responsible production of domestic critical minerals, with a focus on minimizing the environmental impact of mining.

Critical Minerals Security Act, which would direct the Department of the Interior to evaluate the global supply and ownership of critical minerals and make it easier for the U.S. to establish stable supply chains with international allies

title: Hoeven: Grid Power Act Advances Out of Energy Committee
text:
WASHINGTON – Senator John Hoeven issued the following statement after joining his fellow Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee (ENR) members in approving the Guaranteeing Reliability through the Interconnection of Dispatchable (GRID) Power Act, legislation he introduced to help remove delays in the development of new baseload power generation projects that would improve the reliability of the electrical grid.

Hoeven introduced the legislation with Senator Todd Young (R-Ind.) to address lengthy delays in the interconnection queue that can prevent new dispatchable power generation from coming online. Specifically, the bill would:

Following rulemaking from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), authorize regional grid operators to give priority consideration for baseload generation projects seeking an interconnection agreement.

The interconnection queue is where proposed projects wait before grid operators begin conducting their feasibility and system impact studies.

As of 2023, the median wait time was five years for an interconnection agreement, significantly delaying the construction of critical projects.

FERC would be required to initiate rulemaking to establish this process within 90 days of the bill’s enactment and finalize the rule within 180 days.

Establish a timeline of 60 days for FERC to act on baseload generation projects given priority consideration by grid operators.

Timely approval of projects would help address the gap in reliable power generation created by Biden administration rules like the Clean Power Plan 2.0, which accelerated the retirement of American baseload power plants.

“We need the ability to bring new baseload power online to meet growing electricity demand and ensure the reliability of our grid,” said Hoeven. “Our GRID Power Act helps cut through lengthy delays in the interconnection process so we can build the reliable dispatchable power generation our nation needs. With today’s committee approval, we are one step closer to advancing this importance legislation through the Senate.”

title: Senate passes Husted-backed bill to protect Great Lakes
text:
“We must remain vigilant against invasive species and continue protecting our lakes so they can support Ohio and America for generations to come.”

WASHINGTON – The Senate this week passed Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and Sen. Gary Peters’ (D-Mich.) Great Lakes Restoration Initiative Act. This bill would reauthorize federal funding for critical projects like habitat restoration, cleaning up toxic sediments and pollution and preventing the spread of invasive species to protect and maintain the Great Lakes.

The Senate passed the bill without objection.

“The Great Lakes are an environmental and economic asset for the United States. They support thousands of jobs and contribute billions of dollars to Ohio’s regional economy. We must remain vigilant against invasive species and continue protecting our lakes so they can support Ohio and America for generations to come. I’m encouraged to see our bill pass the Senate, and I hope the House will act as soon as possible,” said Husted.

Since 2010, the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative has provided more than $4.1 billion to fund 8,000 projects throughout the Great Lakes region. The initiative has focused on stopping the spread of invasive carp and other invasive species, restoring the Great Lakes coastline and preventing future contamination.

Husted is the only member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee representing a Great Lakes state. He has led efforts to advance the legislation in the Senate.

The legislation builds on Husted’s record of protecting the Great Lakes. In 2025, his Great Lakes Fishery Reauthorization Act became law, reauthorizing the Great Lakes Fishery Commission’s research activities and providing the U.S. Geological Survey’s Great Lakes Science Center with dedicated funding to conduct critical research supporting the region’s multi-billion-dollar fishing industry.

View Husted’s remarks on the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative here.

title: Kaine & Dingell Introduce Legislation to Prevent Campus Sexual Assault and Support Student Survivors
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Senator Tim Kaine, a member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, and U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-6) introduced the Support for Universities and Colleges to Champion the Educational Success of Survivors (SUCCESS) Act and the Survivor Outreach and Support on Campus Act—bicameral legislation to prevent campus sexual assault and improve support for student survivors. The SUCCESS Act, which is cosponsored by U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ), Dick Durbin (D-IL), and John Fetterman (D-PA) would help improve academic outcomes for student survivors and ensure colleges and universities have the resources to support them. The Survivor Outreach and Support on Campus Act, or S.O.S. Campus Act, would require every college and university that receives federal funding to have an independent advocate dedicated to campus sexual assault prevention and response. This legislation is also cosponsored by Senators Booker and Fetterman.

“Every student deserves to live and learn in a healthy and safe environment. We must do everything we can to prevent sexual assault on college campuses and provide comprehensive support to survivors,” said Kaine. “I’m proud to introduce these bills to help ensure survivors can access medical care, counseling, and the academic support they need to heal and continue pursuing their educational and professional goals.”

“Every student deserves to feel safe on their college campus and to know that if they experience sexual violence, they will be supported and taken seriously. The urgency to act has been put into sharp relief as we learn more about the horrific allegations coming out of Cornell,” said Dingell. “These bills will give colleges and universities more tools to prevent sexual violence, support survivors, and help ensure students can continue their education in a safe and supportive environment. No student should ever have to choose between their safety and their education.”

“Colleges have a responsibility to help survivors of sexual violence cope with the trauma of an assault. Yet colleges expect survivors to seek out medical and mental health services on their own, stay on track academically, and feel safe in the same environment where the violence occurred,” said Booker. “It’s unfair to make survivors carry this weight. Every institution of higher education should provide the support survivors need.”

“Survivors of sexual assault deserve to know that their college campuses stand with them. No student should have to choose between their education and getting the support they need after experiencing sexual assault,” said Durbin. “The SUCCESS Act ensures that students have access to the resources and support networks they need to continue their education and achieve their goals.”

“What kind of message does it send to survivors of sexual violence on our campuses if we hear their stories and don’t do anything to help prevent it from happening again? I can’t imagine that kind of unimaginable pain,” said Fetterman. “Today, my colleagues and I are doing something about it. These bills will not only help in the prevention of this violence, but it will help survivors with the resources they need and to continue pursuing their dreams.”

Sexual violence can impact student survivors physically, psychologically, emotionally, and academically. Survivors may face difficulty learning and retaining information, lower grade point averages, and a greater risk of dropping out of school. College and university students deserve the ability to learn without fear of sexual violence, and higher education institutions have an obligation to do everything they can to provide a safe learning environment for their students. The legislation would help colleges and universities provide comprehensive guidance, resources, and support for survivors to make campuses a safer place to learn.

The S.O.S. Campus Act would require campuses to have an independent advocate to conduct public information campaigns on sexual assault prevention and ensure that survivors of sexual assault have access to:

Emergency and follow-up medical care,

Guidance on reporting assaults to law enforcement

Medical forensic or evidentiary exams,

Crisis intervention, ongoing counseling, and assistance throughout the process, and

Information on their legal rights.

The legislation would also require universities to consult with or partner with local rape crisis centers and other community-based organizations to ensure survivors can access the services they need.

The SUCCESS Act would provide funding for universities and colleges to:

Provide higher education re-entry assistance for student survivors of sexual assault and other forms of violence;

Increase training for faculty and administrators on patient-centered care and recognizing signs of trauma;

Provide patient-centered professional development training for academic advisors and counselors;

Provide academic accommodations for students experiencing trauma, such as patient-centered training for tutors or the establishment of a confidential tutoring program specifically designed to assist student survivors of sexual assault and other violence;

Increase mental health services for student survivors of sexual assault and other violence; and

Create or enhance a fund for survivors of sexual assault and other violence to use for wrap-around services like housing, health care, and mental health treatment.

The S.O.S. Campus Act and the SUCCESS Act are endorsed by the American Psychological Association (APA) and the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network (RAINN).

title: Kelly, Cotton Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Get Phones Out of Schools
text:
Bipartisan bill would give schools resources to keep phones and other personal electronic devices out of classrooms

Read in the Washington Post: Bipartisan bill seeks to ban cellphones in schools nationwide

This week, Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Tom Cotton (R-AR) introduced the bipartisan Utilize No Phones in Learning to Unleash Growth in Grades and Educate Distraction-free (UNPLUGGED) Schools Grant Act of 2026 to help schools reduce classroom distractions by keeping phones and other personal electronic devices out of students’ hands.

Cell phones have become a growing distraction in schools, making it harder for students to focus and learn. More than half of American public-school leaders report that cell phones have negatively affected student academic performance, while kids and teenagers are spending increasing amounts of time on screens outside the classroom as well.

“Phones in schools have been a disaster for learning.” said Kelly. “Getting phones out of classrooms will mean fewer distractions and more time for kids to focus on their teachers and lessons. We’re giving schools the tools to make that happen.”

“Arkansas kids deserve classrooms free of distractions. This bill would support Arkansas public schools that choose to tailor their classroom cellphone guidance to ensure students have the most productive school days possible,” said Cotton.

“No other policy change would confer as big and as rapid a benefit to American schools as freeing students from the constant distractions of the buzzing phones in their pockets,” said social psychologist Jonathan Haidt, author, The Anxious Generation & Cofounder, The TAG Movement. “To support kids’ mental health, educational success, and ability to pay attention – all schools in America should go bell-to-bell phone free. Schools that go phone free almost always report increased student engagement, decreased disciplinary problems, and, most touchingly, teachers say that they hear laughter in the hallways again.”

The UNPLUGGED Schools Grant Act is supported by The Anxious Generation movement, the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), and the National Education Association.

Background:

The UNPLUGGED Schools Grant Act would establish a federal grant program for states that adopt policies prohibiting students from possessing or using personal electronic devices during school hours. The funding would help schools put those policies into practice, including by paying for secure storage options such as lockers, lock boxes, or phone pouches.

To qualify for funding, states would develop their policies in coordination with local school districts and in consultation with educators, parents, and students. The bill makes sure parents have a voice in how these policies are developed and can still reach their kids through school personnel about time-sensitive issues, like changes in pick-up times. It also includes exceptions for students who need access to a device because of a health condition, disability, or special need, while giving states flexibility to provide additional exceptions when appropriate.

Kelly, a product of public schools, has made strengthening public education a priority in the Senate. Earlier this year, Kelly introduced the bipartisan Reading Excellence and Achievement for Development (READ) Act to improve child literacy and the Educators for America Act to strengthen the teacher workforce and expand opportunities for Americans to become educators.

title: Kelly, Gallego Celebrate Chiricahua Officially Becoming Arizona’s Fourth National Park
text:
Bipartisan legislation to make this happen passed the Senate last night, now heads to the president’s desk to be signed into law

Today, Arizona Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego celebrated final passage of the Chiricahua National Park Act, bipartisan legislation to designate Chiricahua National Monument in Cochise County as Chiricahua National Park. Representatives Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ-06) and Greg Stanton (D-AZ-04) introduced the legislation in the House, which passed in March.

The designation will make Chiricahua Arizona’s fourth national park, alongside Grand Canyon, Petrified Forest, and Saguaro National Parks. It will protect Chiricahua’s unique landscape while bringing more visitors and economic opportunities to rural southeastern Arizona.

“Chiricahua is one of Arizona’s most extraordinary places. Designating it as our state’s fourth national park will protect this remarkable landscape for generations and bring new visitors and economic opportunities to southeastern Arizona,” said Sen. Kelly. “I’m grateful to everyone involved for working together to get this across the finish line.”

“The unique landscape of Chiricahua National Park will unite people from around the world while opening economic and tourism opportunities for Arizona. The passing of this bill is a win for huge win for Arizona and honors the culture and preservation of the land,” said Sen. Gallego. “Thank you to the Senate and the House for passing this bill, and I look forward to the president signing this into law.”

“It’s been a long hike, but we’re at the summit. After years of work and persistence, Arizona is one signature away from having its fourth national park,” said Rep. Ciscomani. “Chiricahua has long deserved this designation. As the second bill I ever introduced and in my first 100 days in Congress, I am proud to have worked across the aisle and across both chambers to deliver this victory for our district. This is an Arizona priority and a true team effort. I’m grateful to our local partners, including the City of Willcox, public lands advocates, and everyone who has worked alongside us to make this happen. I’m incredibly proud that we are now one signature away from making Chiricahua Arizona Sixth Congressional District’s second national park during our nation’s 250th birthday.”

“Today’s Senate passage is a huge step forward for the Chiricahua National Monument, bringing it one big step closer to becoming Arizona’s fourth national park,” said Rep. Stanton. “This designation will preserve one of Arizona’s greatest natural treasures and draw visitors from around the world to bolster new economic opportunities across Southern Arizona. I was proud to help advance it through the House, and I’m glad to see it moving closer to the finish line.”

“The balancing rocks at Chiricahua National Monument make it one of the most unique and beautiful spots on Earth, which is exactly why its designation as a National Park makes perfect sense,” said Arizona House Democratic Leader Oscar De Los Santos. “Making it Arizona’s fourth National Park ensures the protection and preservation of its natural beauty, while boosting tourism from around the world and growing our economy.”

“The Senate’s passage of the Chiricahua National Park Act is especially meaningful as HECHO and members of our Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council are in Washington, D.C., advocating for Chiricahua and other conservation priorities important to Western communities. Our Arizona delegation, including Willcox Mayor Greg Hancock, met with Senator Kelly’s staff this week and had the opportunity to meet directly with Senator Kelly Wednesday morning. We are grateful for Senator Kelly’s leadership on this legislation and his work to build the bipartisan support needed to move Chiricahua one step closer to becoming a national park,” said Camilla Simon, Executive Director, HECHO.

“Chiricahua is one of Arizona’s most incredible natural wonders, and we are so excited it will finally be protected as a national park,” said Matthew Nelson, executive director of the Arizona Trail Association. “Its rich cultural history, diverse wildlife, and awe-inspiring rock formations will convince visitors that Arizona is like nowhere else on Earth. Anyone who has ever visited knows that Chiricahua is special, but it’s going to need robust funding to bring this little-known national monument up to national park standards. Especially at a time when National Park Service staff has been cut by 25%, funding for parks is being redirected to Washington, DC, and over 1,500 maintenance and infrastructure projects have just been determined to be ‘low priority’ by the Administration, we are concerned that Chiricahua isn’t going to receive the funding necessary to preserve its natural and cultural resources. Our appreciation goes out to Senator Kelly, Representative Ciscomani, and everyone who supported this legislation. May it lead to great things for Cochise County, Arizona, and our entire National Park System.”

“Chiricahua is a hidden treasure. It’s a place more families deserve to experience. Protecting this landscape ensures future generations can encounter the same awe, memories, and connection to this land that my family has cherished. I am thrilled to see this long-awaited designation become a reality and proud that America’s newest national park will be here in Arizona,” said Orlando Cazarez, Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council member.

“For Willcox, this designation represents an incredible opportunity. Chiricahua is a breathtaking and truly special place, and national park status will help more people across the country discover it. More visitors can mean more customers for our hotels, restaurants, and small businesses and more economic growth for our community,” said Greg Hancock, Mayor of Willcox, Arizona.

“It is an important moment to designate Chiricahua as a National Park. This action will celebrate our spectacular public lands and tell future generations that we value access to the outdoors, protection of our cultural history, wildlife, plants, water, quiet, dark skies, and inspiring natural vistas,” said Emily Burns, Program Director for the Northern Sky Islands, Sky Island Alliance.

“The Chiricahuas are a remarkable example of the public lands that make Arizona so special. We commend Representative Ciscomani and Senators Kelly and Gallego for being champions of our public lands and for working across party lines to protect this incredible landscape for generations to come,” said Michael Cravens, Advocacy and Conservation Director of the Arizona Wildlife Federation.

“Chiricahua is part of the story of Cochise County. Growing up in Douglas, it always felt like one of those treasured places right in our backyard. Our county has deep roots, and generations of families have built their lives here. When one of our communities and one of our treasured landscapes receives this kind of national recognition, it is something the entire county can take pride in. We want people to come experience Chiricahua, but we also want them to discover everything else that Cochise County has to offer. Our communities, our history, our small businesses and our landscapes are all part of what makes this county special. The next step is making sure we are prepared to take advantage of the opportunities that increased visitation will bring,” said Kathleen Gomez, Cochise County Board of Supervisors District 2 Supervisor.

“This has been a long road, and it is good to see it reach this point. Chiricahua is an important part of Cochise County, and people here understand what a special place it is. We also know that bringing more attention to the area can create opportunities for our communities, our businesses and our local economy. I’m proud to see Cochise County play a part in getting this across the finish line. Congressman Ciscomani and Senator Kelly deserve a lot of credit for continuing to work on this over the years. They kept pushing the legislation forward, and they worked with people here in Cochise County to understand why this designation matters. We appreciate their commitment to southeastern Arizona,” said Frank Antenori, Cochise County Board of Supervisors Chairman and District 3 Supervisor.

“Chiricahua protects beautiful forests and wildlife, holds thousands of years of history, and offers trails where visitors can experience vast fields of rock pinnacles and some of the best birdwatching in the world. This is an exciting step for Chiricahua and for the interconnected Sky Islands across southern Arizona, and we look forward to working with Senator Kelly and the Arizona delegation to ensure America’s newest National Park receives the funding and staffing it needs to support its visitors and resources,” said Christina Hazard, Legislative Director, National Parks Conservation Association.

“The National Audubon Society applauds the passage of the Chiricahua National Park Act. Known well by birders, the Chiricahua Mountains are ‘sky islands’ which are part of the connected habitat birds need across the hemisphere,” said Sara Brodnax, director of public and protected lands at the National Audubon Society. “Birders already travel to southeastern Arizona for a chance to see the Elegant Trogon and other birds you just don’t encounter often elsewhere in the US. Birding-related travel and recreation drive an annual $107 billion contribution to the US economy. This National Park recognition will further support the local economy and rural communities in Arizona. We thank U.S. Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ-6) for their work.”

Background:

Established in 1924, Chiricahua National Monument spans more than 12,000 acres of towering rock formations, canyons, and diverse wildlife in Cochise County. The legislation also includes protections for traditional cultural and religious sites and ensures continued access for Tribal members for traditional cultural and customary uses.

Kelly has worked for years to make Chiricahua Arizona’s fourth national park, first introducing legislation to redesignate the monument in 2021 and continuing the effort in subsequent Congresses.

The Chiricahua National Park Act is supported by the City of Willcox, the City of Sierra Vista, the City of Benson, the City of Bisbee, Huachuca City, the Cochise County Board of Supervisors, the National Parks Conservation Association, HECHO, the Sky Island Regional Partnership, and the Arizona Trail Association.

title: Senate Passes Kelly Resolution Honoring Arizona Marine Veteran Nicholas DouglasQuets
text:
Last night, the Senate passed Arizona Senator Mark Kelly’s bipartisan resolution honoring the life and service of Nicholas Douglas Quets, a Tucson-born Marine Corps veteran who was murdered by the Sinaloa Cartel while traveling in Mexico in 2024. The resolution expresses condolences to Quets’ family and loved ones, condemns the violent actions of the Sinaloa Cartel and other transnational criminal organizations, and reaffirms the Senate’s commitment to combating cartel violence.

October 18th will mark two years since Quets’ passing.

Earlier this year, Kelly introduced this resolution along with two other bills—the Nicholas Douglas Quets United States–Mexico Rapid Response for Victims of Crime Act and the Nicholas Douglas Quets Border Travel Safety Act—to address gaps in traveler safety and cross-border coordination highlighted by Quets’ murder.

“Nicholas served his country with honor, and his loss is a tragedy. This resolution is one way to keep fighting for justice for him and for Americans everywhere. It’s good to see this get one step closer to the finish line,” said Kelly. “But we’re not done. I won’t stop pushing to get my other two bills passed so no other family experiences what the Quets family has.”

“We wish to publicly express our deepest gratitude to Senator Kelly and his staff for championing a resolution honoring the life and service of our beloved son, United States Marine Corps veteran Nicholas Douglas Quets. Nick was targeted by Sinaloa Cartel cowards and killed during a failed carjacking on October 18, 2024. In our darkest hours, Senator Kelly was among the first to reach out—not just to offer condolences, but to actively discuss how to protect other families from enduring this devastating grief. He followed through by introducing two crucial pieces of legislation aimed at safeguarding Americans. The Senate’s passage of the resolution is a meaningful step toward ensuring Nicks’ legacy lives on. By securing bipartisan support from Arizona Representatives Crane, Ciscomani, and Stanton, Senator Kelly has demonstrated the exact type of cooperative, country-over-party leadership that Americans crave. Thank you, Senator, for placing your constituents above politics and for honoring the sacred warrior ethos of leaving no man behind,” said Warren Douglas Quets, Jr., Lieutenant Colonel, U.S. Army (Retired) and Patricia M. Quets, parents of USMC Veteran Nicholas DouglasQuets.

Representatives Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ-06), Greg Stanton (D-AZ-04), and Eli Crane (R-AZ-02) are introducing companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

title: King, Curtis Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Increase Affordable Housing Across the United States
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Angus King (I-ME) and John Curtis (R-UT) are introducing bipartisan legislation to increase affordable housing across the United States. The Build American Efficiency Act would streamline the process for home builders to determine and locate domestically sourced materials that comply with the Build America, Buy American Act (BABA). This small legislative step would help homebuilders cut costs and avoid bureaucracy as they work to address the national housing shortage.

To accomplish its goals, the Build American Efficiency Act would encourage the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to share industry-led initiatives to certify products and facilities that comply with BABA requirements. The BABA standards were passed in the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. In addition to King and Curtis, the legislation is cosponsored by Senators Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) and Peter Welch (D-VT).

“Despite our country’s desperate need for additional affordable housing options, American homebuilders face steep costs and bureaucratic red tape,” said Senator King. “The Build American Efficiency Act would empower the Department of Housing and Urban Development to share information to help builders, manufacturers, and housing providers navigate complicated compliance requirements and identify verified American-made products. Eliminating this time-consuming and costly additional step for homebuilders will allow them to build more homes faster. It’s a three-page bill that amounts to a common-sense helping hand.”

“Utah’s impressive growth has unfortunately brought with it the strain of rising housing costs—which has already been made worse by unnecessary federal red tape,” said Senator Curtis. “This bipartisan bill is a commonsense fix that makes it easier for builders to identify American-made materials, cut through bureaucracy, and get more affordable homes built faster.”

More specifically, the Build American Efficiency Act would:

Clarify that the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development has the authority to recognize auditable and verifiable systems that document products that comply with Build America, Buy America domestic content requirements

Allow HUD to treat documentation generated under the Make It American Process Standard, or similar standards that provide an auditable and verifiable certification process, as sufficient evidence for domestic content certification

Help manufacturers, builders, and funding recipients more easily determine which products comply with BABA requirements

Reduce time spent navigating waiver requests, duplicative paperwork, and uncertainty over which products have or have not been approved

Preserve flexibility by ensuring the bill does not mandate the use of any one database or prohibit recipients from using other lawful methods to certify compliance.

In Maine, the Build American Efficiency Act is supported by Avesta Housing and Evernorth.

"The Build American Efficiency Act is an important step forward that will help Avesta, and creators of affordable housing everywhere, move ahead with creating desperately needed new homes for individuals and families. By streamlining and simplifying domestic purchasing provisions through clear, verifiable lists of compliant components, this bill removes a significant challenge to building housing that is now causing serious delays, increasing costs of construction, and putting the viability of needed developments at risk," said Jennifer Hawkins, President and CEO of Avesta Housing. "We deeply appreciate the leadership of Sen. King to bring this bipartisan bill forward to address this critical issue and for his unwavering support of housing for Maine people."

“Evernorth is proud to endorse the Build American Efficiency Act. This commonsense legislation is an important first step toward reducing the compliance burden and delays that are making it harder and more expensive to build the affordable homes our communities need,” said Nancy Owens, President of Evernorth.

Nationwide, the bill is supported by ABB, Alliance for American Manufacturing, Associated General Contractors, Eaton, Bipartisan Policy Center Action, Inclusive Abundance Action, Maine Affordable Housing Coalition, National Association of Electrical Distributors, National Association of Manufacturers, National Association of Realtors, National Association of State Housing Agencies, National Electrical Contractors Association, National Electrical Manufacturers Association, Prysmian, Schneider, Siemens, and Southwire.

Senator King has long been committed to ensuring Maine people across the state can access safe and affordable housing and has worked with his colleagues on creative solutions to combat the housing shortage. He introduced the Farmhouse-to-Workforce Housing Act, which would expand the existing Housing Preservation Grants program so rural homeowners can create more housing on their property — such as an attached apartment unit or a small home nearby — to be available for rent. Additionally, King has sponsored the bipartisan Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act to create nearly two million new affordable homes across the country — including thousands in Maine. He also worked with his Republican colleagues to improve affordability of rural homes and farms through the Access to Credit for our Rural Economy (ACRE) Act of 2023.

title: Klobuchar Recognizes Crystal and Justin Kasmiskie as this Year's Angels in Adoption Minnesota Honorees
text:
The Kasmiskie family and Senator Amy Klobuchar at the Angels in Adoption annual celebration in Washington, D.C.

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Coalition on Adoption, spoke at the annual Angels in Adoption celebration hosted by the Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute and recognized Crystal and Justin Kasmiskie from Shakopee, Minnesota, as this year’s Angels in Adoption Minnesota honorees, alongside their adopted sons.

The Kasmiskies adopted their two-year-old twins in December of 2025 but trouble with their visas delayed their travel. The Kasmiskies were faced with a horrible choice: leave one of their twins behind or stay and risk losing both before the visa ban went into effect. They chose to stay with the kids. Ultimately, with Klobuchar’s help, the family received their approved visas and safely departed Liberia.

“Every child deserves a loving home, a nurturing family, and a bright future,” said Klobuchar. “When Crystal and Justin first encountered a technical visa error, they worried they wouldn't be able to bring their sons home before a visa ban was set to take effect. Our office was able to push their visas through and on January 20th, one day before the ban affected visas from Liberia, they departed for home. Since then, their boys have started preschool, spent lots of time with family, and even went apple picking!”

In her role as co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Coalition on Adoption, Klobuchar has been a leader in the fight to give every child a permanent home. The Congressional Coalition on Adoption is the largest bipartisan, bicameral caucus in Congress. To date, Klobuchar’s office has assisted more than 1,500 Minnesota families with their adoption cases.

In response to the visa ban in January, Klobuchar has advocated for adoption visas to be exempted from the travel ban, as well as guidance for families on how to move forward.

In January 2026, Klobuchar led a letter with her Adoption Caucus Co-Chairs, Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND), Rep. Robert Aderholt (R-AL), and Rep. Danny Davis (D-IL), to the State Department requesting immediate guidance and permanent exemptions for adoption visas.

title: Bipartisan Lummis-Kelly MORE American Fuel Act Passes U.S. Senate
text:
Washington D.C. — The U.S. Senate last night passed the Modernizing Outdated Regulations to Expand American Fuel Act of 2026 (MORE American Fuel Act). The bipartisan bill was introduced by Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) and Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ).

The MORE American Fuel Act modernizes outdated Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) licensing requirements for uranium enrichment facilities and aligns them with the process already used for other nuclear facilities and reactors. The bill lets enrichment companies begin construction at their own risk instead of waiting years for a construction license before breaking ground, while preserving public participation and the NRC’s rigorous safety standards.

“Senator Kelly and I agree on something simple: we can keep the NRC’s high safety standards and still stop making enrichment companies wait years just to break ground,” said Lummis. “Wyoming’s uranium and Wyoming’s workers are ready to help secure this nation’s nuclear fuel supply now. I want to thank Senator Kelly for working with me, and I’m pleased that the Senate has agreed it’s time to cut the red tape holding back American enrichment. I urge the House to act swiftly and send this legislation to President Trump’s desk as soon as possible.”

“Nuclear power is a reliable source of energy. Outdated regulations should not hold back production of the enriched uranium needed to power our nuclear reactors,” said Kelly. “This bill will help us improve our energy security while maintaining strong safety and environmental standards, and I’m glad to see it one step closer to becoming law.”

Background:

Nuclear power provides about 18 percent of total U.S. electricity generation, yet U.S. operators import roughly 80 percent of their enriched uranium. That leaves ratepayers exposed to foreign price swings and to dependence on adversarial suppliers, including Russia.

Senator Lummis cosponsored Senator Barrasso’s Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act, signed into law in 2024. The law banned Russian uranium imports beginning in August 2024, and the ban becomes absolute in 2028 when the Department of Energy’s limited waiver authority expires.

Wyoming is home to the nation’s largest uranium reserves and a skilled energy workforce, positioning the state to lead a domestic nuclear fuel buildout.

The MORE American Fuel Act passed the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee by a vote of 18-1 in September.

###

title: U.S. Senate Passes Lummis, Barrasso, Hageman Legislation to Modernize Wyoming School Trust Fund Investments
text:
Washington D.C. — The U.S. Senate last night passed the Wyoming Education Trust Modernization Act, legislation led by Senators Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) and John Barrasso (R-WY) that would give Wyoming’s permanent school land fund greater investment flexibility and potentially increase annual returns for K-12 education.

“Last night, the U.S. Senate passed a bill that will put Wyoming’s school trust fund to better work for our students,” said Lummis. “The fund holds $5.4 billion but earns only about 5 percent, because it’s still bound by investment rules written in 1890. This bill keeps the principal fully protected while allowing modern investment tools that could raise returns. That means millions of additional dollars for Wyoming classrooms every year, with no new taxes. I thank my Senate colleagues for their support, and I urge the House to act quickly so we can get this to President Trump’s desk.”

“Wyoming has made smart, sustained investments in the future of our students. The Wyoming Education Trust Modernization Act will give our state more flexibility in how it manages and grows our permanent school land fund,” said Barrasso. “Diversifying this vital fund will help generate greater returns for students and teachers across Wyoming. With Senate passage, this bill is one step closer to becoming law.”

Background:

Congress established Wyoming’s State Act of Admission upon statehood in 1890, and it governs how the state manages its federally granted school lands. Proceeds from school trust land sales, exchanges, or disposals must be deposited into a permanent land fund under strict federal regulation. Current law prohibits investing the principal, and only accrued interest can be used to fund K-12 education.

Wyoming’s permanent school trust fund currently holds $5.4 billion and generates roughly 5 percent annually under these restrictions. The legislation passed by the Senate would modernize the fund’s investment policies, potentially raising returns from 5% to 8.3% and significantly boosting annual education funding without touching the principal.

The bill preserves all constitutional protections for education funding and maintains principal protection. Only investment returns can be spent, all existing controls on land disposal and exchanges remain unchanged, and the longtime permanent trust fund structure stays fully intact.

The Wyoming Education Trust Modernization Act was introduced by Senators Lummis and Barrasso, and Representative Harriet Hageman in July 2025.

title: Senator Markey Statement on Bipartisan Permitting Reform Proposal
text:
Washington (October 1, 2026) – Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, issued the following statement following the release of a bipartisan permitting reform proposal.

“I’m never going to ignore that Trump’s attacks on American-made clean energy fueled the energy crisis we’re in now—not to mention his boosterism of power-hungry data centers—all of which have been enabled by Republicans in Congress. The Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill and the Trump administration’s illegal actions to block clean energy projects and rescind grants have killed tens of thousands of megawatts of clean power, stopped creation of union jobs, raised costs for families at home and on the road, and dumped pollution in communities across the country. Data center developers are hijacking our energy grid and using ratepayers to subsidize their profit-making operations, while also polluting air and water in surrounding communities. I’m still reviewing text of this proposal, and I will be looking closely at the details. Building transmission is important. It’s also important not to lock in more fossil fuels and lock out communities.”

title: Senator Marshall Praises Forbes Field Being Named Candidate Location for KC-46A Mission
text:
Topeka – U.S. Senator Roger Marshall, M.D. (R-Kansas), praised the Air National Guard’s decision to identify Forbes Field Air National Guard Base in Topeka as one of four candidate locations for its next KC-46A Pegasus mission.

“This is great news for Kansas and well-deserved recognition of the men and women of the 190th Air Refueling Wing,” said Senator Marshall. “Forbes Field has the infrastructure, the experience and, most importantly, the outstanding Airmen needed to take on this next-generation mission.”

The Secretary of the Air Force approved Forbes Field, along with Bangor Air National Guard Base in Maine, Key Field Air National Guard Base in Mississippi, and Rickenbacker Air National Guard Base in Ohio, as candidate locations for Mission Operations Base 9. The selected location is slated to receive eight KC-46A aircraft.

“Forbes Field is the absolute right place for basing the KC-46A Pegasus,” Brig. Gen. Paul Schneider, the adjutant general, said. “The Kansas Airmen of the 190th Air Refueling Wing continue to set the standard for excellence, as demonstrated by their flawless execution during Operation Epic Fury, their ability to maintain personnel strength above 100% of authorized, and remarkable maintenance record. As the Secretary of the Air Force moves forward with the MOB 9 strategic basing process, the 190th stands ready to recapitalize their legacy KC-135s with the modern capability of eight KC-46A aircraft, ensuring Kansas remains the premier hub for global reach.”

In the coming weeks, the Air National Guard’s Basing and Conversions Division will conduct town halls with the four candidate locations to discuss site-survey criteria and upcoming milestones.

title: Merkley Blasts Senate Republicans for Blocking His Bill to Ban Congressional Stock Trading
text:
Washington, D.C. – Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley released the following statement after Senate Republicans blocked his Ending Trading and Holdings in Congressional Stocks (ETHICS) Act:

“Members of Congress are elected to serve the people, not their portfolios.

“Rather than crack down on Congressional stock trading, Senate Republicans not only blocked my comprehensive legislation to ban this deeply corrupt practice, but they also put up a partisan, fatally flawed bill that doesn’t cover the President and would only prevent members of Congress from buying stocks, allowing them to still sell and hold stocks and perpetuating a clear conflict of interest.

“There should be no question about whether a lawmaker is voting on or writing legislation in the best interest of their constituents or the best interest of their investments. We need a real ban on Congressional stock trading, and I urge my colleagues on the other side of the aisle to work with us on meaningful and decisive action to ban this flagrant conflict of interest once and for all.”

On Wednesday, Merkley took to the Senate Floor in an attempt to pass his ETHICS Act, which would ban members of Congress, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children from buying, selling, and holding stocks and other covered investments. Full text of the ETHICS Act can be found by clicking here.

Merkley has been leading the charge to end Congressional stock trading for over a decade. In 2012, Merkley and former Senator Sherrod Brown (D-OH) led an effort to add an amendment to the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge (STOCK) Act banning trading by members of Congress.

In 2023, Merkley first introduced the ETHICS Act, which later became the first-ever bill banning Congressional stock trading to advance out of a Senate committee. The ETHICS Act was the basis for similar bipartisan legislation that also advanced out of committee in the Republican-controlled Senate this Congress.

title: Wyden, Merkley Introduce Bill to Extend Secure Rural Schools Funding
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, both D-Ore., today were joined by their colleagues Mike Crapo and Jim Risch, both R-Idaho, in introducing legislation that would extend funding for the Secure Rural Schools (SRS) program for three years, and clarify congressional intention for distribution of funding for counties in Oregon with Bureau of Land Management lands.

Funding for the program expired yesterday, September 30, 2026.

“Secure Rural Schools is a lifeline for rural Oregon,” Wyden said. “I’ll be working as hard as I can to get this bill across the finish line, but the well-being of rural America shouldn’t be dependent on Congress getting its act together to renew this funding every few years. It’s past time to get rural communities off the financial rollercoaster and deliver a permanent funding solution.”

“The SRS program provides crucial payments that are a lifeline for rural communities here in Oregon and across America—keeping schools open, maintaining roads, restoring watersheds, and providing funding for police officers and firefighters to keep families safe,” said Merkley. “A three-year extension of the program and these common-sense updates are critical to ensuring the federal government upholds its promise to our communities and that local governments can reliably access these important resources.”

Wyden co-authored the SRS law in 2000, and it has brought nearly $4 billion to Oregon counties since then. Funding for the program lapsed in September 2023 and resumed two years later in September 2025, depriving rural counties across the country of critical funding for schools, law enforcement, and infrastructure projects.

title: Wyden, Merkley Press Officials for Answers on UAS Testing Pauses in Pendleton, McMinnville and Tillamook
text:
Oregon senators: “Our constituents have expressed concerns about how the ongoing pause affects the local economies across the state where UAS testing takes place, and they seek a timely resolution”

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley today asked the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and its designated administrator of unmanned aircraft system (UAS) test sites in Pendleton, McMinnville and Tillamook for an update about the recent suspension of all flight operations at those three Oregon locales.

The Oregon senators said their letter comes after operations at those three UAS test sites were paused on Sept. 11 due to concerns at the University of Alaska Fairbanks UAS test site, which serves as the FAA’s designated administrator to test and develop UAS technology, and to oversee operations for test sites across the West.

Cahill, Director of the Alaska Center for Unmanned Aircraft System Integration. “In Oregon, this pause delays testing and development for aerospace and defense contractors, federal customers, and commercial UAS companies who operate at the Pendleton UAS Range, Northwest UAV in McMinnville, and Tillamook UAS Test Range.”

Wyden and Merkley wrote that the testing pause has created significant uncertainty for Oregon communities, noting for example that the Pendleton UAS range generates roughly $2.4 million annually for the Eastern Oregon Regional Airport – roughly 82 percent of the airport’s total revenue at the airport.

“Our constituents have expressed concerns about how the ongoing pause affects the local economies across the state where UAS testing takes place, and they seek a timely resolution,” the senators wrote. “We appreciate the FAA’s efforts to review safety practices and conduct oversight. We also recognize the timeliness and importance of resuming operations at all test sites that have been impacted by the pause.”

The senators asked for responses to their letter by Oct. 7, given the significant economic uncertainty facing the test sites.

title: VIDEO: In Homeland Security Subcommittee, Senator Moody Questions Witnesses on Potential Threats posed to America’s Children and Seniors From AI
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Ashley Moody discussed the dangers of AI, especially when it comes to protecting children and seniors, yesterday in a Homeland Security Subcommittee.

“As a mom, one of my top concerns is the impact AI is having on our children – especially as the technology is ingrained more and more into daily life. We cannot allow Congress to stall, cross its fingers, and hope that everything pans out for the best, because the dark side of AI is being utilized to scam seniors, facilitate addictive algorithms, and steal the image and likeness of our children. We must continue our work in Congress to ensure it never gets out of control. We must win the AI race against China, but we need to do it in a way that protects America’s most vulnerable from AI’s dangerous potential,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

As Florida’s Attorney General, Senator Moody warned about the dangers of AI and worked to protect Floridians:

Ran the “Summer Scams Series: Tech Traps,” warning Floridians about AI voice-cloning “grandparent” scams, ChatGPT-generated phishing, and AI-assisted sextortion schemes targeting teens.

Publicly highlighted how generative AI made sextortion more believable and scalable.

Launched investigations into Meta and Instagram, as well as took legal action, over the platform’s algorithms and practices that sought to addict children to using the service and then profit off the children’s data.

As U.S. Senator, Moody has introduced and cosponsored bills that directly address AI-generated content and platform design:

NO FAKES Act (Nurture Originals, Foster Art, and Keep Entertainment Safe Act of 2026):

Creates a federal intellectual-property right in an individual’s voice and visual likeness. It makes it unlawful to distribute unauthorized AI digital replicas (deepfakes) and can hold platforms liable if they know the replica is unauthorized. The Senate Judiciary Committee advanced it unanimously in June 2026.

Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA): Requires covered platforms to default to the strongest safety settings for minors, give users and parents the ability to turn off addictive design features and algorithmic recommendations, and provide better parental tools and reporting.

Senator Moody has introduced the SWIPES Act and the STOP Scams Against Seniors Act.

She has also sponsored the James T. Woods Act which passed committee and closes gaps that prosecutors previously faced when threats involved material that is now often AI-generated.

title: Murkowski Advances Three Alaska Energy and Resource Bills Through Committee
text:
Washington, DC—The Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources (ENR) during a business meeting today reported three bills championed by U.S. Senator Lisa Murkowski (R-AK). The measures would strengthen Alaska’s energy security by investing in next-generation geothermal technologies; improving electric grid resilience; and expanding efforts to map critical mineral and other resources. The bills now go to the full Senate for consideration.

Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (Earth MRI): S. 4870 would reauthorize Earth MRI, a U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) program that improves understanding of geologic hazards, critical minerals, geothermal resources, and other subsurface resources across the country. Since its launch in 2019, Earth MRI has accelerated project timelines, reduced exploration risk, and lowered costs by making foundational geologic information publicly available. Current funding for Earth MRI is set to expire at the end of FY26.

The legislation would reauthorize Earth MRI for an additional five years at funding levels similar to those provided under IIJA. The bill would also expand the program to include geologic hydrogen, an emerging domestic energy resource that is attracting growing scientific and commercial interest.

Next-Generation Geothermal Research and Development Act (H.R.8790): S.4406 would establish Research and Development (R&D) Programs at the Department of Energy (DOE). These programs would ensure that existing programs are also available for the testing of these next-generation technologies, enhance the collaboration between DOE and the Department of the Interior (DOI) to locate ideal conditions for next-general geothermal energy production, and expand public-private partnerships by establishing a Next-Generation Geothermal Center of Excellence to advance enhanced geothermal energy technologies, including supercritical geothermal energy production.

Securing Community Upgrades for a Resilient Grid Act (SECURE Grid Act): S. 4166 would empower states to more fully assess risks to their electric grids, from extreme weather to cyber threats and other vulnerabilities.

Each year, states must submit a State Energy Security Plan (SESP) to receive funds from the State Energy Program, which are used to design, develop, and implement renewable energy and energy efficiency programs. The SECURE Grid Act would require future SESPs to account for additional threats and vulnerabilities, including supply chain dynamics, extreme weather, potential physical attacks on the grid, and the impact of growing energy demand.

By assessing these additional factors, states would be better able to recognize and respond to weaknesses in their energy infrastructure. The legislation would also require states to coordinate with suppliers of manufactured components and infrastructure to better understand and prepare for potential disruptions.

title: Murkowski and Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Increase Affordable Housing
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) joined Senators Angus King (I-ME) and John Curtis (R-UT) in introducing bipartisan legislation to increase affordable housing across the United States. The Build American Efficiency Act would streamline the process for home builders to determine and locate domestically sourced materials that comply with the Build America, Buy American Act (BABA). This small legislative step would help homebuilders cut costs and avoid bureaucracy as they work to address the national housing shortage.

To accomplish its goals, the Build American Efficiency Act would encourage the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to share industry-led initiatives to certify products and facilities that comply with BABA requirements. The BABA standards were passed in the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

"I'm committed to using every federal resource available to make building homes in Alaska more streamlined and affordable across the board,” said Senator Murkowski. “This legislation will help identify products that are made in America more easily, cutting through red tape to get more homes built with American-made materials around the country.”

“Despite our country’s desperate need for additional affordable housing options, American homebuilders face steep costs and bureaucratic red tape,” said Senator King. “The Build American Efficiency Act would empower the Department of Housing and Urban Development to share information to help builders, manufacturers, and housing providers navigate complicated compliance requirements and identify verified American-made products. Eliminating this time-consuming and costly additional step for homebuilders will allow them to build more homes faster. It’s a three-page bill that amounts to a common-sense helping hand.”

“Utah’s impressive growth has unfortunately brought with it the strain of rising housing costs—which has already been made worse by unnecessary federal red tape,” said Senator Curtis. “This bipartisan bill is a commonsense fix that makes it easier for builders to identify American-made materials, cut through bureaucracy, and get more affordable homes built faster.”

More specifically, the Build American Efficiency Act would:

Clarify that the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development has the authority to recognize auditable and verifiable systems that document products that comply with Build America, Buy America domestic content requirements

Allow HUD to treat documentation generated under the Make It American Process Standard, or similar standards that provide an auditable and verifiable certification process, as sufficient evidence for domestic content certification

Help manufacturers, builders, and funding recipients more easily determine which products comply with BABA requirements

Reduce time spent navigating waiver requests, duplicative paperwork, and uncertainty over which products have or have not been approved

Preserve flexibility by ensuring the bill does not mandate the use of any one database or prohibit recipients from using other lawful methods to certify compliance.

Nationwide, the bill is supported by ABB, Alliance for American Manufacturing, Associated General Contractors, Eaton, Bipartisan Policy Center Action, Inclusive Abundance Action, Maine Affordable Housing Coalition, National Association of Electrical Distributors, National Association of Manufacturers, National Association of Realtors, National Association of State Housing Agencies, National Electrical Contractors Association, National Electrical Manufacturers Association, Prysmian, Schneider, Siemens, and Southwire.

title: Murphy, Hawley Announce Breakthrough Bipartisan Legislation to Force AI Developers to Prioritize Safety or Face Prison Time
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Senators Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) and Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) announced bipartisan legislation to ensure artificial intelligence (AI) agent operators and developers are held liable for hacking incidents. AI agents are hacking into public websites, networks, and servers. This poses potentially dire consequences to anything connected online—including hospitals, utilities, banks, and other critical infrastructure.

“Hacking is a crime, and when AI agents conduct dangerous cyberattacks, the corporations and executives responsible for those AI agents need to be held accountable,” said Senator Murphy. “Our bipartisan bill forces the heads of big AI companies to develop responsibly or face prison time for the damage done by their products to everyone else.”

“These AI agents are committing cyberattacks. If Big Tech companies are going to design AI agents that wreak havoc, these companies better be on the hook for any damage that is caused," said Senator Hawley. "That’s why I’m introducing legislation to ensure AI agent operators and developers are held liable for hacking incidents. With this liability regime in place, AI companies will have every incentive to keep their products safe.”

The bipartisan AI Agent Accountability Act would:

Hold AI Agent Operators Liable. AI agent operators would be held criminally and civilly liable under the provisions of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA), including for knowing operation of an AI agent that recklessly causes computer hacking damage or loss.

Hold AI Developers Liable. AI agent developers would be held criminally and civilly liable for failure to implement reasonable safeguards against hacking when they knew or had reason to know of the AI agent’s hacking capabilities.

Empower AGs with Power to Enjoin AI Agent Hacking. The Attorney General and state attorneys general are granted power to sue to enjoin AI agent operators and developers when they commit, conspire to commit, or attempt to commit a hacking offense under the CFAA.

Senator Murphy has been a leading voice in the U.S. Senate on the threat unregulated artificial intelligence poses to the cultural and economic health of the United States. In 2025, Murphy was honored in the TIME AI 100 as one of the most influential people shaping the conversation on artificial intelligence. This month, he joined the UN General Assembly to outline the path ahead for Congress to address Americans’ growing concerns around AI, including job loss, competition with China, and humanity losing control over the technology.
