title: Murray, Top Appropriators Introduce Bill to Impose Significant Penalties on Trump Admin for Using Taxpayer Dollars to Air Political Propaganda
text:
Penalties for Propaganda Act cuts OMB’s budget by $20 million each instance taxpayer dollars are used for propaganda

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray, Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and top Senate appropriators introduced the Penalties for Propaganda Act, a bill to impose penalties on the Trump administration for breaking federal law and using taxpayer dollars to air government propaganda.

“Not a cent of Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars should ever be used to run political ads glorifying the president. Clearly, this administration couldn’t care less about what the law says or about wasting Americans’ tax dollars on obscene ads. Congress cannot sit on its hands. If the president is going to defy federal law to run propaganda celebrating himself—and his budget director is going to allow it—there must be consequences,” said Senator Patty Murray. “This fair-minded bill hits White House Budget Director Vought’s operating budget each time this administration willfully violates our laws to spend federal funding on North Korea-style propaganda. It is not too much to expect the White House Budget Office to respect the law and the basic principle that tax dollars should not fund political ads. Democrats and Republicans alike have made clear that tax dollars shouldn’t be funding these ads, and I hope every one of my colleagues who agrees will support this bill and work with me to get it signed into law.”

In recent days, the Trump administration has spent at least $2.9 million in taxpayer funds airing several political ads celebrating Trump, according to AdImpact. Federal law prohibits taxpayer funding of political propaganda, including Section 718 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026, which states that: “No part of any appropriation contained in the act or any other Act shall be used directly or indirectly, including through a private contractor, for publicity or propaganda purposes within the United States not heretofore authorized by Congress.”

The Penalties for Propaganda Act imposes a new penalty for violating the anti-propaganda provision contained in federal law. The bill cuts the budget of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), headed by Director Russ Vought, by $20 million each time any part of the administration violates the law.

In addition to Senator Murray, original cosponsors of the legislation include: Senator Jack Reed, Ranking Member of the Financial Services and General Government Subcommittee; Senator Jeanne Shaheen, Ranking Member of the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Subcommittee; Senator Jeff Merkley, Ranking Member of the Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies Subcommittee; Senator Chris Coons, Ranking Member of the Defense Subcommittee; Senator Tammy Baldwin, Ranking Member of the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies Subcommittee; Senator Chris Van Hollen, Ranking Member of the Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies Subcommittee; Senator Martin Heinrich, Ranking Member of the Legislative Branch Subcommittee; Senator Gary Peters, member of the Committee and Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee; Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, Ranking Member of the Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies Subcommittee.

When the government-funded Trump ads first aired, Vice Chair Murray and Ranking Member Reed wrote to White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles demanding the ads come off the air and reminding the White House of federal law. When the Committee became aware the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is bankrolling the ads, Vice Chair Murray and Senator Chris Murphy, Ranking Member of the Homeland Security Subcommittee, wrote to Secretary Markwayne Mullin to demand DHS stop airing the ads and provide the Committee with all relevant information about the spending and contracts. DHS has so far failed to share this information.

title: PASSED: Murray & Daines Floodplain Bill Passes the Senate, Cutting Red Tape, Simplifying Pathway for Ecosystem Restoration
text:
ICYMI: Murray Floodplain Bill Picks Up Dozens of Key Endorsements, Momentum Grows as Commonsense Bipartisan Legislation Is Introduced in the House

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, released the following statement after Senate passage of her Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act—bipartisan legislation Senator Murray introduced with Senator Steve Daines (R-MT) last year. The Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act is a straightforward, commonsense bill that would create a new pathway for ecosystem restoration projects in floodplains that meet specific low-risk criteria—simplifying the approval process for important restoration work while still upholding flood safety standards.

U.S. Representatives Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D, WA-03), Troy Downing (R, MT-02), Janelle Bynum (D, OR-02), and Bryan Steil (R, WI-01), have introduced identical companion legislation in the House of Representatives. The Senate bill now needs to be passed out of the House before it can be signed into law.

“This is great news for Washington state. We are one step closer to making it easier to get ecosystem restoration projects approved. This is a commonsense, zero-cost fix that will cut red tape and allow critical restoration projects in Washington state to move forward,” said Senator Murray. “Government should be making it easier to protect our environment, not harder. And here in Washington state, ensuring our waterways stay healthy is critical for not just our environment, but for our communities and economy as well. I urge my colleagues to waste no time in passing this legislation.”

“This is huge news for Montana. Critical ecosystem restoration projects across our state have been abandoned due to FEMA’s onerous and costly ‘No Rise’ rule. This commonsense, bipartisan bill will reduce unnecessary burdens on important conservation and restoration work, while continuing to keep our communities safe from flooding, and I’m glad to see it pass the Senate. Next step: the U.S. House!” said Senator Daines.

Background on the Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act:

Under current Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) policy, any proposed development in a regulated floodway, whether it’s a shopping mall or salmon habitat, must prove that it will not increase the base flood elevation (BFE) of the area. This requirement is commonly referred to as the “No Rise” rule. While important for protecting communities from increased flood risks, it has had major unintended consequences on important environmental restoration in Washington state and across the country.

In Washington state, many salmon habitat restoration projects involve placing woody debris in rivers and streams to slow water flows and create sheltered areas where juvenile salmon can develop. These projects, and many others, often fail the “No Rise” rule. Currently, the only way to address these impacts is to first update FEMA’s flood maps to account for the projected BFE impacts. This requires extensive and very expensive hydrologic and hydraulic analyses, often performed by a third-party engineer. FEMA then reviews the analyses, replicates them, and approves them internally before giving the okay to move forward, which can take several years to complete. While this process often makes sense in an urbanized, flood-prone community, it is an unnecessary exercise for restoration in rural areas.

Many communities in Washington state have avoided doing restoration work in regulated floodways—which makes up much of the state—to avoid the associated costs. This bill would create a more efficient process for ecosystem restoration in regulated floodways while addressing the “No Rise” issue, which has been a priority concern for Tribal communities and conservation advocates in Washington and across the country.

The following organizations have endorsed Senator Murray and Daines’ Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act: Smarter Safer Coalition; American Rivers; Association of State Floodplain Managers; National Association of Conservation Districts; The Nature Conservancy; Trout Unlimited; Bonneville Environmental Foundation; City of Kenmore; City of Sammamish; City of Seattle; Seattle Public Utilities; Environmental Policy Innovation Center; Environmental Science Center; Island County; King County Department of Natural Resources and Parks; Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe; Montana Trout Unlimited; National Wildlife Federation; Puget Sound Partnership; Puget Sound Salmon Recovery Council; River Alliance of Wisconsin; Southern Environmental Law Center; Upper Deschutes Watershed Council; Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife; Wild Salmon Center; Wisconsin Council of Trout Unlimited; Wisconsin Land and Water Conservation Association; Wisconsin Wetlands Association; WRIA 8 Salmon Recovery Council (Lake Sammamish, Lake Washington, Cedar River Watersheds); City of Shoreline; Mountains to Sound Greenway Trust; Rock River Coalition; and Clean Wisconsin.

“The Puget Sound Partnership is delighted to see the Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act pass the Senate. This legislation is a tremendous step towards accelerating the pace and scale of restoration in Puget Sound and around the country. For too long, critical salmon habitat restoration projects that had no impact on human infrastructure were obligated to complete the same costly hydraulic and hydrologic analyses as subdivisions and strip malls—a process that caused years of delay and millions of dollars of cost increases. Thanks to Senator Murray’s leadership and persistence, this bill will provide local governments with the flexibility they need to get restoration projects done faster and more cheaply. On to the House!” said Mindy Roberts, Executive Director of the Puget Sound Partnership.

“Healthier floodplains are a win-win for people and nature. They can reduce flood risks, improve water quality and provide important habitat for fish and other wildlife,” said Cameron Adams, Policy Advisor for The Nature Conservancy. “The Nature Conservancy applauds the Senate for passing the Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act, which will give communities the flexibility they want and need to scale up science-backed floodplain restoration. We commend Senators Murray and Daines for their attention to this critical issue and strongly support the full passage of FERA into law.”

“In the face of extreme weather and increasing pressures on our nation’s rivers, we need to maximize investments in natural infrastructure and streamline projects that strengthen community resilience, protect public health, and keep our rivers healthy,” said Eileen Shader, Senior Advisor for American Rivers Action Fund. “The Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act is a smart, common-sense step forward to ensuring the regulatory process is efficient and cost-effective. We commend the bipartisan leadership of Senators Murray and Daines advancing this bill and urge the House to take action to pass the bill before the end of the 119th Congress.”

Senator Murray has been a champion for protecting and strengthening critical salmon and fish populations throughout her time in the Senate. Senator Murray secured a historic $2.85 billion investment in salmon and ecosystem restoration programs—including $400 million for a new community-based restoration program focused on removing fish passage barriers in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law—and in the Inflation Reduction Act, Murray secured hundreds of millions for Washington state priorities including $15 million for the Pacific Coastal Salmon Recovery Fund, $3 million to support facilities at the Olympic Coast National Marine Sanctuary, $27 million for Pacific salmon research, and more.

As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Murray has protected critical funding for salmon recovery projects in the Fiscal Year 2026 government spending bills she negotiated and passed into law, including: $75.75 million for the Pacific Salmon account at the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), a $750,000 increase over FY25 funding levels; $27.5 million for Mitchell Act salmon hatcheries, a $4 million increase, to help raise salmon and steelhead for release in the Columbia River Basin for harvest and conservation purposes; $65 million for the Pacific Coastal Salmon Recovery Fund, which the Trump administration proposed eliminating this program altogether in their budget request; $28 million in NOAA construction funds for critical improvements and upgrades at the Northwest Fisheries Science Center in Seattle; $1 million for the Northwest Straits Initiative; $1.5 million for management, intervention, and mitigation of invasive European Green Crab, and more.

title: Senator Murray Reintroduces Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act to Increase Access to Life-Saving Cancer Screenings
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and former chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, reintroduced the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act, legislation that would increase the availability of preventive, life-saving cancer screenings at safety net health care providers like Planned Parenthood. The bill would create new grant and pilot programs to expand access to preventive services and screenings for breast and gynecological cancers—especially for low-income women and women of color—and train health care providers in providing high-quality cancer screening, early detection, and follow-up care.

Jeanette Acosta was a fierce women’s health advocate, a former congressional staffer, and a White House intern in the Obama administration. In 2017, she lost her battle with cervical cancer at the age of 32.

“I’m proud to reintroduce the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act in honor of Jeanette Acosta, a fierce advocate who fought to make sure every woman could get the health care she needs,” said Senator Murray. “Too many women suffer preventable deaths because they didn’t have access to the cancer screenings that would have detected their condition early on. That is an unacceptable tragedy. We know that early detection saves lives—not to mention health care costs—and investing in preventive services to help more women get treatment before it’s too late is just common sense. I’m not going to stop fighting to pass this crucial piece of legislation in Jeanette’s memory.”

“It is an honor that the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act of 2026 is in our daughter’s name. Over eight years ago cervical cancer took the life of our precious and valiant daughter, Jeanette. At the young age of 32, after one year of battling her cancer and suffering incomparable pain and extensive treatment, Jeanette died from her advanced cancer. Jeanette prayed that women be spared from the agony of cervical cancer, and this bill would help to achieve her hope for many women” said Frank X. Acosta, Ph.D., Jeanette Acosta’s father. “This bill will have a lasting and positive national impact in the fight against cancers that afflict women. During her own fight with cancer, Jeanette reached out and provided support and encouragement to other women coping with cancer. She also emphasized the importance of prevention against the onset of cervical cancer. Jeanette, always a warrior for social justice, wanted to shine a light on the disparities to access to prevention and cancer health services for low-income, Latina, and Black women. This bill would brightly illuminate and help to close the gap between cancer prevention and health services and the countless women who have not and may not be able to access these services. Jeanette would adamantly support this bill.”

“Early detection and preventive care saves lives, and everyone deserves access to these critical health services. Planned Parenthood Federation of America is grateful to Sen. Murray for continuing to honor the legacy of former Planned Parenthood patient and health care advocate Jeanette Acosta, who worked to ensure more people can get the care they need,” said Alexis McGill Johnson, president and CEO, Planned Parenthood Federation of America. “The Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act is an important step to increase access to life-saving breast and gynecological cancer screenings, particularly for Black, Indigenous and Latina women who face longstanding barriers to care. We are proud of the over 500 Planned Parenthood health centers providing these essential health services to patients.”

The bill is co-sponsored by: Senators Alsobrooks (D-MD), Baldwin (D-WI), Blumenthal (D-CT), Booker (D-NJ), Duckworth (D-IL), Gallego (D-AZ), Gillibrand (D-NY), Klobuchar (D-MN), Merkley (D-OR), Rosen (D-NV), Schiff (D-CA), Shaheen (D-NH), Van Hollen (D-MD), Whitehouse (D-RI), and Wyden (D-OR).

The bill is endorsed by: American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology, American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Black Women’s Health Imperative, Human Rights Watch, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, National Asian Pacific American Women’s Forum, National Council of Jewish Women, National Family Planning & Reproductive Health Association, National Latina Institute for Reproductive Justice, National Partnership for Women & Families, National Women’s Law Center Action Fund, Ovarian Cancer Research Alliance, and Planned Parenthood Federation of America.

title: NEWS: U.S. Senate Passes Sen. Ossoff’s Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen Emergency Alerts; Heads to President’s Desk to Become Law
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff’s bipartisan bill to strengthen emergency alerts during natural disasters has passed the Senate.

Last night, the U.S. Senate passed Sens. Ossoff and John Cornyn (R-TX)’s bipartisan Mystic Alerts Act to improve distribution of wireless emergency alerts (WEA). The Senate unanimously passed H.R. 7022, the House version of their bill.

The bill previously passed the U.S. House of Representatives and now heads to the President’s desk to become law.

In August, Sens. Ossoff and Cornyn introduced the bipartisan bill to enable emergency alerts to be delivered via satellite communications technologies when other systems fail during emergencies, including natural disasters such as hurricanes, wildfires, and floods.

The bipartisan bill comes after last year’s devastating flood in Central Texas that killed over 100 people, where it was later reported residents did not receive emergency alerts after cellular infrastructure was damaged.

“When storms, disasters, or threats to public safety threaten our state, crisis management is key. Our bipartisan bill will help upgrade America’s emergency alert systems to keep Georgia families safe and informed,” Sen. Ossoff said.

“More than 130 people were tragically killed in the July 4th floods that ravaged Central Texas last year, many of whom did not receive emergency alerts due to compromised cellular networks that were knocked out by the storm,” said Sen. Cornyn. “This bill will address this technology shortfall and honor the memory of those lost by ensuring Texans and all Americans can receive wireless emergency alerts on their mobile devices via satellite even when disaster strikes, and I look forward to President Trump signing it into law soon.”

Sen. Ossoff continues working to strengthen public safety.

This year, Sen. Ossoff brought Republicans and Democrats together to deliver $175,000 in Federal funding to help upgrade the Spalding County Sheriff Office’s helicopter rescue infrastructure after the County experienced difficulties in emergency response to Hurricanes Helene and Milton, and Sens. Ossoff and Rev. Warnock brought Republicans and Democrats together to help establish a central law enforcement command center in Norcross.

Also, this year, Sen. Ossoff brought Republicans and Democrats together to deliver $1,031,000 in Federal funding to help the Conyers Police Department strengthen emergency response efforts by purchasing new portable radios and a Mobile Command Vehicle.

In 2023, Sen. Ossoff delivered new resources through the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to construct a new hurricane and tornado safe room on Tybee Island, providing a safe area for emergency personnel who must remain on the Island during hurricanes and other disaster situations.

title: Padilla Joins Cortez Masto, Wyden, Durbin in Demanding Trump Administration Abandon Proposed Plan to Strip Tax Credits from 700,000 Taxpayers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Immigration Subcommittee, joined Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), and Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) in demanding the Trump Administration withdraw a proposed rule that would prevent up to 700,000 Deferred Action on Childhood Arrivals (DACA) and Temporary Protected Status (TPS) recipients and other tax-paying immigrants from claiming tax credits they are eligible for.

The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and the Department of the Treasury are proposing a rule change that would prevent hundreds of thousands of taxpayers from claiming the Adoption Tax Credit, the American Opportunity Tax Credit, the Child Tax Credit, and the Earned Income Tax Credit. DACA and TPS recipients have been lawfully filing their taxes and claiming these credits for decades. In their letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and IRS CEO Frank Bisignano, the Senators expressed concern over the proposed rule.

“According to your own estimates, the proposed rule change could affect up to 700,000 taxpayers,” wrote the Senators. “This would include more than 300,000 individuals living in households with a DACA recipient, two-thirds of whom are U.S. citizens and who have, on average, lived in the United States for over 28 years. The practical effect of these new regulations would be to deny tax credits to immigrants who are legally eligible for them and lawfully present in our country, and to create a byzantine and unworkable system for both tax preparers and taxpayers.”

“The Administration has no legal authority to change congressionally enacted tax law via regulation…” the Senators continued. “Since the passage of PRWORA in 1996, no federal agency has interpreted refundable tax credits as federal public benefits restricted to qualified immigrants. If Congress intended for refundable tax credits to be treated as federal public benefits, it has had over 30 years to clarify the statute.”

“The proposed rule is clear regulatory overreach that would have disastrous impacts for lawfully present immigrants and their families who are legally eligible for refundable tax credits,” concluded the Senators.

In addition to Padilla, Cortez Masto, Wyden, and Durbin, the letter was signed by Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), and Patty Murray (D-Wash.)

Last year, during consideration of the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” Padilla filed amendments related to restoring eligibility for the child tax credit to all taxpayers and to removing social security number requirements for various tax credits and benefits discussed in the letter. In July, Padilla and Cortez Masto led their colleagues in filing a bicameral amicus brief urging the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit to uphold a lower court’s order blocking ICE from using — or even viewing — tens of thousands of taxpayers’ addresses found to be illegally obtained from the IRS. Padilla and Durbin also sent a letter to Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin urging them to halt improper $1.8 million fines on law-abiding immigrants. In June, Padilla and Durbin led over 50 colleagues in objecting to the Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA)’s recent decision to weaken legal protections for DACA recipients.

Full letter is available here.

title: Senate Unanimously Passes Bipartisan Padilla, Schiff Bill to Support Over 500 Acres of Tribal Land Management
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — The Senate unanimously passed U.S. Senator Alex Padilla’s (D-Calif.) Pit River Land Transfer Act, a bicameral and bipartisan bill to promote Tribal management of over 500 acres of land in California by transferring federal land to the Pit River Tribe. Padilla introduced the legislation with Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) last year to protect Tribal communities and local environment in surrounding regions.

The Senate passed an amended version of the late Representative Doug LaMalfa’s (R-Calif.-01) companion bill, which now heads back to the House of Representatives for a final vote.

“Senseless conflict and bureaucratic barriers have kept California Tribes from managing their ancestral lands, and it’s past time we take action to help Tribes protect their communities and local environment,” said Senator Padilla. “I am grateful that the Senate unanimously passed this critical bill. We’re another step closer to ensuring the Pit River Tribe can steward the land they have inhabited for countless generations.”

“I am proud to see our legislation to help the Pit River Tribe restore their ancestral homelands and promote Tribal sovereignty pass the Senate,” said Senator Schiff. “This bill will help the Pit River Tribe manage the Four Corners site as their ancestors did.”

The Pit River Tribe consist of 11 autonomous bands traditionally inhabiting the area surrounding the Pit River and its tributaries. They are known for their deep spiritual connection to the land, with a rich cultural heritage centered around fishing, hunting, and seasonal gatherings.

This bill would transfer 557 acres of federal land administered by the United States Forest Service to the Secretary of the Interior to be held in trust for the Pit River Tribe. The Tribe has been actively trying to acquire this land through various governmental processes for over a decade. However, they have experienced a series of delays that have added years to the process.

The proposed land to be transferred is known as the Four Corners Property, located in Shasta County. The Tribe has strong cultural and historical connections to the Four Corners, and they view it as a central landmark of their ancestral lands. In October 1970, members of the Tribe erected a Quonset hut on the Four Corners, staking a peaceful, yet firm claim. That month, over 100 sheriff’s deputies, federal marshals, and forest rangers ordered the occupants to evacuate the property, which eventually resulted in violence and the hospitalization of several Tribal members.

Padilla is a strong advocate for restoring Tribal ownership of ancestral lands. In July, Padilla testified at a Senate Committee on Indian Affairs hearing to advocate for critical water investments for California Tribes. In 2024, the Senate passed Padilla’s Jamul Indian Village Land Transfer Act, which established over 170 acres as trust lands for the benefit of the Jamul Tribe. Under the Biden Administration, a series of Padilla’s bills to restore Tribal stewardship of sacred lands and ensure federal land management laws respected Tribal sovereignty were signed into law. The package included laws to take more than 2,500 acres of land in the San Jacinto Mountains into trust for the Agua Caliente Band of Cahuilla Indians and to place roughly 1,000 acres of federal land located in Humboldt and Siskiyou counties into trust for the Karuk Tribe.

title: Senate Passes Peters and Cornyn Bipartisan Legislation to Protect Commercial Satellites from Cybersecurity Threats
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Bipartisan legislation led by U.S. Senators Gary Peters (D-MI) and John Cornyn (R-TX) to help commercial satellite owners and operators defend against growing cybersecurity threats has passed in the Senate. Commercial satellites support GPS navigation, weather forecasts, agriculture, scientific research, global communications, and more. The senators’ Satellite Cybersecurity Act of 2025 would help secure these critical satellites against attacks by hackers, foreign adversaries, and cybercriminals that could cause serious disruptions to our economic and national security. The legislation now heads to the House for consideration.

“Commercial satellites are essential to our national security, our economy, and the daily lives of Americans, so we must ensure they are not vulnerable to attacks from cybercriminals and foreign adversaries,” said Senator Peters. “I'm glad that this bipartisan, commonsense legislation has passed the Senate. It’s critically important that the U.S. businesses utilizing commercial satellites receive the support and resources needed to safeguard their satellite systems, especially as cybersecurity threats become more advanced.”

“This legislation would ensure commercial satellite networks are secure against cyber threats and bad actors, and I look forward to it passing the House and heading to the President’s desk soon,” said Senator Cornyn.

The rise of small, affordable satellites has led to a sharp increase in the number of commercial satellites in orbit, but this proliferation has created new risks. Many satellites transmit sensitive data without adequate safeguards, leaving them vulnerable to interception and cyberattacks. Recent studies showed that roughly half of surveyed satellite signals were unencrypted despite the sensitive information or private data they carried.

The Satellite Cybersecurity Act of 2025 requires the Department of Commerce, in coordination with other federal agencies, to develop voluntary cybersecurity recommendations tailored to satellites. It directs the Department of Commerce to create a publicly available online clearinghouse so companies can easily access best practices and information to secure their systems. The legislation also requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to examine efforts to secure commercial satellites from cybersecurity threats, identify any duplication of effort, and assess how satellite systems integrate into critical infrastructure sectors.

The legislation is supported by the Satellite Industry Association and the Information Technology Industry Council (ITI).

Peters continues to lead efforts to ensure our nation is equipped to defend against cyberattacks. Peters’ historic, bipartisan provision to require critical infrastructure owners and operators to report if they experience a substantial cyberattack, or if they make a ransomware payment, was signed into law. Peters’ bipartisan bills to enhance cybersecurity assistance to K-12 educational institutions, bolster cybersecurity for state and local governments, strengthen the federal cybersecurity workforce, and help secure federal information technology supply chains have also been signed into law.

title: Ricketts, Colleagues to Blanche: Investigate Communist China’s Criminal Marijuana Organizations
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE) joined fellow Senators Tom Cotton (R-AR), Susan Collins (R-ME), and Ted Budd (R-NC), in sending a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche.The infiltration of Chinese criminal networks into American farmland is a national security threat. These illegal marijuana grow operations serve as gateways to drug and human trafficking. The letter requests an investigation into Communist China’s criminal organizations operating illegal cannabis and intoxicating-hemp enterprises that threaten the health and safety of Nebraskans.

In part, the Senators wrote:

“We write requesting that the Department of Justice (DOJ) investigate the growing role of Chinese transnational criminal organizations in America’s cannabis and intoxicating-hemp markets. Recent reporting and investigations suggest Chinese criminal networks are exploiting vulnerabilities in federal law to operate expansive illicit drug enterprises that threaten our communities and national security.”

Full text of the letter may be found here and below.

Dear Attorney General Blanche:

We write requesting that the Department of Justice (DOJ) investigate the growing role of Chinese transnational criminal organizations in America’s cannabis and intoxicating-hemp markets. Recent reporting and investigations suggest Chinese criminal networks are exploiting vulnerabilities in federal law to operate expansive illicit drug enterprises that threaten our communities and national security.

The Drug Enforcement Administration’s 2025 National Drug Threat Assessment found that Chinese transnational criminal organizations dominate marijuana cultivation and distribution in the United States, especially in states with legal cannabis markets. These organizations purchase and lease American land for illegal grow operations, traffic foreign workers, and use toxic pesticides and fertilizers shipped from China, including chemicals banned in the United States. The scale and complexity of these networks make them difficult to track and raise concerns about what other illicit or synthetic products they may be introducing into the U.S. market.

Last year, seven Chinese nationals were charged with running grow houses, smuggling workers from China, and laundering millions of dollars in proceeds. In April 2026, 29 Chinese nationals were charged in a nationwide black-market marijuana operation centered in Oklahoma. Most recently, local authorities in Siskiyou County, California detailed a sprawling system of industrial-scale illegal grows, many of which are run by Chinese nationals. The growers have been linked to human trafficking, violent crime, and toxic foreign pesticides. But their scale and a “shell game” of property records have complicated efforts to dismantle them.

Congress has recognized the need to address vulnerabilities in this market, including closing gaps in the 2018 Farm Bill that allowed unregulated intoxicating hemp and THC products to proliferate. These reforms are set to take effect on December 11, 2026. Leaving the loophole unaddressed would give these networks additional time to flood American commerce with synthetic products. This would also further entrench their operations on American soil, fund their enterprises with illicit revenue, and expose consumers to unregulated, dangerous synthetic products masquerading as legal hemp.

While this will address harmful products currently in the market, questions remain about who is financing and supporting these organizations operating within the industry. We therefore request that the DOJ fully investigate these criminal networks, including their financing, land usage, chemical imports, and any connections to the Chinese Communist Party.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

title: Sen. Rick Scott Introduces Bills to Protect the U.S. Stock Market from Communist Chinese Military Companies
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, U.S. Senator Rick Scott introduced two bills directing the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to identify and suspend Chinese Communist Party (CCP) military companies from trading on U.S. exchanges.

The bills, known as the Know Your Sanctioned Securities Act and the Protecting U.S. Investors from Chinese Military Companies Act, would publicize Communist China-tied companies and bar these companies from being publicly traded on American exchanges.

Senator Rick Scott said, “Communist China’s military companies want to use U.S. markets and exchanges to fund the CCP’s efforts to attack our way of life using dollars from American investors. We can’t let that happen. Communist China has chosen to be our enemy and it’s time for Congress to act by passing these bills to protect Americans from funding an adversary which wishes to destroy us.”

The Know Your Sanctioned Securities Act:

Directs the SEC to attach a ticker modifier "CMC" (Chinese Military Company) to securities of companies identified by the Department of War as supporting Communist China’s military.

Mandates the SEC establish rules for removal of the modifier if an entity is delisted.

The Protecting U.S. Investors from Chinese Military Companies Act establishes:

Mandatory Trading Suspension: Within 10 days of a U.S. Department of War Section 1260H list revision, the SEC must indefinitely suspend trading of securities for any Chinese military company that remains on the list across two consecutive annual revisions.

OFAC Exception and Congressional Notice: If the Office of Foreign Assets Control of the Department of the Treasury (OFAC) adds a covered company to its Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex (CMIC) Companies List, the SEC must notify relevant congressional committees within 10 days that it won’t take action due to that company’s presence on Treasury’s Non-SDN CMIC list.

SEC Authority Limitations: The SEC is restricted to issuing regulations strictly necessary to implement suspensions and notifications, and is explicitly barred from determining list criteria, expanding trading prohibitions beyond the statute, or regulating unrelated entities and transactions.

Both bills are endorsed by Coalition for a Prosperous America (CPA) and the American Securities Association (ASA).

Jon Toomey, President of CPA, said, "American retirees should never be funding Communist China's military. Senator Scott's bills are critical to ensuring investors know what they own and keeping U.S. savings out of the People’s Liberation Army’s hands. CPA salutes Senator Scott for putting American investors first."

Chris Iacovella, American Securities Association President and CEO, said, "ASA applauds Senator Scott for prioritizing America's economic and national security by holding Communist China accountable. When the Pentagon designates a company as a Chinese military company, that company has no business raising capital from American working families, savers, and retirees. These CCP-controlled firms have traded freely on U.S. exchanges for years despite those designations — that's not a procedural gap, it's a strategic failure that Senator Scott's bills fix."

title: On Ninth Anniversary of 1 October Shooting in Las Vegas, Rosen Honors Victims, Calls for Common-Sense Gun Reform
text:
Watch Senator Rosen’s Full Remarks HERE

WASHINGTON, DC – On the ninth anniversary of the tragic 1 October shooting, the deadliest mass shooting in American history, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) delivered a floor speech honoring the 60 people who lost their lives as a result of the tragedy. Senator Rosen recognized the heroism of Las Vegas’ first responders and urged Congress to take action against gun violence and pass common-sense gun safety laws to prevent more tragedies – including passing her bipartisan bill to ban bump stocks.

Below are Senator Rosen’s full remarks:

I rise today ahead of the ninth anniversary of one of the darkest days Las Vegas has ever seen. The shocking tragedy of October First, 2017, the largest mass shooting in American history.

Like many Las Vegas evenings, tens of thousands of visitors came down to the Las Vegas Strip for a concert, the Route 91 Harvest Music Festival.

In the midst of the music, the dancing, and the fun, a deranged gunman opened fire on the festival, killing innocent concertgoers and leaving so many injured and traumatized.

It took only ten minutes for him to carry out this brutal attack, but the consequences of his actions remain with us for a lifetime.

Fifty-eight innocent lives were taken on the night of October First, and in the years since, we’ve lost two more individuals as a result of this horrific tragedy.

Families were left without their loved ones, parents without children, children without their parents.

We owe an endless debt of gratitude to those brave police officers, firefighters, and paramedics who selflessly ran into the chaos and confusion of the night just to help.

On this dark day, we saw our city come together like never before to support the victims.

In the wake of the shooting, President Trump instituted a ban on bump stocks, which the 1 October gunman used to kill so many in just ten minutes.

Unfortunately, the Supreme Court has since overturned this common-sense ban, and the epidemic of gun violence in this country continues to persist to this very day.

This year alone, the United States has seen more than 350, 350, mass shootings.

We are not powerless in Congress. We can do something about the scourge of gun violence. We can do something.

As we honor the memories of the innocent individuals brutally murdered nine years ago, we also must recommit ourselves to that action to ensure that no other community experiences a tragedy like this again. The cost is forever and is too deep

We must come together and pass the bipartisan bill I helped introduce to ban bump stocks before another community lives through a day like 1 October.

Las Vegas has shown that we can survive the darkest of days by coming together as a community and supporting one another.

This is why we will always be Las Vegas strong.

I am proud of our community. I am proud of our resilience. We will continue to fight against gun violence.

Thank you.

title: Rosen Introduces Resolution to Ban Elected Officials and their Families from Profiting from Federal Stakes in Private Companies
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) introduced a resolution this week stating that the President, Vice President, Cabinet secretaries, Members of Congress, and their families should not profit when the federal government acquires or sells shares in private companies. The resolution calls for banning all federal elected officials and their immediate family members from receiving any compensation or fee from any federal acquisition, sale, or transfer of a stake in a private company. It also calls for prohibiting such individuals from being sold or given any such stake the government has acquired. This comes after multiple documented reports that the federal government has used billions in taxpayer dollars to acquire equity stakes in firms directly tied to the Trump family, as well as other high-ranking Cabinet members and officials. Since January 2025, federal agencies have announced more than 35 transactions to acquire equity in private companies, representing more than $27 billion in taxpayer funds.

“As hardworking Americans are struggling to keep food on the table, pay for gas, and afford health care, Donald Trump, his family, and other senior administration officials have continued to enrich themselves with Americans’ hard-earned money,” said Senator Rosen. “I have introduced this resolution to make it clear that taxpayer-funded investments need to benefit Americans, not just a select few.”

Senator Rosen has continued to fight against the misuse of taxpayer dollars. This year, she introduced a bill to ban Trump and his Cabinet members from using federal funds for self-promoting ads. Senator Rosen’s bipartisan No CORRUPTION Act, which was signed into law, closed a loophole that allowed former members of Congress to continue receiving taxpayer-funded pensions after being convicted of felonies. Last Congress, she also supported the Government Spending Oversight Act to help reduce fraud, waste, and abuse in federal spending.

title: NEWS: Sanders, 19 Senators Push to Nearly Double Emergency Home Heating Assistance After Trump’s War with Iran Spikes Costs for Americans
text:
WASHINGTON, Oct. 1 — As one in five American families are forced to make unacceptable choices between whether to pay their utility bills, heat their homes, purchase their prescription drugs or put food on the table, Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and 19 Democratic senators today urged the Trump administration to drastically increase funding to $7 billion for the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP).

In 2025, LIHEAP helped approximately six million Americans heat their homes over the winter. However, because LIHEAP funding today is lower than it was twenty years ago after adjusting for inflation, four out of every five Americans who are eligible cannot access this crucial assistance.

“As the cost of home heating skyrockets across the country due to the illegal and unconstitutional War in Iran, we urge you to request an emergency appropriation of at least $3 billion for the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program,” Sanders and the senators wrote. “Without immediate action, senior citizens on fixed incomes, working families with kids, and people with disabilities are at serious risk of going cold this winter. In the richest country in the history of the world, we cannot let that happen.”

According to the New York Times, heating oil costs for Americans are up roughly 60% since Israel and the United States started attacking Iran early this year — resulting in families that use heating oil paying an additional $800 and families that use electricity or propane paying an additional $100 this winter.

“Emergency LIHEAP assistance is needed now more than ever. Without this vital funding, states will be forced to turn away families, reduce benefits, or exhaust heating assistance funds well before winter is over,” the senators concluded. “Being able to heat your home in the freezing cold is not a luxury. It is a matter of life and death.”

In addition to Sanders, Sens. Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) also signed the letter.

title: NEWS: Sens. Schiff, Padilla Announce $25 Million to Improve State Route 71 in Pomona, Reduce Traffic Congestion
text:
Pomona, CA — Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) announced $25 million in federal grants from the U.S. Department of Transportation for the State Route 71 Gap Closure Project.

The grant will upgrade the current four-lane expressway in Pomona to an eight-lane freeway, construct auxiliary lanes between Mission Boulevard and Valley Boulevard, reconstruct two bridges over existing railroad facilities, install soundwalls along the corridor, and construct an ADA-compliant pedestrian overcrossing.

“I am proud to help deliver $25 million to expand the 71 Freeway and upgrade the pedestrian overcrossings for the thousands of Californians who take this route each day. It will improve safety and efficiency, reduce traffic congestion at one of our critical roadways in Pomona, and improve pedestrian access – making travel more seamless and keeping pedestrians safe,” said Senator Schiff.

“I’m proud to have helped secure $25 million for highway, bridge, and pedestrian improvements that will ease congestion, shorten commutes, and give residents relief from highway noise, while creating good local jobs. This funding will help get Angelenos home to their families sooner and keep goods moving through Southern California,” said Senator Padilla.

“Metro is pleased to be receiving a $25 million INFRA grant from the U.S. Department of Transportation for the State Route 71 Gap Closure Project,” said Metro CEO Stephanie Wiggins. “We are grateful for the remarkably strong support for this project from U.S. Senator Alex Padilla, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff and members of the LA County Congressional Delegation. This Measure M voter-approved project will significantly reduce congestion and travel times, improve safety and connectivity – all while enhancing the movements of goods and people across our region. I welcome this infusion of federal funding that will help complete this project and express my appreciation to the local, state and federal stakeholders whose collaboration are making this project a reality.”

Background: Senators Schiff and Padilla have consistently secured federal investments to modernize and repair California’s highways and aviation infrastructure.

Most recently, they secured a combined $53.8 million for critical infrastructure investments through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act of 2021, also known as the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.

title: NEWS: Sens. Schiff, Padilla Press Big Tech CEOs on Social Media Platforms’ Efforts to Combat Election Disinformation Amid Trump Admin Election Attacks
text:
“Platforms that condone, support, or advance efforts to disenfranchise U.S. voters will be scrutinized and held accountable, including through oversight and potential legislation”

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both-D-Calif.), both members of the Senate Judiciary Committee, pressed the top executives of the largest social media companies about their plans to combat misinformation and disinformation on their platforms ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

“Today, election mis and disinformation remains a serious danger to American democracy and Americans’ right to vote, even more so because of the Trump Administration’s sustained efforts to diminish the public’s trust in elections across the county, including California. Nowhere is that more clear than in the Administration’s efforts to influence and deter mail-in voting… As a result, Congress must conduct rigorous oversight over dangerous election mis and disinformation propagated via social media, as we consider investigations and legislation to remedy it and prevent it from happening in current and future elections,” the Senators wrote.

In their inquiry, the lawmakers note how the Trump administration’s efforts to sow mistrust in the upcoming elections and advances in artificial intelligence are creating new opportunities for large-scale election mis and disinformation and demonstrate the need for social media companies to do their part to protect election integrity. The lawmakers note that in recent years, the companies have continued to retreat from the responsibility of ensuring that information online is accurate.

“We take our constitutional duty to protect shared democratic principles seriously. Your thorough and prompt responses to these inquiries are required for these efforts, as they will inform our work on legislative solutions to strengthen federal elections and combat large-scale mis and disinformation. Platforms that condone, support, or advance efforts to disenfranchise U.S. voters will be scrutinized and held accountable, including through oversight and potential legislation,” the Senators wrote.

The Senators are requesting answers on the companies’ policies to identify and respond to election mis and disinformation, what actions they will be taking for the 2026 midterm elections, the steps to ensure that the Supreme Court’s mail-in ballot ruling is not subject to mis and disinformation campaigns that undermine the integrity of mail-in voting, and whether they’ve received requests from the Trump admin relating to election security. They’re also asking the companies to ensure to preserve all records and communications on this on an ongoing basis.

The inquiry is being sent to xAI’s CEO Elon Musk, Google’s CEO Sundar Pichai, TikTok’s CEO Adam Presser, Snap, Inc’s CEO Evan Spiegel, YouTube’s CEO Neal Mohan, Meta Platform’s CEO Mark Zuckerberg, and Head of Instagram Adam Mosseri.

The full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Mr. Musk, Mr. Presser, Mr. Mohan, Mr. Mosseri, Mr. Pichai, Mr. Spiegel, and Mr. Zuckerberg:

We are writing to seek information regarding your plans to combat misinformation and disinformation on your social media platforms during the 2026 midterm elections. As you know, the Supreme Court recently rejected mail ballot restrictions proposed by the Trump Administration. This is now the law of the land, and it is your responsibility to ensure that widespread mis and disinformation about our electoral system does not take hold on your platforms.

In 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, we led members of Congress in writing to your companies regarding the spread of mis and disinformation on your platforms leading up to the 2024 elections. Despite the ongoing spread of false and misleading content on social media sites, your companies have for years “retreated from some of [your] past commitments to promote election integrity.”

Today, election mis and disinformation remains a serious danger to American democracy and Americans’ right to vote, even more so because of the Trump Administration’s sustained efforts to diminish the public’s trust in elections across the county, including California. Nowhere is that more clear than in the Administration’s efforts to influence and deter mail-in voting. For example, on September 15, 2026, President Trump reacted angrily to the Supreme Court’s 7-2 decision with a false claim that mail-in voting is “totally corrupt and out of control.” President Trump even criticized his own Supreme Court nominees for supposedly “mak[ing] cheating by Radical Left [Democrats], on Mail-In Ballots, a much easier thing to do.”6 As a result, Congress must conduct rigorous oversight over dangerous election mis and disinformation propagated via social media, as we consider investigations and legislation to remedy it and prevent it from happening in current and future elections.

President Trump’s self-serving partisan attacks are not the only new challenge to election integrity. Advances in artificial intelligence and chatbots are creating new opportunities for large-scale election mis and disinformation by both foreign and domestic actors. To be sure, addressing false information about the process of voting is entirely different than censoring a point of view. For example, using social media to tell citizens that Election Day is on Wednesday or that mail-in ballots are illegal is simply election interference. Meanwhile, your companies have continued to retreat from the responsibility of ensuring that information online is accurate. Under the circumstances, Congress has no choice but to carefully scrutinize how social media platforms respond to large-scale election mis and disinformation, both before and after the 2026 midterm elections, which are already underway.

Congress’s Constitutional power to conduct investigations stands on equal footing with its authority to legislate and appropriate. To that end, please provide by October 15, 2026, a detailed written response regarding your company’s current policies to identify and respond to election mis and disinformation and what actions you will be taking for the 2026 midterm elections, along with written answers to the following questions:

What steps are you taking to ensure that the Supreme Court’s clear ruling that state’s mail-in ballot procedures must not be disturbed for the November 2026 midterm elections is not subject to mis and disinformation campaigns that undermine the integrity of mail-in voting? For example, if a campaign alleges that mail-in voting is not permitted in California for the November 2026 midterm elections, how will you ensure that false statement is addressed?

Has your company received any communications from the Trump Administration related to election security or the United States Postal Service’s procedures for mail-in ballots? If so, what instructions or requests did you receive, and how have you engaged with them?

Do you currently have any plans to change your election integrity policies between now and Election Day 2026 (November 3, 2026)? If so, please describe the changes and the reasoning for any particular change.

How will your company address mis and disinformation made by political actors, verified accounts, or synthetic accounts, and how will they be treated differently, if at all, compared to ordinary users?

What are your companies’ plans for keeping Congress fully informed about mis and disinformation campaigns and potential changes in your companies’ election integrity policies?

These records are needed for the U.S. Senate to exercise its essential oversight and legislative functions. We further request that you preserve all records and communications relating to the topics addressed in this letter, from January 1, 2025, to the present and continue preserving such materials on an ongoing basis. This preservation hold applies to all relevant records within your possession and any person or entity representing or purporting to be acting on your behalf. This includes, but is not limited to, records and communications via email, whether official or personal; mobile devices; encrypted or disappearing messaging applications; social media; calendar entries; meeting notes; and voicemail and text messages. To the extent that you use any auto-delete functions, you should immediately suspend auto-delete functions and notify persons with control over potentially relevant records of similar preservation obligations.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. We take our constitutional duty to protect shared democratic principles seriously. Your thorough and prompt responses to these inquiries are required for these efforts, as they will inform our work on legislative solutions to strengthen federal elections and combat large-scale mis and disinformation. Platforms that condone, support, or advance efforts to disenfranchise U.S. voters will be scrutinized and held accountable, including through oversight and potential legislation. We look forward to your prompt response, including a written confirmation that you are preserving all records related to this congressional inquiry.

title: Schmitt Helps Secure $42 Million for I-70 Improvements
text:
U.S. SENATE— Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt announced that following his push, the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT) has been awarded$42,101,350 through the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight and Highways Projects (INFRA) Grant Program for improvements to Interstate 70 near St. Louis Lambert International Airport. The award will be used to implement corridor & interchange improvements along I-70 from Cypress Road (east of US 67) to the upcoming Natural Bridge interchange (west of I-170). This will include interchange improvements at the I-70/Cypress, I-70/Airflight, and I-70/Natural Bridge intersections

“Interstate 70 is one of the most important transportation arteries in Missouri, connecting families, businesses, freight, and travelers throughout the St. Louis region and beyond. This $42 million helps to complement the broader I-70 widening project, with a targeted investment to make a critical stretch of I-70 safer and more efficient while improving access to Lambert Airport,” said Senator Schmitt. “I was proud to support MoDOT’s application and work with Secretary Duffy and the Department of Transportation to bring these resources home to Missouri. As St. Louis makes major investments in the future of Lambert Airport, we also need the infrastructure surrounding it to be ready for that growth.”

“America’s infrastructure is rated a C. Instead of wasting federal dollars on trains to nowhere, President Trump is investing in desperately-needed infrastructure upgrades that will enhance the way people and projects move,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “Senator Schmitt’s advocacy was critical in delivering the $42 million needed to make corridor and interchange improvements along I-70, which will support traffic around St. Louis Lambert International Airport. This Administration is committed to making our supply chains resilient and our partners in Congress make that possible.”

“Lambert International Airport is a vital transportation hub for St. Louis, the state and the entire region,” said MoDOT Director Ed Hassinger. “This grant allows for much needed improvements to I-70, making access to the airport easier and more efficient. This is another example of how federal, state and local partners can come together to deliver projects for Missourians. We appreciate Senator Schmitt’s commitment to this important project, and we look forward to delivering it for our customers.”

In July, Senator Schmitt wrote Secretary Duffy in support of MoDOT’s INFRA application, noting that the proposed improvements would strengthen the St. Louis region’s connections to national air and roadway commerce while improving traffic flow along the corridor.

title: Sens. Scott, Booker sickle cell awareness resolution passes the Senate with unanimous support
text:
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Senate unanimously passed Senators Tim Scott (R-S.C.) and Cory Booker’s (D-N.J.) resolution designating September 2026 as Sickle Cell Disease Awareness Month.

“Raising awareness about sickle cell anemia means working toward a future where Americans living with the disease can lead healthier lives with fewer limitations. The Senate’s unanimous passage of this resolution reinforces our commitment to making treatment and care more accessible, affordable, and attainable,” said Sen. Scott. “New gene therapies should give us all hope, but we still have significant hurdles to overcome to ensure every American battling SCD has the opportunity to live out their American Dream.”

The resolution was cosponsored by Sens. Katie Britt (R-Ala.), Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.), James Lankford (R-Okla.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), and Todd Young (R-Ind.).

Read the full text of the resolution here.

Background:

Sen. Scott has long worked to improve access to treatment and care for Americans living with sickle cell anemia.

Earlier this year, Sens. Scott and Booker’s Sickle Cell Disease and Other Heritable Blood Disorders Research, Surveillance, Prevention, and Treatment Act of 2025 was signed into law as part of the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026.

Additionally, Sen. Scott introduced the Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Reauthorization Act of 2026, which would reauthorize the National Marrow Donor Program and National Cord Blood Inventory through 2031. These programs help patients with diseases, including sickle cell anemia, access bone marrow and cord blood transplants.

In 2025, Sens. Scott and Booker reintroduced the Sickle Cell Disease Comprehensive Care Act, which would allow state Medicaid programs to provide comprehensive, coordinated care to patients with sickle cell anemia through a health home model.

title: Department of Defense Responds to Slotkin: Assures No Plans to Send Troops to Polls, Hegseth Silence Continues
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last night, U.S. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, received a response to her letter demanding confirmation confirming that the Department of Defense would not send uniform military to polling locations and that the role of election administration and security is the responsibility of the state and local officials, not the Department of Defense.

The response came from Assistant Secretary of Defense Mark Ditlevson, who was able to confirm that “the Department has no plan to deploy active-duty troops or Federalized National Guard to polling sites, nor does it have any plan to interfere with ballots, voting machines, or other election-related materials,” citing compliance with Federal law. Notably, Hegseth has still remained silent on this issue and President Donald Trump continues to float the idea of using federal forces at the polls and invoking the Insurrection Act.

In August, Slotkin was able to get General Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to confirm that the U.S. military has no plans to deploy federal troops or federalized National Guard members to polling places during the November 2026 midterm elections, and no plans to seize ballots, voting machines, or other election-related materials. In his response, Caine noted that “election administration and security remain the fundamental responsibility of state and local officials.”

Watch Slotkin on MS NOW here.

Read the response from Ditlevson here.

Background:

Slotkin, sent letters to General of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Caine and Secretary of Defense Hegseth asking for a written response and commitment to keep the U.S. military out of the midterm elections. In previous letters sent by Slotkin, General Mark Milley, General CQ Brown, Secretary Lloyd Austin, and Secretary Mark Esper, were each able to provide a response and confirm they would follow the law and our constitution—which is clear about military interference in our elections.

Slotkin also sent letters to Attorney General Todd Blanche, Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin, Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation Kash Patel, and Chief of the National Guard General Steven Nordhaus asking for a written response and commitment to keep federal forces and law enforcement agents out of the midterm elections.

Slotkin has yet to receive responses from Attorney General Todd Blanche, Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin, and Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation Kash Patel.

title: U.S. Senator Tina Smith’s Measures to Simplify, Update Tax Filings for Farmers and Consumers Passes Senate
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Tina Smith (D-MN) successfully included two measures to help Minnesotans navigate their taxes in legislation that passed the Senate. Sen. Smith’s first measure would adjust the deadline for farmers to file their taxes to align with when most other Minnesotans would file theirs, while her second would require the IRS to track how often they make taxpayers re-submit the same paperwork due to bureaucratic errors. The measures were included in the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act that passed the Senate unanimously.

“Nobody enjoys filing their taxes, but what makes it even worse is how cumbersome and illogical our tax system is, particular for farmers,” said Sen. Smith. “These measures are simple, common-sense solutions. Farmers should get just as much time to prepare their tax filings as everyone else, and the IRS needs to keep track of how often it makes taxpayers submit the same document over and over again.”

The Farm Tax Filing Deadline amendment will give farmers and fishers until Tax Day, April 15, to file their taxes without penalty. Under current law, farmers and fishers must file and pay estimated taxes by March 1 to avoid penalties. Meanwhile, most other taxpayers have until April 15 to file their taxes without penalty. The current earlier deadline left farmers and fishers scrambling to get all the paperwork done in time while everyone else gets an extra month and a half.

The Reporting on Document Management to Avoid Duplicative Requests to Constituents amendment that requires the IRS to track how many documents the agency asks taxpayers to re-submit, even though there was nothing wrong with the documents previously submitted. This amendment won’t cost the government any extra money and will require the IRS to report how many copies of documents it requests from a single taxpayer. This information will then be presented annually to Congress for the next five years to track the progress or lack-there-of.

The Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act (TAS) passed the Senate unanimously on September 30 and now heads to the House of Representatives.

The TAS Act includes more than 60 bipartisan reforms to improve the taxpayer experience, including recommendations from the National Taxpayer Advocate and Finance Committee members on both sides of the aisle.
